title: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL supports minor versions 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25
summary: Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for PostgreSQL now supports the latest minor versions 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25. We recommend that you upgrade to the latest minor versions to address Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of PostgreSQL, and to benefit from the bug fixes and improvements added by the PostgreSQL community. You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate multiple upgrades in phases, validating on lower-priority environments before upgrading your most critical ones. You can also use Amazon RDS Blue/Green deployments to minimize downtime for minor version upgrades. For more information, see Upgrading RDS for PostgreSQL DB engine . title: AWS Lambda now supports orchestrating MicroVMs with Lambda durable functions
summary: Today, AWS announces a developer preview of a new extension for orchestrating Lambda MicroVMs with Lambda durable functions . The extension adds durable operations for running work on MicroVMs and managing their lifecycle. You can use the new operations to build software factories, security scanners, or orchestrate CI/CD jobs that run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated sandboxes. With Lambda durable functions, you can build resilient, multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing and automatic retries. Lambda MicroVMs are a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume, and state preservation for running user-generated or AI-generated code. With this launch, you can run individual tasks in a MicroVM or launch a MicroVM session, where tasks share the same files and memory. The durable function manages the MicroVM lifecycle and runs each task as a durable operation. It checkpoin

title: Amazon CloudWatch Omni now integrates with PagerDuty
summary: Amazon CloudWatch Omni alerts can now automatically create PagerDuty incidents, so notifications flow directly into your existing incident management workflows. This reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR) by eliminating manual notification steps and ensuring consistent incident workflows. CloudWatch Omni is a fully managed AI-powered observability experience built on open standards that unifies monitoring for AI agents, applications, and infrastructure. PagerDuty is an incident management platform that routes alerts to the right on-call responders and coordinates their response. When an Omni alert fires, Omni creates a PagerDuty incident. In PagerDuty, Omni alerts follow your existing on-call schedules and escalation policies, so critical alerts reach the right responder wherever they are, at any hour. Omni alerts include severity, the affected service, and a link back to the related data in Omni, so responders have the context they need to diagnose the problem. For PagerDuty integrati

Session Manager, a capability of AWS Systems Manager, stores each account's regional session preferences in the SSM-SessionManagerRunShell document. title: Amazon EC2 M8g instances are now available in Israel (Tel Aviv)
summary: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) M8g instances are available in the Israel (Tel Aviv) region. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton4 processors and deliver up to 30% better performance compared to AWS Graviton3-based instances. Amazon EC2 M8g instances are built for general-purpose workloads, such as application servers, microservices, gaming servers, midsize data stores, and caching fleets. M8g instances are up to 40% faster for databases, up to 30% faster for web applications, and up to 45% faster for large Java applications than AWS Graviton3-based M7g instances. These instances are built on the AWS Nitro System , which offloads CPU virtualization, storage, and networking functions to dedicated hardware and software to enhance the performance and security of your workloads. M8g instances offer larger instance sizes with up to 3x more vCPUs and memory than Graviton3-based M7g instances. M8g instances are available for purchase in this region via Savings

title: Amazon EC2 M9gd instances are now available in Asia Pacific (Seoul)
summary: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) M9gd instances are available in the Asia Pacific (Seoul) region. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton5 processors, the fifth generation of custom-designed CPUs, which deliver the best price performance for a broad range of workloads running on Amazon EC2. M9gd instances deliver up to 25% better compute performance than AWS Graviton4-based M8gd instances. They are up to 30% faster for databases, up to 35% faster for web applications, and up to 35% faster for machine learning. These instances are built on the sixth-generation AWS Nitro System and are the first to feature the Nitro Isolation Engine . The Isolation Engine uses formal verification to provide mathematical assurance that customer workloads are isolated from each other and from AWS operators, pioneering a new standard for mathematically proven cloud security. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton5 processors, the fifth generation of custom-designed CPUs, which deliver the best price performance for a broad range of workloads running on Amazon EC2. title: AWS IoT Core quotas and usage are now visible in AWS Service Quotas console
summary: AWS IoT Core now publishes its most used service quotas and your current usage against the quotas in AWS Service Quotas console , improving observability and monitoring of API limits and quotas. This launch enables you to monitor your service quota usage, set alarms before you are throttled, and request quota increases ahead of planned growth. AWS IoT Core is a fully managed service that securely connects IoT devices at scale to the AWS cloud and routes IoT device data to AWS and third-party services. As your device fleet grows, your applications depend on quotas for operations, such as connecting and authenticating devices, publishing and subscribing to messages. Previously, service quotas and usage were not visibile in AWS Service Quotas Console and you had to contact AWS Support to learn about your current utilization before throttling occured. Now you can view quotas and usage for both device messaging (data plane) and resource management (control plane) APIs. You can also use Amaz

title: AWS IoT Core now uses dedicated IPv6 address ranges for the HTTP rule action
summary: AWS IoT Core can now send traffic to HTTPS endpoints within a dedicated, published IPv6 address range. This launch enables you to configure your HTTPS endpoints to accept requests only from AWS IoT Core and block all other traffic, thereby reducing your endpoint's exposure to public internet. AWS IoT Core is a fully managed service that securely connects IoT devices at scale to the AWS cloud and routes IoT device data to AWS and third-party services. AWS IoT Core's HTTP rule action delivers IoT device data to any HTTPS endpoint, such as your application servers, on-premises systems, or partner services. With this launch, you can choose from AWS IoT Core's published IPv6 range, and add the fixed IPv6 range to an Amazon API Gateway resource policy , a security group , or your firewall rules . Your HTTPS endpoints will then accept traffic only from AWS IoT Core, giving you network layer control over who can reach your endpoint. To get started, configure your HTTPS endpoint destination to

title: Amazon Transcribe Turbo: more accurate transcripts and natural turn-taking for voice agents, now in public preview
summary: Amazon Transcribe Turbo, our next-generation speech-to-text model, is now in public preview in US East (Ohio) for batch and streaming. Turbo improves accuracy, supports custom vocabulary, and formats numbers, dates, currency, phone numbers and addresses following each locale's conventions. Streaming: English, Portuguese, French, Italian, German and Spanish supported. Word Error Rate (WER) drops ~14% relative in English and 11% relative in the other languages versus the current production model, and formatting accuracy improves by more than 20 points. Batch: English Turbo is generally available in most AWS Regions. Portuguese, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic are now in preview, with ~16% lower word error rate. The base model needs no API, code, or SDK changes. title: AWS IAM extends trusted identity propagation to IAM federation and IAM Roles Anywhere, and simplifies it in IAM Identity Center
summary: Trusted identity propagation (TIP) carries the identity of a human user or workload with requests to supported AWS Services. Customers can use that identity in IAM policy conditions for access control and to identify the originating human user or workload in AWS CloudTrail. AWS is expanding TIP to AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) federation and IAM Roles Anywhere , while simplifying the existing TIP experience in AWS IAM Identity Center. In addition, IAM outbound identity federation now enables customers to request an AWS-signed JSON Web Token (JWT) that includes identity information from TIP sessions, allowing external services to identify the human user or workload that originated the request. With TIP for IAM federation, customers can map the human or workload identity, along with optional runtime claims such as a risk score or a CI/CD workflow name, from the SAML assertion or OIDC token used for federation to the role session. title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless is now available in the Africa (Cape Town) Region
summary: Starting today, the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless is available in the AWS Africa (Cape Town) Region. Customers can now use a fully managed search, vector and analytics engine that provisions resources in seconds, auto scales instantly to meet changing demand, and scales to zero when idle, so customers only pay for the compute they use. With this launch, customers in the Africa (Cape Town) Region can run agentic AI, search, and observability workloads without provisioning or managing clusters. Compute is fully separated from storage, which lets customers scale compute independently to reduce costs during low-traffic periods while remaining ready for traffic spikes. With scale-to-zero and pay-per-usage pricing, customers can save up to 60% compared to provisioning OpenSearch clusters for peak loads. To learn more, see the OpenSearch Serverless documentation and pricing page . For the full list of AWS Regions where OpenSearch Serverless is available, see the Regional Ser

title: AWS CloudFormation makes resource coverage comprehensive with 206 new types
summary: AWS CloudFormation now supports 206 additional resource types across 88 services, including Amazon SageMaker Hub, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore PolicyEngine, and Amazon EC2 Snapshot. This closes key gaps in CloudFormation coverage and helps customers to standardize on safe and scalable infrastructure management workflows. The launch utilized a new AI-driven internal framework to collapse the costs of onboarding resource types to CloudFormation, setting up CloudFormation for continued coverage expansion. AWS Cloud Control API supports all new resource types that CloudFormation supports. Additionally, Cloud Control API now supports 224 read-only resource types across 99 services, making it easier to find and inspect existing AWS resources. CloudFormation resource coverage is available across all AWS Regions where the underlying service is available. To learn more, visit the AWS resource and property types reference , the Cloud Control API resource list , and the AWS CloudFormation User Guide

title: CVE-2026-135614 - Sensitive data redaction bypass in the troubleshooting tool in Amazon ECS MCP Server
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-200-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 11:00 AM PST Description: Amazon ECS MCP Server is an open-source Model Context Protocol server that lets AI agents and assistants manage and troubleshoot Amazon ECS workloads using the operator's AWS credentials. We identified CVE-2026-135614, an issue in the troubleshooting tool of the Amazon ECS MCP Server (awslabs.ecs-mcp-server) before 0.1.36. With the sensitive data setting at its default, the troubleshooting tool returned container environment variable values and secret references from ECS task definitions without the redaction the setting is intended to apply. This might allow a remote actor who can influence the agent's input, for example through prompt injection, to obtain those values. Impacted versions: < 0.1.36 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.

title: CVE-2026-135414 - Server-side request forgery in snapshot repository registration in Amazon OpenSearch Service
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-201-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 11:15 AM PST Description: Amazon OpenSearch Service is a managed service for deploying, operating, and scaling OpenSearch clusters in the AWS Cloud. We identified CVE-2026-135414, an issue in snapshot repository registration in Amazon OpenSearch Service. A user with snapshot management permissions on a domain could set a repository endpoint that caused the domain's service-operated nodes to send requests to network destinations that the user specified. This issue is addressed in service software R20260720. We recommend that customers update their domains to R20260720 or later. Impacted versions: Amazon OpenSearch Service service software before R20260720 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service new engine now joins logs, traces, and metadata
summary: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports distributed joins, high-cardinality aggregations, and OpenSearch query DSL on the new engine. Observability data often spans logs, traces, service metadata, deployment records, and tenant data. Engineers and their AI agents must connect these datasets to determine what failed, where it failed, and who was affected. With Piped Processing Language (PPL) or SQL, engineers and agents can query multiple petabytes of data to connect an error log to its trace, and enrich telemetry with service ownership or deployment metadata, in one query. High-cardinality aggregations measure incident impact across millions of distinct hosts, users, or tenants. The new engine spreads aggregations and joins across data nodes, so you don't need to copy related data into a single index first. With routing key support, you can keep related documents on the same shard, so lookups and joins on that key stay fast. In addition to PPL and SQL, the new engine now supports OpenSe

title: Amazon Connect Customer dashboards now support grouping historical metrics by time interval
summary: Amazon Connect Customer analytics dashboards now support grouping historical metrics by time interval on trailing widgets, giving contact center managers granular control over how performance data is visualized over time. Trailing widgets now display data grouped by 15-minute, 30-minute, one-hour, daily, and weekly intervals. For example, a workforce manager investigating a spike in average handle time can switch from a daily view to 15-minute intervals to pinpoint the exact period the spike occurred, then zoom out to a weekly view to confirm whether it reflects a broader trend. Time interval grouping on dashboards is available in all AWS regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more, see the Amazon Connect Customer Administrator Guide. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website .

title: Amazon EC2 X8i instances are now available in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region
summary: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) X8i instances are available in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region. These instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors available only on AWS. X8i instances are SAP-certified and deliver the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. They deliver up to 43% higher performance, 1.5x more memory capacity (up to 6TB), and 3.3x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation X2i instances. X8i instances are designed for memory-intensive workloads like SAP HANA, large databases, data analytics, and Electronic Design Automation (EDA). Compared to X2i instances, X8i instances offer up to 50% higher SAPS performance, up to 47% faster PostgreSQL performance, 88% faster Memcached performance, and 46% faster AI inference performance. X8i instances come in 14 sizes, from large to 96xlarge, including two bare metal options. To get started, visit the AWS Management Console

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports managed observability and user management extensions for Slurm clusters
summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports managed cluster extensions for Slurm clusters. You can install, configure, update, and remove managed features through the SageMaker AI console or API. The first two extensions cover observability and user management. Earlier, every observability or user management change for HyperPod Slurm clusters meant editing lifecycle scripts and then replacing or rerunning nodes. Now, HyperPod manages these features for you, and you keep lifecycle scripts and custom AMIs for your organization's own software. For each extension, you declare a configuration. HyperPod validates it and applies it to every node, including nodes you add later. It then reports the extension's status and the health of each node. The observability extension collects node, GPU, Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), Slurm job, and Slurm cluster metrics. It sends them to Amazon CloudWatch or Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, and you can add Amazon Managed Grafana dashboards. The user manag

title: Amazon API Gateway announces API Portal
summary: Today, Amazon API Gateway announces API Portal , a new feature that discovers, governs, and documents the APIs and AI endpoints behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancer, and Amazon CloudFront across your AWS organization. Many organizations can't see which APIs are running, which were never registered, which are no longer maintained, and which lack protection. API Portal builds a continuously updated inventory using AWS-side traffic logs and service configuration records, with nothing to install, no logs to forward, and no traffic to reroute, for a single account or your entire AWS organization. Every discovered API starts as a shadow API until you choose to manage it. API Portal labels each API as public or private and identifies AI endpoints, including MCP servers, A2A servers, and LLM endpoints. For managed APIs, it flags those that stop receiving traffic or lose their owner and evaluates security posture against best practices such as authentication, throttling, and AWS

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports OpenSearch version 3.9
summary: You can now run OpenSearch version 3.9 on Amazon OpenSearch Service. OpenSearch 3.9 helps you reduce vector memory and storage, evaluate search quality with more large language model (LLM) providers, build more responsive AI agents, and control access to shared resources. This release adds a new half-float vector type and a bf16 encoder, which store each vector dimension in 16 bits to reduce the memory and storage your vector indexes need. New 2-bit and 4-bit scalar quantization lets you choose the right balance of compression and recall for each workload. Base64-encoded vector ingestion makes request payloads smaller, which speeds up bulk loading. In addition, radial search now uses a redesigned graph traversal to improve both recall and throughput. In Search Relevance Workbench, LLM-as-a-Judge now works with Amazon Bedrock and other LLM providers through ML Commons connectors. You can also retry failed documents, edit ratings, and reuse earlier judgments to reduce repeated LLM calls.

title: AWS WAF introduces simplified pricing
summary: AWS WAF now offers simplified pricing that follows what you protect instead of how you configure it. Previously, you paid separate charges for each web ACL, rule, rule group subscription, and capacity tier, making every security decision a billing calculation. Now, your bill follows three dimensions: the resources you protect, the traffic AWS WAF inspects, and the level of protection you apply. This makes the cost-benefit trade-off easy to understand, and adding or changing rules no longer changes your rate. This new pricing goes into effect on Feb 1, 2027. The new model makes protection costs predictable before you deploy. Each web ACL now includes up to 2,500 WCU at no extra charge, up from 1,500, and you can add rules such as Bot Control common protections or the Anti-DDoS rule group without additional fees. title: AWS WAF announces automated discovery and protection for LLM, MCP, and A2A endpoints using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
summary: Automated AI endpoint discovery and protection are now generally available, enabling you to discover language model (LLM), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent2Agent (A2A) endpoints behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancers, and Amazon CloudFront across your AWS Organization and protect them using AWS WAF. Discovery is available through the new API Gateway API Portal, which recognizes the AI endpoints among the APIs it discovers automatically from traffic logs and service configuration records, with no agents to deploy or logs to forward. An undocumented, public-facing MCP server appears as a shadow API. For unprotected AI endpoints, customers can enable protection using WAF. Protection is available through the new AWS WAF AI Security managed rule group, which protects your AI endpoints. AWS WAF implements protocol recognition and compliance checks to block malformed MCP and A2A messages. When you enable content inspection, the rule group calls Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

title: Amazon Connect Customer launches the ability to force logout agents directly from the analytics dashboard
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now allows supervisors to force logout agents directly from the real-time analytics dashboard, eliminating the need to manually contact agents to end their sessions. Force logout ends all active agent sessions and records the logout event in the Login/Logout report, so agent timecards stay complete. For example, a supervisor identifies an agent who left their workstation without logging out after a shift, and force logs them out from the dashboard, preventing idle time from accruing on the agent's timecard. Agent force logout is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more about analytics dashboards, see the Amazon Connect Customer Administrator Guide . To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website .

title: Amazon Connect Customer now lets you test AI model version upgrades for automated evaluations
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now enables managers to test new AI model versions for automated evaluations before switching, so evaluation scores remain consistent through model upgrades. When a new version becomes available, managers can test how it would score the same contacts compared to the current version of the model. This lets managers catch scoring differences across models and adjust evaluation criteria before those differences affect agent performance results. Managers also have the flexibility to choose how evaluation forms handle model updates. They can automatically upgrade to the latest model version for ongoing accuracy improvements or stay on a specific version for consistent scoring. This feature is supported in all AWS commercial regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more, visit our documentation and our webpage .

title: Amazon Connect Customer expands automated performance evaluations to 45 new languages
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now uses generative AI to automate evaluations of human and AI agent performance in 45 additional languages, such as Arabic, Dutch, Indonesian, and Polish. Managers define custom evaluation criteria in natural language and receive AI-generated evaluations with justifications in their preferred language. Performance evaluations also support cross-language evaluation and can complete assessments in English, even when the conversation is in another language. This enables multilingual contact centers to use a standardized evaluation framework across languages. This feature is supported in all AWS commercial regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. For information about Amazon Connect pricing, please visit our pricing page . To learn more, visit our documentation and our webpage .

title: Amazon CloudFront is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
summary: Amazon CloudFront is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud. Organizations with strict EU sovereignty requirements can now deliver websites, applications, and APIs with the performance, security, and scale of CloudFront, all within the EU. Until now, customers had to build and run their own delivery and TLS termination infrastructure to keep traffic and data inside the EU. With CloudFront in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud, content delivery, TLS termination, logs, and customer configuration stay within the European Sovereign Cloud boundary. The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is physically and logically separate from other AWS Regions, and only EU-resident personnel operate it. This helps governments, healthcare, financial services and other regulated industries meet data residency and operational sovereignty requirements without trading away performance and scale. Customers use the same CloudFront APIs and console experience they already know making it easy to transfer over e

title: AWS Partner Central expands analytics access with Partner Central Agents and Data Subscriptions
summary: AWS Partners and AWS Marketplace sellers now have two new ways to access their analytics data in AWS Partner Central. Partner Central Agents answer questions in plain language, and Data Subscriptions deliver Partner Central data to an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket every day. Partner Central Agents answer questions about leads, marketing campaigns, opportunities and pipeline, and funding, without navigating dashboards or exporting to spreadsheets. AWS Marketplace sellers can also ask about usage, agreements and renewals, billing, collections, and disbursements. Partners can get the same answers in their own artificial intelligence (AI) assistants and agents through the Partner Central Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Data Subscriptions deliver ready-to-use datasets to an S3 bucket daily, covering leads, marketing campaigns, partner account relationships, opportunities and pipeline, and AWS Marketplace usage, agreements, and renewals. title: AgentCore runtime instances are now generally available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances are now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region. Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances in your own account, while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. With runtime instances, teams in AWS GovCloud (US) can choose GPU-accelerated, memory-optimized, or compute-optimized instance types for their agents and run agent sessions of up to 14 days. Agent instances, storage volumes, and session data stay in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region, which helps public sector organizations and their partners meet data residency and compliance requirements. Runtime instances work alongside the default serverless, microVM-based AgentCore runtime, so you can pick the right compute for each agent without changing how you deploy or invoke it. You are charged for the management of the compute provisioned, in addition to your Amazon EC2 costs. To get started, visit AWS News Blog or AgentCore documentati

title: RDS PostgreSQL now supports PostgreSQL 19.0 in the Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment
summary: Starting today, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 19.0 is available in the Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment , allowing you to evaluate PostgreSQL 19.0 on Amazon RDS PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL 19.0 introduces the REPACK command with a CONCURRENTLY option, which removes table and index bloat with minimal locking. You can now enable parallel autovacuum for faster index vacuuming, and logical replication to synchronize sequence values to the subscriber. Two new extensions, pg_plan_advice and pg_stash_advice, let you guide query planner decisions. Refer to the PostgreSQL community announcement for more details. Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment DB clusters are retained for a maximum period of 60 days and are automatically deleted after the retention period, along with their backups and snapshots. A snapshot created in the Preview Environment cannot be copied to a production environment. You can use the PostgreSQL dump and load functionality to import or export your databases from the Previ

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports NCCL profiling for training jobs
summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL) profiling with the HyperPod NCCL Profiler, giving you visibility into communication performance across the nodes and GPUs in a distributed training job. SageMaker HyperPod helps you scale generative AI model development across hundreds or thousands of AI accelerators. Previously, one throttled GPU or degraded link could slow the whole job without an error, and finding it meant stopping the job to run NCCL tests. Now, the HyperPod NCCL profiler loads as a plugin in your training job and sends per-rank bandwidth and timing to Amazon CloudWatch or Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, with no changes to your training code. For example, if training throughput drops with no errors, the NCCL profiler dashboard on Amazon Managed Grafana flags the node whose GPUs fall behind their peers and shows whether they are throttled, so you find it without stopping the job. title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now detects Kubernetes issues affecting training
summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now detects Kubernetes issues that disrupt training, such as crash-looping device plugins or missing DaemonSets, on clusters orchestrated by Amazon EKS. SageMaker HyperPod is purpose-built infrastructure for AI/ML model development, with built-in fault tolerance and automated cluster recovery. Previously, when a device plugin crash-looped or a taint evicted a job's pods, the job's error rarely named the pod or node, so engineers pieced the cause together from kubectl output and per-rank logs. Now, the new HyperPod Kubernetes Resource Monitoring Agent watches nodes, critical pods such as NVIDIA device plugins, and required DaemonSets that impact HyperPod and Kubeflow training jobs. The agent correlates Kubernetes issues with the training jobs they affect and reports them as Kubernetes events and Amazon CloudWatch logs. For example, if a device plugin keeps crashing on one node mid training run, the agent flags the node as it loses GPUs and, when the job fails,

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now detects and recovers hung training jobs on Slurm clusters
summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports hung job detection for Slurm-orchestrated clusters, which finds training jobs that have stopped making progress and returns them to the job queue. SageMaker HyperPod helps you provision resilient clusters for training and deploying AI/ML models. Previously, a job that hung on an NCCL timeout, a stalled data pipeline, or a deadlock kept its GPUs while Slurm reported it as running, until you noticed that the job is not making progress. Now, if a training run hangs, HyperPod detects it within minutes from the job's output and GPU activity, or from log patterns that you define, such as your training step message or an NCCL error, and writes an event to Amazon CloudWatch. You can also have HyperPod cancel the hung job and let Slurm requeue it, so the job can restart from its last checkpoint instead of holding its GPUs idle. You turn on detection per job with an environment variable that points to a rules file, and it works with any framework, including

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod extends AMI auto-patching to Slurm and inference on EKS
summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now automatically patches AMIs on Slurm clusters and introduces a new AMI patching strategy for Amazon EKS clusters that deploy inference workloads. SageMaker HyperPod is purpose-built infrastructure for training and deploying foundation models at scale. Previously, patching a Slurm cluster meant waiting for training runs to finish, scheduling downtime, and upgrading nodes by hand, which could take days of coordination between infrastructure admins and research scientists. Also, auto-patching on Amazon EKS waited for nodes to go idle, which suited training workloads but left nodes serving inference workloads, which rarely go idle, without critical AMI updates. Now, HyperPod patches both while jobs and models keep running: Auto-patching (Slurm): HyperPod patches each node only when it is idle, so running jobs aren't disrupted. title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod deep health check now validates training correctness
summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod clusters orchestrated by Amazon EKS now support MultiNodeTrainingValidation, a deep health check that validates nodes train correctly before your jobs run. SageMaker HyperPod is purpose-built infrastructure for AI/ML model development, with built-in fault tolerance and automated cluster recovery. Previously, a GPU with a subtle fault could pass hardware stress and connectivity tests and still compute wrong results, and the first sign was often NaN or infinite loss in a production training run. Now, The new MultiNodeTraining Validation check trains a fixed Megatron-LM workload on each instance and then across instances over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), and fails any instance whose training loss is NaN, infinite, or diverging, or whose training doesn't finish in time. For example, you can run the check before a multi-week pre-training run, and with automatic node recovery, HyperPod reboots or replaces any instance that fails, so a faulty GPU doesn't surface day

title: Amazon CloudFront Announces HTTP/2 Support for Connections to Origins
summary: Amazon CloudFront now supports HTTP/2 connections to custom origins and VPC origins. HTTP/2 lets CloudFront send many requests over fewer connections to your origin. This means fewer connections and TLS handshakes for your origin to handle, which improves performance for API and agentic workloads, such as AI agents calling MCP servers or mobile and web apps calling backend APIs. Until now, CloudFront connected to origins only over HTTP/1.1, which handles one request at a time per connection. When traffic spiked, for example when an AI agent made many tool calls at once, CloudFront had to open more origin connections. Each new connection added latency and load. With HTTP/2, those requests share connections, so your origin does less work and responds faster. HTTP/2 is also supported for WebSocket connections that support extended CONNECT. If your origin doesn't support HTTP/2, CloudFront automatically falls back to HTTP/1.1, so you don't need to change anything on your origin. HTTP/2 to

title: AWS Global Accelerator now preserves client IPs for NLBs with TLS listeners
summary: AWS Global Accelerator now preserves the client IP address for traffic sent to Network Load Balancer (NLB) endpoints with TLS listeners. You can terminate TLS at your NLB and still see the original client IP address in your application. This means you can apply security groups, geo-blocking, rate limiting, fraud detection, audit logging, allowlists, and compliance controls based on the real client IP. Previously, you couldn't add an NLB with a TLS listener to an accelerator that had client IP address preservation enabled. You had to choose between terminating TLS at the NLB and seeing the real client IP address. With this launch, you get both. This helps with workloads that need TLS termination at Layer 4, such as non-HTTP TCP protocols, applications that require static or Elastic IP addresses, and high-throughput traffic where a Layer 7 load balancer isn't a fit. To enable this feature, add an NLB with a TLS listener as an endpoint to an accelerator with client IP address preservation

title: Announcing metal size for Amazon EC2 G7 instances
summary: Today, AWS announces the general availability of the metal size for Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) G7 instances, accelerated by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. G7 instances deliver up to 4.6x AI inference performance and up to 2.1x graphics performance compared to G6. Customers can use the metal size of G7 instances to run physical AI simulations, deploy AI agent sandboxes, and accelerate graphics workloads that need direct access to bare metal infrastructure. G7 metal instances enable customers to run specialized workloads that require a custom virtualization stack, hypervisor-level GPU drivers, or licensing-restricted applications. The metal size of G7 instances feature 8 NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with 32 GB of memory per GPU and custom Intel Xeon 6 processors. They support 192 virtual CPUs (vCPUs), 768 GiB of system memory, and 700 Gbps of Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking bandwidth. The new metal size is available in the A

title: Amazon Aurora serverless for MySQL now supports up to 384 ACUs
summary: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports database capacity of up to 384 Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs) for Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition, a 50% increase from the previous maximum of 256 ACUs. Each ACU provides approximately 2 gibibytes (GiB) of memory with corresponding CPU and networking, so a single Aurora serverless database can now scale up to 768 GiB of memory. When the workload completes, Aurora serverless automatically scales down to zero. This makes Aurora serverless especially well-suited for agentic AI applications, which typically have bursts of activity, long idle windows, and unpredictable traffic patterns. Aurora serverless handles all of it automatically, scaling capacity with your agents, so you only pay for what you use. With 384 ACU support, customers can now use Aurora serverless for even more demanding workloads while continuing to scale down to zero when not in use, paying only for the capacity consumed. For new clusters, select a supported Aurora MySQL engine version

title: AWS WAF announces automated discovery and protection for API endpoints
summary: Automated API discovery and protection are now generally available, enabling you to discover every API behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancers, and Amazon CloudFront across your AWS Organization and protect them using AWS WAF. Discovery is available through the new API Gateway API Portal, which identifies the APIs automatically from traffic logs and service configuration records, with no agents to deploy or logs to forward. The API Portal classifies the APIs it finds, identifies zombie and shadow APIs, evaluates each API's security posture, and reports findings, including the ones that are missing WAF protections. For unprotected APIs, customers can enable protection using WAF. Protection is available through the new AWS WAF API Security managed rule group, which protects your APIs against the most exploited API attack categories: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA), where the attackers change record IDs in requests to read other users' data, Broken Authentication an

title: AWS DevOps Agent adds Access Profiles and AWS Organizations
summary: AWS DevOps Agent now gives you more ways to govern and control your AWS DevOps Agent instances. With the new Access Profiles feature you can link IAM IDC users in your Agent Spaces to specific permission sets. For example, you can use Access Profiles to limit the ability to create or update skills and memories to a select set of users. AWS Organizations support allows you to more easily configure your Agent Space's AWS account access permissions by automatically aligning accounts in organizations with your Agent Spaces. For the list of AWS Regions where AWS DevOps Agent is available, see the supported Regions table . See all the latest AWS DevOps Agent features on the release history page.

title: AWS CodeDeploy now supports suspending Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling processes
summary: AWS CodeDeploy can now suspend Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling processes during EC2 in-place deployments to Auto Scaling groups. CodeDeploy is a fully managed service that automates application deployments to Amazon EC2 instances, on-premises servers, AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon ECS services. This launch helps prevent scaling activities from terminating or replacing instances while CodeDeploy is updating them, which can cause a deployment to fail. You can choose to suspend any combination of these processes (Terminate, AZRebalance, InstanceRefresh, and ScheduledActions) on a deployment group, or on a single deployment. CodeDeploy suspends the processes you choose before it deploys and resumes them when the deployment succeeds, fails, or is stopped, so you don't need custom scripts to suspend and resume processes during deployments. A setting on the deployment group applies to every deployment in that group, including deployments that your existing pipelines start. You can configure this f

title: Amazon SageMaker Studio now supports training job submission and model deployment for SageMaker HyperPod clusters
summary: Amazon SageMaker Studio now provides a native developer experience for Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, enabling data scientists to submit distributed training jobs, deploy models, and monitor workloads through a visual interface on HyperPod clusters orchestrated with Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). SageMaker HyperPod is a purpose-built infrastructure for distributed training and fine-tuning of foundation models at scale, designed to reduce infrastructure management overhead. Submitting training jobs and deploying custom models on HyperPod at scale requires familiarity with kubectl and authoring Kubernetes manifests, creating operational burden for data scientists who prefer to work in an interactive development environment. With this launch, data scientists can now submit distributed PyTorch and Ray training jobs and deploy models from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, Amazon S3, or Amazon FSx, through single-page forms with a live YAML preview in SageMaker Studio. Compute configu

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod launches a redesigned console experience for creating Amazon EKS-orchestrated clusters
summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers a redesigned AWS Management Console experience for creating clusters orchestrated by Amazon EKS. A guided workflow helps ML infrastructure administrators and platform teams set up networking, instance groups, storage, permissions, resiliency, observability, lifecycle scripts, and tags. Required settings are kept apart from optional ones. You enter only what is needed to create the cluster and add other capabilities later, when you need them. You can start with smart defaults or choose a workload profile that applies a coordinated set of settings based on how you plan to use the cluster. You can then adjust individual and advanced settings as needed, reducing repetitive setup while retaining control over the configuration. The redesigned experience is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker HyperPod is available. To learn more, check our documentation .

title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports viewing capacity reservations
summary: Amazon SageMaker AI now lets you view SageMaker Capacity Reservations in the SageMaker console, AWS CLI, and AWS SDKs. Previously, customers had no self-service way to see their reserved capacity, including reservation timelines and instance availability, and had to rely on AWS Support to plan their own workloads. Starting today, administrators can review the capacity they hold without leaving SageMaker AI. Administrators can list reservations with their status, instance type, availability zone, instance count, start time, and end time. Customers can view their SageMaker Capacity Reservations under Reserved Capacity section in SageMaker Console. They can open a reservation to see its details, including the ML reservation ARN to use in a SageMaker Inference Endpoint configuration. Additionally, the details page lists the SageMaker AI resources that can use the reservation, such as Amazon SageMaker HyperPod clusters and SageMaker Inference endpoints, and shows the status of each associat

title: Amazon Inspector expands runtime reachability analysis for ECR and EC2 findings
summary: Amazon Inspector has expanded its vulnerability management capabilities with runtime reachability analysis for findings originating from Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances. Previously, Inspector reported every vulnerability found in a resource, including packages that were never used by applications. Security teams had to manually assess which vulnerabilities actually posed risk in their deployed environments. Now, Inspector automatically identifies which vulnerabilities are potentially reachable by analyzing package placement in container images and process activity on EC2 instances. With runtime reachability analysis, you can focus remediation efforts on vulnerabilities that matter most to your security posture. For container images, Inspector determines whether a vulnerable package is within your application's dockerfile paths defined by WORKDIR, ENTRYPOINT, or CMD instructions. For EC2 instances, Inspector identifi

title: Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML now supports search across multiple instance types and AWS Regions
summary: Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML now lets customers search across multiple instance types and AWS Regions in a single search, making it easier to find and reserve the capacity their ML workloads need. With Capacity Blocks for ML, customers can reserve accelerated compute instances such as Amazon EC2 P6-B300, P6-B200, and Trn2 instances, for a future start date and for up to 6 months. Until now, customers looking to buy Capacity Blocks had to run a separate search for every instance type and Region combination. Starting today, customers can use a single search in the AWS Management Console to look for Capacity Blocks across multiple instance types and Regions, making it easier to secure capacity without repeated searches. Customers can also programmatically search for capacity across multiple instance types within a Region with a single API call using DescribeCapacityBlockOfferings. This feature is available for all Instance Capacity Blocks in AWS Regions where EC2 Capacity Blocks for

title: Amazon Connect Customer AI agents now fill in step-by-step guides
summary: AI agents in Amazon Connect Customer can now populate fields of a step-by-step guide for contact center agents during live customer interactions. With step-by-step guides, managers can design forms and other user interfaces for common workflows, such as rebooking a trip or submitting a claim. Now, AI agents can fill in a guide when it first loads and suggest updates during live conversations, saving time and improving data accuracy. When contact center agents speak to customers, they spend valuable time recording the information they need to solve the customer's problem in a step-by-step guide. For example, when a traveler calls an airline to change her flight, the agent might record her booking reference, dates of travel, and seat preferences. Now, Connect Customer's AI agents can automatically suggest and populate information like this, based on the context of the conversation. Human agents can review each suggestion, accept or reject suggestions individually or in bulk, and make any

title: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP adds AWS CloudFormation and Console support for snapshots, clones, and data replication
summary: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP now lets you snapshot, clone, and replicate your data directly from the Amazon FSx Console and AWS CloudFormation. Today’s launch allows you to protect and copy your ONTAP data using the same AWS tools that you use across the rest of your AWS environments, with a few clicks in the AWS console or as part of your infrastructure-as-code workflows. FSx for ONTAP is the first and only storage service that allows you to launch and run fully managed, fully featured ONTAP file systems in the cloud. Previously, you could only set up and manage snapshots, volume clones, and SnapMirror replication via the ONTAP CLI or REST API. Starting today, you can also use the Amazon FSx Console, Amazon FSx API, and AWS CloudFormation, in addition to the ONTAP CLI and REST API, to manage these resources. AWS Console and CloudFormation support for these resources are available in all AWS Regions where FSx for ONTAP is available. To learn more, visit the FSx for NetApp ONTAP user gui

title: You can now copy data server-side between Amazon S3 buckets and Amazon FSx file systems with S3 Access Points
summary: You can now use Amazon S3 Access Points to copy or move data server-side between Amazon S3 general purpose buckets and Amazon FSx file systems within the same AWS Region, making it faster, lower-cost, and easier to move your data between S3 and FSx or across FSx file systems. An S3 Access Point for FSx is an S3 endpoint that allows you to access the data on your Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP and Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file systems via the S3 API and from S3-based services and applications. You can also use S3 Access Points to transfer data to and from your file system without the need to mount it—for example, to copy data into your file system from an S3 bucket owned by a partner or to export job results into another team's bucket. Previously, S3 Access Points for FSx didn't support server-side copies, so transferring your data meant downloading and then uploading each object from a server you run. title: Amazon CloudWatch Query Studio now supports saved queries
summary: Amazon CloudWatch Query Studio now lets you save your PromQL and SQL metrics queries and reuse them. You no longer need to rewrite or search for queries you run often, such as a latency query you check during every incident. You can save a query under a name and use "/" in the name to organize queries into folders. In the Saved tab of the Queries panel, you can search, sort, and preview your saved queries. You can then apply one to replace what's in the studio, append it to your current queries, edit it, or delete it. Saved queries are stored in your account and Region, and you control who can create, view, and delete them by using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions. You can also manage them programmatically with the new PutMetricDataQueryDefinition, GetMetricDataQueryDefinition, ListMetricDataQueryDefinitions, and DeleteMetricDataQueryDefinition APIs. title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock expands language support and country-aware search
summary: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock, the tool that grounds AI agents and applications in cited, current web information, now supports five new languages, plus non-US English, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Bedrock: Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Japanese. Agents serving users in these languages get results that draw on local-language sources. We are also introducing a new optional country field that biases results toward sources from a specific country - just pass an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as “JP” or “DE”. This is useful for agents that serve users in multiple countries, for questions whose answer depends on the user's actual or preferred location (e.g., local regulations, prices or public officials), and for surfacing regional sources. Both the expanded language support and the optional country field are available today in every Region where Web Search is offered: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo

title: AWS Lambda now publishes Event Function state change events to Amazon EventBridge
summary: AWS Lambda now publishes Event Function state change events to Amazon EventBridge . Lambda emits an event each time an Event Function version changes state because of a customer action, such as creating, updating, publishing, or deleting a function. These events help platform and DevOps teams to trigger automation as soon as a function becomes ready to invoke, an update finishes, or an operation fails, without polling the GetFunction API. Customers use Lambda Event Functions to build APIs, event processing workloads, multi-step workflows, and data pipelines. As organizations grow to thousands of functions, platform teams need to know when a function changes state so they can take the next step. For example, a deployment pipeline can run integration tests and then shift alias traffic once a new version becomes active. title: AWS Network Firewall introduces automated Internet firewall in public preview
summary: AWS Network Firewall announces the public preview of automated Internet firewall, a new centralized control that allows you to configure Network Firewall, with native network address translation (NAT) capability, on the internet gateways of all the Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) in your environment. Using automated Internet firewall mode, you can centrally define your Network Firewall security rules and enforce them on all inbound and outbound traffic across the internet gateways of your VPCs. You are not required to make routing or architectural changes to deploy automated Internet firewall. You can deploy it across select VPCs or your entire account, organization or organization unit. AWS Network Firewall is a stateful, managed, network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention service for your VPC. Customers use it to inspect their traffic and secure AWS resources. summary: AWS Network Firewall announces the public preview of automated internet firewall (Preview), a new centralized control that allows you to configure Network Firewall, with native network address translation (NAT) capability, on the internet gateways of all the Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) in your environment. Using automated internet firewall (Preview) mode, you can centrally define your Network Firewall security rules and enforce them on all inbound and outbound traffic across the internet gateways of your VPCs. You are not required to make routing or architectural changes to deploy automated internet firewall (Preview). You can deploy it across select VPCs or your entire account, organization or organization unit. title: AWS Compute Optimizer automation rules now support organizational units
summary: AWS Compute Optimizer automation rules can now target the organizational units (OUs) you manage with AWS Organizations, making it easier for large organizations to scale optimization across their accounts. Previously, management accounts could target up to 50 member accounts per rule. Now, a single rule can cover every account in an OU, including accounts added later. You also have the flexibility to exclude specific child OUs or member accounts as needed. Automation rules help you save cost and improve performance by applying recommended actions on a daily, weekly, or monthly schedule when they match your criteria. These actions include cleaning up unattached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes and upgrading volumes to the latest-generation volume types. For example, from your management account, you can create an automation rule to clean up unattached volumes across your entire organization, while allowing resource owners to tag and exclude volumes they want to keep. title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to additional AWS Regions
summary: Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports additional AWS Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes, and MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate in near real-time. With user data in the standby Region, you can redirect traffic and keep authentication available if there is a disruption in your primary Region. Previously, MRR was available in 16 commercial Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. You can now also use MRR to replicate your user data to Asia Pacific (Hyderabad, Hong Kong, Jakarta, Malaysia, Melbourne, New Zealand, Osaka, Taipei, Thailand), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Milan, Spain, Zurich), Israel (Tel Aviv), Mexico (Central), Africa (Cape Town) Regions, helping y

title: Amazon Neptune Serverless now delivers up to 30% better performance and smarter scaling
summary: Amazon Neptune Serverless now delivers up to 30% better performance at the same price per Neptune Capacity Unit, running on AWS Graviton4 processors. The new Graviton4-based platform also brings an improved scaling algorithm that adjusts Neptune Capacity Units (NCUs) more closely to your workload. This especially helps applications with many concurrent graph queries, such as real-time fraud detection, recommendation engines and generative AI applications that run graph lookups on every request. Neptune Serverless scales database capacity automatically as your application’s demand changes, so you can run graph applications with spiky or unpredictable traffic, such as fraud detection, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications, without provisioning for peak capacity. You pay only for the capacity you use. All newly created Neptune Serverless instances will be using AWS Graviton4 processors. You can create new Neptune Serverless instances using AWS Management Console or the AW

title: Amazon CloudWatch extends the PromQL query window to 30 days
summary: Amazon CloudWatch now supports a 30-day query window for PromQL queries against OpenTelemetry metrics, up from 7 days. You can query a month of data in a single request, chart month-over-month and week-over-week trends on one dashboard, and alarm on a 30-day baseline. Teams typically define service level objectives (SLOs) over a 30-day rolling window, longer than a 7-day query can measure. You can now calculate availability and remaining error budget for a full SLO period in one query, and alarm when a service is on track to exhaust its budget. A month of history also makes capacity forecasts more reliable, because a 7-day baseline skews to a single busy weekend. This feature is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where PromQL queries against OpenTelemetry metrics in Amazon CloudWatch are available. To get started, see Query OpenTelemetry metrics with PromQL in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide .

title: Amazon CloudWatch EKS Container Insights now offers built-in monitoring for open source Kubernetes tools
summary: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces built-in monitoring for open source tools running on your Amazon EKS clusters, including Karpenter, KEDA, vLLM, KServe, SGLang, Ray and Knative Serving. You get dashboards for the tools you already use without running Prometheus or Grafana yourself. Monitoring starts automatically when you enable OTel Container Insights. For your AI inference workloads, you can see queued requests, time to first token, and KV cache usage for each model server. For autoscaling, you can see which scalers are failing and how long your scale loop takes. CloudWatch tags every metric with its pod, workload, and node, so you can trace a slow model server to the node it runs on. These EKS solutions are available in version 8.0.0 and later of the add-on and Helm chart, in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. title: Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on now supports custom OpenTelemetry and Prometheus telemetry
summary: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces support for your own application telemetry in the CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on. The CloudWatch agent you already run now accepts metrics, traces, and logs from your applications, so you don't deploy and operate a separate collector to get them into CloudWatch. Applications instrumented with an OpenTelemetry SDK send to an OTLP endpoint that the agent serves on every node, on by default. Metrics arrive as CloudWatch metrics you query with PromQL, traces go to AWS X-Ray and Transaction Search, and logs go to CloudWatch Logs. For Prometheus metrics, the agent scrapes the targets described by standard ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor objects, with no Prometheus operator to run and no change to your scrape configuration. Each team defines its own targets alongside its application rather than in one central add-on configuration. Label selectors let you choose which monitors CloudWatch scrapes. title: AWS Private CA now supports X.509 IAM condition keys
summary: AWS Private Certificate Authority (AWS Private CA) now supports IAM condition keys that describe the certificate being issued. You can write IAM policies that allow or deny a certificate request based on its subject, subject alternative names (SANs), public key, signature algorithm, validity period, key usage, extended key usage, and basic constraints. You can share one private CA across teams and accounts, and each team can issue only the certificates your policies allow. Previously, IAM policies could control who requests certificates from which CA, and with which certificate template, but not what the certificate contains. To keep each team to its own domain names, customers ran a separate CA for each team or built their own authorization layer in front of AWS Private CA. Now, AWS Private CA evaluates your policies against the certificate as it would be issued, before anything is signed, and denies requests that don't comply. title: Amazon Transcribe announces a synchronous transcription API
summary: Amazon Transcribe now offers a synchronous transcription API, TranscribeAudio . Send a complete audio file in a single request and get the full transcript back in the same response. There is no job to start, no status to poll, no connection to manage. The transcripts are as accurate as Amazon Transcribe batch transcription, so you can add fast, accurate speech-to-text to interactive applications such as voice assistants, agent-assist tools and on-demand "transcribe this clip" features. The synchronous API supports the Amazon Transcribe features you already use, including: Word-level timestamps and smart formatting for numbers, dates, currency and phone numbers Automatic language identification Speaker diarization, and channel identification for up to two channels Custom vocabulary and vocabulary filtering, which you can provide directly in the request with no setup step PII redaction Send audio inline (up to 25 MB) or from Amazon S3 (up to 500 MB), 0.5 seconds to 1 hour long, in WAV, M

title: Amazon DynamoDB vector search now supports new inline filter operators
summary: Amazon DynamoDB vector search inline filters now support range comparisons, value lists, and logical operators in addition to the equality operator, so you can narrow a vector search to exactly the items you want. You can now filter on numeric ranges such as price, rating, or publish date, match an attribute against a list of values, check whether an attribute exists, and combine conditions with OR and NOT. Amazon DynamoDB vector indexes store vector embeddings alongside your operational data, and the SearchVectors API returns the items whose embeddings are most similar to your query vector. The search condition expression in a SearchVectors request now accepts the comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, and BETWEEN on Number attributes, the IN operator, the attribute_exists and attribute_not_exists functions, and the logical operators AND, OR, and NOT. DynamoDB applies the filter during the search, so every result it returns matches. For example, a retail application can return the product

title: Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on now supports telemetry filtering
summary: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces telemetry filtering for the CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, so you can stop paying to ingest telemetry you don't use. You can now set cluster-wide include and exclude lists for namespaces, metric names, and pod and node labels. Exclude the non-production namespaces you don't monitor, drop high-cardinality metrics by name, and keep only the labels you group by rather than every label on every resource. Because ingestion is billed per GB, collecting less lowers what you pay, and you can adjust filters with a single add-on configuration update as your clusters change. Telemetry filtering is available in version 8.0.0 and later of the EKS add-on and Helm chart, in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. summary: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart now offers a model leaderboard in Amazon SageMaker Studio. You can use it to compare foundation models side by side on throughput, latency, and cost, and then deploy or customize the model that fits your workload. Comparing models has usually meant reading model cards one at a time and relying on benchmark scores that different sources published under different conditions. The JumpStart leaderboard puts consistent measurements in one view. AWS evaluates every model on three reasoning benchmarks, BIG-Bench Hard, GPQA Diamond, and MMLU-Pro, using the same evaluation setup for each model. AWS also measures time to first token, throughput, and instance cost on SageMaker for each JumpStart deployment configuration. You can use all of the filters already available for JumpStart models, such as model provider, license, and input and output modality, to narrow the list. You can also choose a use case profile and an optimization goal (balanced, cost, latency, or throu

title: AWS Partner Central Agents now help partners create and manage Partner Central and Marketplace support cases
summary: AWS Partner Central Agents now help AWS Partners create and manage AWS Partner Central and AWS Marketplace support cases in one place. The agents are available 24/7 and draw on Partner Central account details and authoritative, partner-specific knowledge from AWS to resolve most inquiries instantly. If a inquiry needs a support engineer, the agents will gather details and create a case. This reduces the time partners spend looking for help, and gives support teams the context they need to resolve cases faster. Partners can handle a case from start to finish in one chat, with the full record in AWS Support Center. To create a case, partners can start describing their issue to AWS Partner Central Agents or use the prompt "get support." The agents gather additional details necessary to resolve the case, set the category, and draft the description. Partners review and submit the case, and the agents route the case to the right support team. In the same chat, partners can view case communic

title: AWS Lambda now supports a batch size of up to 10,000 messages for Amazon SQS FIFO queues
summary: AWS Lambda now supports a batch size of up to 10,000 messages for Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue event source mappings (ESMs) in provisioned mode , up from 10 messages previously. With larger batches, you can process high-volume, ordered workloads such as financial transactions, order processing, and inventory updates with fewer invocations and higher throughput. Lambda continues to preserve message ordering within each message group. Customers use SQS FIFO queues with Lambda to build event-driven applications that need strict message ordering and deduplication. With provisioned mode for SQS ESMs, you can use throughput controls to set a minimum and maximum number of event pollers to meet strict performance requirements. Previously, provisioned mode customers who needed higher throughput for SQS FIFO queues were limited by the maximum batch size of 10 messages. This required them to scale out invocations or add custom buffering logic, which added operational overhe

title: AWS Lambda now provides cost optimization recommendations for Event Functions
summary: AWS Lambda now provides cost optimization recommendations for Event Functions in AWS Trusted Advisor . These recommendations identify on-demand functions where moving to Lambda Managed Instances (LMI) is estimated to reduce costs, and provide configuration guidance for running on LMI. With these recommendations, you can lower your Lambda costs by focusing your efforts on the functions with the greatest estimated savings. LMI lets you run Lambda functions on Amazon EC2 instances while maintaining the operational simplicity of Lambda. With LMI, you can access specialized compute configurations and drive cost efficiency through EC2 pricing options such as Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, without managing infrastructure. Previously, to determine whether a function was a good fit for LMI, you had to analyze its invocation patterns, estimate LMI costs, and select the right instance type and memory-to-vCPU ratio yourself. This manual process added overhead and delayed savings. With this

title: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases
summary: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases, powered by AWS Glue Data Quality, which profiles and evaluates your tables at catalog scale from a single configuration. You define data quality checks once for a catalog, a database, or a single table, and AWS Glue Data Quality evaluates every table in scope, including tables added later, on the cadence you choose. Quality issues surface as data changes, without per-table setup or manual runs, which helps keep bad data from reaching downstream consumers. You can use built-in profiling options that AWS Glue provides for common baseline statistics or provide your own Data Quality Definition Language (DQDL) ruleset with analyzers, rules, or both to hold every table in a database to the same quality standards. You have the flexibility to run evaluations once when you create the configuration or set up triggers, so evaluations run on a schedule or whenever table metadata changes, including every Apache Ice

title: Amazon S3 Vectors raises the filterable metadata limit to 40 KB per vector
summary: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports up to 40 KB of filterable metadata per vector, up from 2 KB. You can attach and filter on more attributes per vector, such as category, permissions, timestamps, and descriptive tags, so your retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic, and semantic-search applications can narrow results by more of the fields that matter to them. S3 Vectors provides native support to store and query vectors in Amazon S3, delivering purpose-built, cost-optimized vector storage and query at billion-vector scale. With this launch, indexes in new vector buckets support the higher limit by default, with no change to how you write vectors with PutVectors or run filtered queries with QueryVectors. To use the higher limit on an existing index, update it in place to enhanced index mode with the UpdateIndexMode API. The higher filterable metadata limit is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon S3 Vectors is available. To get started, use the AWS CLI, AWS S

title: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler adds 589 new API actions and event bus targets
summary: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler expands its AWS SDK integrations with 589 new API actions across 81 AWS services, and adds templated targets for the enhanced EventBridge Custom event bus. You can now schedule direct invocations of a broader set of AWS services without writing custom integration code. EventBridge Scheduler is a serverless scheduler that allows you to create, run, and manage billions of scheduled events and tasks across more than 270 AWS services, without provisioning or managing the underlying infrastructure. With a new templated target, you can schedule event delivery directly to the Custom event bus using its PutEvents or PutRawEvents API. The templated target also makes it easier to add metadata fields to each event. For example, you can send an event to your bus every night at midnight to start a reconciliation workflow, with no function in between to call the API. The new API actions are available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon EventBridge Scheduler is ava

title: AWS CloudFormation Service-Managed StackSets adds custom execution roles with nested stacks support
summary: AWS CloudFormation StackSets now supports custom execution roles for service-managed stack sets, which enables you to scope the permissions StackSets uses in each target AWS account. StackSets deploys the same infrastructure, such as networking and security settings, across thousands of accounts and Regions in one operation. With a custom execution role, you can also use nested stacks, macros, and transforms in service-managed stack sets, which allows you to deploy the reusable templates you use for individual stacks across your organization. With a custom execution role, you define what StackSets can do in each account. By default, service-managed stack sets use a role in each account that can provision any resource in a template without additional setup, and that default remains available. Now, you can provide a template that defines an IAM role, called the execution role, and StackSets creates it in each account before deploying. For example, a stack set that creates Amazon S3 bucke

title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Webhook Events
summary: Amazon EventBridge now supports Webhook Events for the enhanced Custom event bus, so SaaS applications, AI agents, and custom integrations can send events to a bus over HTTPS. You no longer need to deploy and operate your own API endpoint and compute to receive webhooks and publish them to your bus. The EventBridge Custom event bus is a serverless event broker that enables you to create scalable event-driven applications by routing events between your applications, SaaS integrations, and AWS services. When you create a webhook event source on your bus, EventBridge provides a managed HTTPS URL and verifies each request using an HMAC signature, a static token, or basic authentication. EventBridge then publishes accepted events to the bus, where Subscribers filter and deliver them like any other event. For example, shipment status updates from a logistics partner can reach your order tracking and customer notification Subscribers as soon as the partner sends them. Webhook Events are avail

title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Amazon MSK as a target
summary: Amazon EventBridge now supports Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) as a target for the enhanced Custom event bus, so you can deliver events to Kafka topics without running your own producer. The EventBridge Custom event bus is a serverless event broker that enables you to create scalable event-driven applications by routing events between your applications, SaaS integrations, and AWS services. To deliver events to MSK, you create a Subscriber that specifies the cluster ARN and topic. You can also configure Kafka producer settings such as partition key, acknowledgment level, and record headers. EventBridge supports both public and private, serverless and provisioned clusters. When you create a Subscriber for a private cluster, EventBridge automatically sets up a private connection to the cluster. For example, teams that publish to a shared Custom event bus can now deliver purchase-order events to the MSK topics their payments team already consumes from. Amazon MSK ta

title: Amazon MSK Standard Brokers adds support for Apache Kafka version 4.2
service: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
summary: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) now supports Apache Kafka version 4.2 on Standard brokers. A key highlight of this release is Queues for Kafka, which is now production ready. With Queues, multiple consumers can process messages from the same topic partitions, which improves parallelism and throughput for workloads that need point-to-point message delivery. This release also includes Eligible Leader Replicas (ELR) enhancements that improve leader election correctness and strengthen availability. The new consumer rebalance protocol makes consumer group rebalances smoother and faster. The new Streams Rebalance Protocol extends broker-side coordination to Kafka Streams applications so tasks get assigned more efficiently. For the full list of improvements and bug fixes, see the Apache Kafka 4.2 release notes .
