title: Amazon Connect Customer expands how teams track and act on service level agreements for cases
summary: Amazon Connect Customer enhances service level agreements (SLAs) for cases, so teams can set service goals for more of their work and respond faster when a case falls behind. Admins can set SLAs on case fields beyond status, such as requiring a case’s severity to drop from high to medium within 24 hours. Admins can add an email action to SLA breach rules, so the assigned agent learns right away when a case misses its SLA. Developers can use APIs to adjust a case’s SLA deadline when the team is waiting on information from an outside party, such as a partner. Cases is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .

title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 8.4.12 is now generally available
summary: Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 8.4 supports MySQL 8.4.12. This release includes several security enhancements and bug fixes. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by community MySQL. For more details, refer to the Aurora MySQL 8.4 and MySQL 8.4.12 release notes. You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your clusters in phases, validating on lower-priority environments before upgrading your most critical ones. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon Aurora User Guide

title: Amazon ECS Action Logs now cover tasks, container instances, and capacity providers
summary: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) now extends Action Logs to include tasks, container instances, clusters, and capacity providers, so you can see why your tasks failed or why your clusters didn't scale as desired. Action Logs provide detailed, timestamped records of the actions Amazon ECS performs on your behalf, and until now covered service deployments and managed daemon updates. With the expanded coverage, you can diagnose task failures and scaling issues yourself, and resolve them faster than before, without contacting AWS support. If you use Action Logs already, you receive the new events automatically with no configuration changes. When a task fails to start, Action Logs show the reason. Examples include image pull failures, missing permissions for Amazon EBS volumes, or lack of available IP addresses in the subnet. When a running task stops, you can see the container exit code and the health check that triggered the stop. For cluster infrastructure, Action Logs recor

title: Introducing Amazon EC2 T9g instances based on Graviton5
summary: AWS is announcing the general availability of new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T9g instances, which offer the best price performance among general-purpose EC2 instances. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton5 processors and built on the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards. T9g instances deliver up to 45% better price performance compared to previous generation T4g instances, and offer four sizes: nano, micro, small, and medium. These instances are designed for workloads requiring low to moderate CPU utilization, including data processing, login gateways, small databases, microservices, low-traffic websites, freemium services, staging and development, and short-duration compute tasks such as batch processing, event-driven functions, and CI/CD pipelines. T9g instances deliver up to 2.3x the compute performance, 1.5x higher network bandwidth, and 2.8x higher EBS bandwidth compared to T4g instances. They are built on the sixth-generation AWS Nitro System and feature the Nitro Is

title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 7 additional AWS regions
summary: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 7 additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Canada (Central), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), South America (São Paulo), and US West (N. California). With this launch, you can use Lambda MicroVMs in a total of 21 AWS Regions. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume speeds, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code. The service enables secure, stateful, and responsive code execution for applications including AI coding assistants, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. With today's launch, developers can run Lambda MicroVMs closer to their end-users in 7 additional Regions, helping meet latency and data residency requirements. To get started, create a MicroVM image from your Dockerfile, then launch MicroVMs from that image. Give each user or job their own MicroVM with a dedicated HTTPS URL that suppo

title: Amazon MSK now supports in-place upgrade from Standard brokers to Express brokers
service: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
summary: You can now upgrade existing Amazon MSK Provisioned clusters from Standard brokers to Express brokers in place, with fully managed data migration and no application changes. Express brokers are designed to deliver up to 3x more throughput per broker, scale up to 20x faster, and recover up to 90% faster compared to Standard brokers. With in-place upgrade, you can get the performance and operational benefits of Express brokers in hours, without needing to create a new cluster or having to migrate your data and applications to it. The upgrade keeps cluster endpoints unchanged, eliminating application cutovers, and preserves consumer offsets, so stateful applications such as Apache Flink and Kafka Streams continue without reprocessing or duplicates. Express brokers make Apache Kafka simpler to manage and more cost-effective to run at scale, with pay-as-you-go storage that scales automatically and built-in best practice defaults for higher resilience. Previously, upgrading to Express broker

title: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus supports 2B active metrics and 300K rules per workspace
summary: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus now supports up to 2 billion active metric time series and up to 300,000 total recording and alerting rules per workspace. Customers can also create multiple workspaces per account. This lets them store and analyze billions of Prometheus metrics across their organization. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, Prometheus-compatible monitoring service. It helps you monitor and alert on operational metrics at scale. It scales ingestion and storage automatically for high-cardinality workloads across containerized, serverless and hybrid environments. To get started, create an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace. To raise your active series or rules limits, file a service limit increase request in AWS Support Center or AWS Service Quotas. To learn more, see the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus user guide and the product page.

title: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region
summary: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region, along with Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, Prometheus-compatible monitoring service, that helps you monitor and alert on operational metrics at scale. Customers in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud can now run Prometheus-compatible monitoring workloads in-region, which lowers latency for local workloads and keeps metric data within the region. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector is a fully managed, agentless collector. It discovers and collects Prometheus metrics from your container workloads, so you do not need to run collection agents yourself. The collector sends metrics to an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace, where you query and analyze them. A workspace is a logical space for storing and querying Prometheus metrics. title: AWS Lambda adds support for Node.js 26
summary: AWS Lambda now supports creating serverless applications using Node.js 26, for both Lambda Web Functions and Lambda Event Functions. Developers can use Node.js 26 as both a managed runtime and a base container image (Event Functions only). AWS will automatically apply updates to the managed runtime and base image as they become available. Node.js 26 is the latest long-term support release of Node.js and is expected to be supported for security and bug fixes until April 2029. With this release, you can use the latest Node.js 26 features in Lambda, such as the Temporal API for easier date, time, and time zone handling, and enhancements to the Fetch API. You can use Node.js 26 with Powertools for AWS Lambda (TypeScript) , a developer toolkit to implement serverless best practices and increase developer velocity. You can also use the full range of AWS deployment tools, including the Lambda console, AWS CLI, AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM), AWS CDK, and AWS CloudFormation to depl

title: Amazon S3 increases the read request rate for general purpose buckets by up to 2x
summary: Amazon S3 now supports at least 11,000 GET/HEAD requests per second per partitioned prefix, up from 5,500, for general purpose buckets. A partitioned prefix is a prefix whose keys S3 has assigned to their own partition to serve a high request rate, and S3 creates them automatically as your traffic grows. With this higher request rate, you can retrieve data faster for read-intensive workloads such as machine learning training, data analytics, and data transfers. To maximize throughput, distribute your requests across multiple prefixes so that S3 can scale each one independently. This increase applies automatically to your existing read requests in all AWS Regions, with no changes required to your applications and at no additional charge beyond standard S3 request pricing. To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 user guide and the S3 product page .

title: AWS Lambda adds support for Python 3.15
summary: AWS Lambda now supports creating serverless applications using Python 3.15. Python 3.15 is generally available for Lambda Event Functions and is available in public preview for Lambda Web Functions. This is the first Python runtime for Web Functions, which until now only supported Node.js. With this launch, developers can also build web applications and APIs on Web Functions in Python. Developers can use Python 3.15 as both a managed runtime and a base container image (Event Functions only), and AWS will automatically apply updates to the managed runtime and base image as they become available. Python 3.15 is the latest release of Python. With this release, you can use the latest Python 3.15 features in Lambda, such as explicit lazy imports that can reduce function startup time, the new frozendict and sentinel built-in types, and an improved JIT compiler. You can use Python 3.15 with Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python) , a developer toolkit to implement serverless best practices and inc

title: AWS CloudFormation increases the default stacks per account quota to 300,000
summary: AWS CloudFormation now supports up to 300,000 stacks in each AWS account and Region by default (previously 2,000), which enables you to add stacks as your workloads grow without requesting a quota increase. CloudFormation manages related AWS resources as a stack that you create, update, and delete as one unit. Teams that deploy a separate stack for each customer, environment, or developer can now scale those patterns within a single account. A higher default quota allows you to keep growing workloads in the accounts where they already run. Previously, accounts that needed more than 2,000 stacks in a Region requested a quota increase through Service Quotas. Now, the default quota covers these workloads without a request. For example, a software provider that deploys one stack for each customer can grow from 2,000 to 300,000 customer stacks in one account and Region. Existing stacks work without changes. The higher quota applies to stacks you create in the CloudFormation console or with

title: AgentCore runtime instances now support Amazon EC2 G7 instances
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances now support Amazon EC2 G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. G7 instances give agents that do 3D rendering or model inference another GPU option, alongside families such as G6e and G7e. To use G7, add G7 instance types, from g7.2xlarge to g7.48xlarge, to the allowed instance types of your capacity provider. AgentCore installs the NVIDIA drivers on the instance, so standard container images run GPU workloads without bundling drivers. For example, an agent can render 3D scenes or run a vision model on its own GPU, in sessions of up to 14 days . G7 instances on runtime instances are available in select AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), and Asia Pacific (Syd

title: ​​​Amazon RDS for Db2 now supports renaming databases​
summary: ​​Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Db2 now supports renaming databases in place. You can rename a database on your DB instance by calling the new rdsadmin.rename_database stored procedure. Previously, renaming a database required you to back it up and restore it under a new name. With rename, the database keeps its data in place, so it's faster than backing up and restoring the database.​ ​​Database rename simplifies workflows such as replacing a database with a restored copy. For example, after you restore a copy of a database from a backup, you can rename the original database, and then give its name to the restored copy, without changing your application connection strings. Database rename runs as a background task that you can monitor with rdsadmin.get_task_status.​ ​​Database rename is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for Db2 is offered. To get started, see the Amazon RDS User Guide .​​

title: Amazon RDS for Db2 now supports new Canadian time zones
summary: ​​Amazon RDS for Db2 now supports four new time zones, America/Vancouver, America/Edmonton, America/Inuvik, and America/Winnipeg, that reflect the updated local time rules for British Columbia, Alberta, the Northwest Territories, and Manitoba in Canada. As of November 1, 2026, these provinces and territories observe permanent daylight saving time and no longer set their clocks back by an hour.​ ​Data stored in UTC is unaffected, but values based on the instance's local time, such as CURRENT TIMESTAMP, CURRENT DATE, default timestamp columns, scheduled jobs, and business-day batch logic, can be affected. With these new time zones, you can keep local time values accurate for workloads operating in these regions. ​​You can select the new time zones when you create a new RDS for Db2 instance. To change the time zone of an existing instance, contact AWS Support, as modifying the time zone of an existing instance is not supported through the AWS CLI, API, or SDK. If your instances serve work

title: Amazon RDS for Db2 now supports object-level audit policies
summary: Amazon RDS for Db2 now supports object-level audit policies, giving you fine-grained control over which database objects are audited. You can create custom audit policies and attach them to specific tables, users, groups, roles, and authorities in your RDS for Db2 databases. With object-level audit policies, you can focus on auditing the objects that matter most — for example, a single table that contains sensitive data or a specific user — without generating audit records for your entire database. Object-level audit policies complement the existing database-level audit logging in Amazon RDS for Db2. You can use both at the same time, and they operate independently. Amazon RDS provides stored procedures to create, modify, attach, detach, and drop object-level audit policies. Audit records are uploaded to the same Amazon S3 bucket that you configured for Db2 audit logging. Object-level audit policies for Amazon RDS for Db2 are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for Db2 is ava

title: Amazon Route 53 now supports Availability Zone (AZ) affinity routing
summary: Amazon Route 53 now supports Availability Zone (AZ) affinity routing, which routes DNS queries from your VPCs to resources in the same AZ as the client that sends the query. This helps you keep traffic within the same AZ as the client, reducing latency and improving application performance. Until now, customers who wanted lower latency used other routing policies, such as latency-based or geoproximity routing. With this launch, DNS queries from your clients are answered with resources in the same AZ. This keeps traffic within the AZ and gives your clients faster responses. If there's no record for the client's AZ, Route 53 falls back to a record for a less specific location: the Zone Group, then the AWS Region, and then Global, in the same order. To get started, create AZ-affinity records and choose a location type for each: Availability Zone, Zone Group, Region, or Global. For Availability Zone records, specify the AZ ID, such as use1-az1. You can associate a health check with any AZ-

title: Amazon VPC IPAM policies now support automated internet firewall and AWS Lambda Web Functions and MicroVMs
summary: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) IP Address Manager (IPAM) policies now support AWS Network Firewall automated internet firewall and AWS Lambda Web Functions and MicroVMs. You can centrally configure IPAM policies across AWS accounts and AWS Regions to allocate public IPv4 addresses to these resources from specific IPAM pools, such as Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) addresses or Amazon-provided contiguous IPv4 blocks. This enables a stronger security posture, simplifies network and security operations, and can reduce public IPv4 costs when you use BYOIP. Many customers allowlist the public IPs of their AWS resources in network access control lists (ACLs) and firewalls. Previously, keeping these resources on allowlisted addresses depended on each application team. With this launch, you can define allocation rules for them alongside existing resource types, so security teams can add IP-based filters with confidence that these resources draw addresses from approved ranges. For Lambda Web Func

title: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks now supported in the AWS Asia Pacific (Osaka)
summary: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks are now supported in the AWS Asia Pacific (Osaka) Region. Outposts racks extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to virtually any on-premises data center or colocation space for a truly consistent hybrid experience. Organizations of every size, from startups to enterprises to public sector agencies, can now order Outposts racks connected to this newly supported Region to optimize for latency and data residency needs. This regional expansion provides additional flexibility in the number of AWS Regions that customers' Outposts can connect to. To learn more about second-generation Outposts racks, read the AWS Outposts blog post and user guide . For the latest list of countries and territories and the AWS Regions where second-generation Outposts racks are supported, see the AWS Outposts FAQs page .

title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports customer managed keys in AWS KMS
summary: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports customer managed keys (CMK) in AWS Key Management Service (KMS) for data encryption at rest. CMK gives you full control over the lifecycle and usage of your KMS keys , helping meet compliance requirements in regulated industries like financial services and healthcare. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code. Use MicroVMs to build applications like AI coding assistants, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. To get started, create a CMK in AWS KMS and configure its cryptographic properties, metadata, and AWS IAM access permissions. Then, specify this CMK as a parameter when you create a MicroVM image or run a MicroVM. title: AWS CDK Blocks reaches general availability
summary: AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) Blocks, known as AWS Blocks in preview, is now generally available. It is an expansion of the CDK that simplifies building production-grade applications on AWS, by providing production-ready building blocks for common app features, such as data storage and processing, background jobs, and building AI agents. CDK Blocks build upon CDK constructs. CDK constructs are reusable pieces of code that define AWS infrastructure, such as a database or a storage bucket. CDK Blocks packages a CDK construct along with the connecting code applications need to use that infrastructure, incorporating AWS service-specific best practices, such as safe retries, dead-letter routing and partial-batch failures, and a local testing setup, reducing the code and configuration you need to write and maintain. It also enables you to compose and share your own custom components that incorporate your organization's requirements, helping teams build production ready applications fas

title: AWS Backup now supports incremental backups for Amazon DynamoDB
summary: AWS Backup now supports incremental backups of Amazon DynamoDB tables, enabling you to reduce backup storage while maintaining backup schedules as frequent as one hour. Until now, AWS Backup created a full copy of your DynamoDB tables. With this launch, after an initial full backup, each incremental backup now captures only the data that changed, and AWS Backup takes a new full backup every 15 days. This lets you store less data and back up more often. You can restore from any recovery point in the chain, and you can schedule incremental backups anywhere from hourly to weekly frequencies. You can store incremental backups in both AWS Backup vaults and logically air-gapped vaults. Cross-Region backup copies are also incremental, further increasing your savings. AWS Backup turns on incremental backups automatically for new customers who protect DynamoDB. title: Announcing a new skill for AI agents in Amazon Textract Core
summary: Amazon Textract Core now lets AI agents extract text, tables, forms, and other data from documents through a skill, with no server to run or infrastructure to deploy. The skill guides an agent to the right Amazon Textract Core API for each document and includes a tested parser that converts the output into reading-order text and structured fields, such as answers to questions, receipt and invoice details, and identity document fields. Previously, teams that connected an agent to Amazon Textract had to build and maintain their own integration. You ask in natural language, and the agent returns the answers you need. The skill processes multi-page PDFs and returns every page in reading order. It uses confidence scores to accept high-confidence results and flags the rest, so you can route them to your own review process. For example, you can ask an agent to turn a patient's intake form into structured data and flag unclear fields for staff review. The skill is available at no additional ch

title: Amazon VPC Lattice now supports CloudWatch metrics for VPC resources
summary: Amazon VPC Lattice now publishes Amazon CloudWatch metrics for VPC resources. Resource owners — those who share resources via VPC Lattice — and resource consumers — those who access those shared resources — can now see TCP traffic to resources such as databases, clusters, and on-premises endpoints. Resource owners get metrics for resource gateways and resource configurations. Consumers get metrics for resource endpoints, service network endpoints, and service network VPC associations. Previously, resource access logs were the primary way to see this traffic, but they required additional processing and provided limited real-time visibility. Now you can monitor your layer-4 resources directly in CloudWatch. With these metrics, you can proactively catch connectivity issues and optimize resource capacity. Capacity planning metrics — including bytes processed, new flows, and active flows — let resource owners monitor traffic per resource gateway and per resource configuration to track load

title: Amazon Transcribe now available in AWS European Sovereign Cloud
summary: Amazon Transcribe is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. Customers who need to keep data and operations within the EU for regulatory compliance and data sovereignty requirements can now use automatic speech recognition (ASR) in the Region to turn speech into text. Amazon Transcribe offers two ways to transcribe audio in this Region. Batch transcription processes media files stored in Amazon S3, and streaming transcription returns text in real time from live audio over HTTP/2 or WebSocket. Both support custom vocabularies, so you can improve recognition of domain-specific terms such as product names, industry jargon, and proper nouns. To learn more, see Getting started with Amazon Transcribe , Supported languages and language-specific features , and AWS European Sovereign Cloud pricing .

title: Amazon Textract Insights is now generally available
summary: Amazon Textract Insights brings document understanding to Amazon Textract. It is a new generative AI feature of Amazon Textract, and is now generally available in the US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) AWS Regions. Amazon Textract Insights splits, classifies, and extracts structured data from documents in a single asynchronous request. Documents like insurance claims, tax packets, and onboarding packages often arrive as one long scan that holds many documents in no fixed order. Processing them has meant assembling and operating separate steps for text detection, splitting, classification, and extraction. Amazon Textract Insights handles that work in one managed request, with no AI models to train. How it works: You define the fields you need in a blueprint, a JSON schema that describes each field in natural language, or you can start from a library of AWS public blueprints for common document types such as W-2s, invoices, and bank statements. Amazon Textract Insights can split

title: Amazon SageMaker adds new capabilities – improved blueprints and catalog experience, simplified data quality monitoring, and support for DuckDB 2.0 and DuckDB extensions
summary: Improved blueprints: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now gives project teams more ownership of their data and resources, within governance policies that administrators set centrally. Additional releases include faster notebook queries through DuckDB 2.0 support and data quality monitoring at catalog scale. Improved data quality monitoring: Teams can also profile entire catalogs and databases to keep data statistics current. Project members can get email notifications for all supported notification types, including data quality and data profiling runs. Improved catalog experience: Administrators can now manage metadata forms, business glossaries, and custom asset types in one place, with a consistent experience across all domain types. They can also transfer asset ownership to the project that knows the data best. Members of that project can then curate those assets and approve or reject subscription requests themselves. title: Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones now support public DNS fallback
summary: Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones now support public DNS fallback. When a query for a name in your private hosted zone's domain doesn't match a record in the zone, Route 53 returns the answer from public DNS instead of a "name not found" (NXDOMAIN) error. Public DNS fallback is part of the Advanced Hosted Zones offering. Until now, Route 53 treated an associated private hosted zone as fully authoritative for its domain, so queries for names that weren't in the zone returned NXDOMAIN. To resolve a few names privately, customers also had to copy every other record from their public zone into the private hosted zone and keep the two in sync. With public DNS fallback, you add only the names you need privately, and every other name resolves from your existing public DNS. For example, your private hosted zone for example.com points example.com to a private endpoint, while partner.example.com exists only in public DNS. Before, a lookup for partner.example.com returned NXDOMAIN. Now it reso

title: Amazon Route 53 now offers Advanced Hosted Zones
summary: Amazon Route 53 now offers Advanced Hosted Zones, a new hosted zone tier with additional guardrails, visibility, and resilience features. Advanced Hosted Zones include Change Guardrails that prevent accidental record deletions, record-level Change History, and public DNS fallback in private hosted zones. A single mistaken DNS change can take part of your domain offline, such as deleting a record that is still serving traffic or removing a delegation that resolvers are still using. To protect against this, customers build their own validation pipelines, review processes, and audit tooling. With Change Guardrails turned on, Route 53 checks each change before applying it. It blocks deleting a record that is still receiving DNS queries, a record that an alias record in the same hosted zone points to, or a delegation that is still in use. When a guardrail blocks a change, Route 53 rejects the whole request with an error that explains why, and no records change. Guardrails apply to every cha

title: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP launches a new generation of file systems with up to 3.6x higher performance
summary: Today, we're announcing third-generation Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file systems, which deliver up to 216 GB/s of throughput and 8.6 million SSD IOPS per file system, up to 3x more throughput and up to 3.6x more SSD IOPS than previous-generation file systems. Built on the latest AWS compute and storage technologies, third-generation file systems give you even more flexibility to scale performance as your workloads and usage patterns evolve. FSx for ONTAP is the first and only storage service that allows you to launch and run fully managed, fully featured ONTAP file systems in the cloud. FSx for ONTAP file systems are powered by up to 12 highly available (HA) pairs of file servers to deliver storage and performance scalability. With previous-generation file systems, each HA pair delivers up to 6 GB/s of throughput and 200,000 SSD IOPS. With third-generation file systems, each HA pair delivers up to 18 GB/s of throughput and 720,000 SSD IOPS, giving you even more flexibility to scale yo

title: AWS Partner Central guides now available in the console and through AWS Partner Central Agents
summary: AWS announces AWS Partner Central guides with access through the AWS Partner Central console and the AWS Partner Central Agents Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. The guides give AWS Partners one place to search, read, and share content that AWS organizes to help partners grow and expand their business. The guides hold authoritative, partner-specific knowledge on programs, benefits, technical topics, marketing, funding, and more, which requires sign-in and permissions. Partners benefit from more accurate answers about programs, benefits, and requirements. Partners can browse by topic, search instantly across every guide, and see content based on their recent activity and AWS program updates. Partners can also ask AWS Partner Central Agents questions in their own words, such as "Which guides explain the requirements for the AWS Foundational Technical Review?" or "Show me everything in Migration Acceleration Program quick reference." Partner Central guides complement the public informa

title: CVE-2026-132607 - GCM authentication tag length downgrade in Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-191-AWS Publication Date: 11/19/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-132607, an issue in the decryption component of Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP in the AWS SDK for PHP. The client did not verify the length of the AES-GCM authentication tag recorded in an object's metadata. A user with read and write access to an encrypted object, who knows or can guess its plaintext, might craft a ciphertext that decrypts to plaintext of their choice of the same length. This requires repeated writes to the object. The issue does not disclose the plaintext or the encryption key. Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.

title: AWS Marketplace now supports agentic payments with AgentCore
summary: AWS Marketplace now supports agentic payments over the x402 protocol, so AI agents can discover and buy select products and pay per request in US dollars through AgentCore payments, part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Agents often need paid APIs, data, or content mid-task, but access usually requires a person to sign up, add a payment method, and create an API key. With agentic payments, customers skip that per-seller setup, and charges settle on their existing AWS bill with no crypto wallet required. Customers enable the AWS Marketplace payment connector in AgentCore payments, then they or their agents find listings through the AWS Marketplace connector in AgentCore Gateway. For example, a research agent can buy a single web search, or a coding agent can call a paid guardrail service. Customers can set spending limits, approved sellers, and guardrails before agents transact, Private Marketplace policies still apply, and transactions appear in AWS CloudTrail and AWS Cost Explorer. title: Amazon Cognito now supports client ID metadata documents
summary: Amazon Cognito now supports OAuth client ID metadata documents (CIMD). Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. With CIMD, Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and AI agents can sign users in to your user pool without registering a separate app client. Previously, each external client needed its own app client, either created in advance or through dynamic client registration, and you had to manage and clean up those clients over time. With CIMD, a client uses an HTTPS URL as its client ID and publishes a JSON metadata document at that URL. When the client starts sign-in, Cognito fetches and validates the document and uses it to identify the client and validate its sign-in request. You decide which clients to accept with CIMD policies that map URL patterns to one of your app clients, and Cognito grants only the scopes and grant types that both the app client and the metadata document allow. For example, a co

title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now delivers up to 50% higher write throughput
summary: With upgrades to its storage layer, Amazon Aurora DSQL now delivers up to 50% higher write throughput for many transactional workloads. Data loads finish sooner, and tables whose primary key always increases, such as tables keyed by a timestamp, an identity column, or a time-ordered ID like ULID or UUIDv7, see even greater benefits. Applications such as audit logs, ledgers, and event feeds are read in time order, and keying them by time keeps those reads fast. You can now use that design for write-heavy tables too. In our tests, an audit log table keyed by event time accepted up to 200% more inserts per second. The improvement is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL is available, for new and existing clusters, at no additional cost. To learn more, see the Aurora DSQL User Guide .

title: Amazon CloudFront adds IP based routing and connection logs to SaaS Manager
summary: Amazon CloudFront now allows web development and SaaS platforms to serve different tiers of customers on the same wildcard domain by using IP addresses to route them to the right configuration. For example, these platforms can serve premium and pro customers from dedicated Anycast static IP address lists, each with its own configuration, and serve free-tier customers on the shared CloudFront IP addresses, all under *. example.com . Additionally, these customers also have visibility into viewer connections with connection logging. Previously, CloudFront chose the configuration from the domain name alone, so the same domain always went to the same configuration. With address-based selection, you can register the same wildcard domain on several IP lists and send each list to its own tenant. Because you control which clients resolve to which IP list, you can shift traffic between your service tiers without your customers needing to make any changes. You can also serve IoT devices, embedded

title: Amazon CloudFront simplifies domain moves and onboarding for SaaS Manager
summary: Amazon CloudFront now lets web development platforms and SaaS providers move a customer's domain to their platform in a single request with no downtime, and serve requests to the domain while the TLS certificate is being configured. The CloudFront multi-tenant distributions allow these platforms to serve many customer domains from one shared configuration. Together, these features help move existing AWS customers to multi-tenant distributions without impacting their traffic. Previously, moving a domain that was already in use required disabling the original distribution, using a wildcard workaround, or contacting AWS Support. Now you can bring customer domains onto your multi-tenant setup as part of creating or updating a tenant. With the new OnDomainTakeover option, CloudFront checks domain ownership through DNS records and then moves one or more domains in a single request. This works within an AWS account or across accounts. If you add a domain before its certificate is issued, Clou

title: Amazon Connect launches Resolutions, an agentic solution for high-volume operational work
summary: Amazon Connect Customer announces the general availability of Resolutions, an agentic operations solution that resolves high-volume work end-to-end, including refund requests, transaction disputes, fraud investigations, and insurance claims. Resolutions helps businesses reduce resolution times and cost to serve by combining the reasoning of AI agents with the reliability of deterministic workflows. Every request follows business policy, gets the oversight it requires, and ends in a verifiable outcome. Managers describe a process in natural language or upload standard operating procedures (SOPs), and Resolutions generates a Work plan in minutes. As it builds the Work plan, Resolutions asks clarifying questions that surface exceptions, set decision rules, and define approval thresholds, closing the gaps an SOP leaves open. Resolutions then opens a Resolutions Case for each incoming request and applies the right Work plan. AI agents gather information, apply policy, act across your busine

title: AWS Marketplace agent mode now helps you assess, buy, and deploy solutions
summary: You can now assess a seller's security, buy, and deploy supported products in one conversation with AWS Marketplace agent mode, the conversational AI experience for procuring cloud solutions. You share your requirement once, and agent mode applies them as it guides you through discovery, purchase, and deployment. Describe your use case in natural language to get recommended software, services, AI agents and tools, and multi-product solutions that fit your business needs. To assess a seller's security, request documents such as System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2 reports, and get a criterion-by-criterion assessment against a standard cloud security questionnaire, the Consensus Assessments Initiative Questionnaire (CAIQ). When you're ready to buy, sign in with your AWS account. Agent mode explains pricing and terms so you know what you're committing to, shows your organizations' purchase requirements, and completes the purchase after you review the terms and confirm. For supported p

title: AWS Lambda durable functions now supports OpenTelemetry tracing
summary: AWS Lambda announces OpenTelemetry (OTel) support for Lambda durable functions. You can now trace your durable executions and emit traces to Amazon CloudWatch and other industry-standard observability tools. This helps you find bottlenecks in your system, root cause failures faster, and understand how your workflows behave in production. With Lambda durable functions, you can build resilient, multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing and automatic retries. Durable functions can run for hours, or days, suspending and resuming across many Lambda invocations. The new OpenTelemetry plugin emits a unified trace that spans a full durable execution, including steps, waits, callbacks, and chained function invocations. You can use the trace to gain operational insights across your executions including step durations, retries, and failures across executions. The OpenTelemetry plugin is available for the TypeScript, Python, and Java SDKs. Yo

title: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications now supports WebAuthn redirection
summary: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications now supports WebAuthn redirection, so users can sign in to websites and applications in their streaming session with a FIDO2 authenticator on their local device, such as a security key, Windows Hello, or Touch ID. Previously, an authenticator attached to the user's computer was not available inside the streaming session, so organizations that require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA) had to use weaker sign-in methods or keep those applications off WorkSpaces Applications. This helps organizations with FIDO2 requirements stream those applications. When an application in the session makes a WebAuthn request, WorkSpaces Applications forwards it to the user's device, where the authenticator signs it and returns the response. Private keys never leave the user's device. Administrators turn it on per stack in the console or API, and on Windows fleets can limit it to an allow list of processes. For example, a bank can let employees sign in to M

title: Amazon Route 53 now supports health checks for private endpoints
summary: Amazon Route 53 now offers Private Endpoint Health Checks, enabling business-critical workloads that never touch the public internet, such as internal APIs, databases, and self-hosted nodes behind internal load balancers or in private subnets, to use native health monitoring and automatic DNS failover. Customers can health-check any reachable private target by IP address, domain, or port over HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP. Customers can associate these health checks with Route 53 DNS records across routing policies in private hosted zones, so Route 53 routes traffic only to healthy endpoints and manages failover automatically. Previously, teams built custom control loops using Amazon CloudWatch alarms, AWS Lambda functions, and the Route 53 API to achieve DNS failover for private resources. With t his approach , failover took several minutes and added operational burden. Detection and DNS failover with Private Endpoint Health Checks are designed to complete in seconds rather than minutes, the se

title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports deal-level revenue attribution for AWS Marketplace offers and opportunities
summary: Today, AWS announces deal-level revenue attribution for AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) capabilities. AWS Partners can now see how the AWS revenue measured for their products maps to specific AWS Marketplace offers and/or APN Customer Engagements (ACE) opportunities. Until now, partners who implemented AWS Revenue Measurement via Resource Tagging , User Agent String or AWS Marketplace Metering could view aggregated, product-level attributed revenue. With this launch, partners can view attributed revenue by offers and opportunities on the Attributed Revenue dashboard in AWS Partner Central for components hosted in partners' own AWS accounts. Two new capabilities make this possible: Revenue Attribution IDs and Marketplace Revenue Share. A Revenue Attribution ID is a unique identifier that allows partners to allocate a product's measured AWS revenue to specific offers and opportunities. Partners create a Revenue Attribution ID, associate it with their deal

title: IAM Roles Anywhere now supports aliases to simplify workload configuration
summary: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles Anywhere now supports aliases, which are readable names that you assign to trust anchors, profiles, and certificate revocation lists (CRLs). Your workloads can request temporary credentials using a trust anchor or profile alias Amazon Resource Name (ARN) instead of an ARN with a system-generated ID, and you can use alias ARNs in many of the operations that manage these resources. Aliases make configurations easier to read and review: an alias ARN that ends in alias/trust-anchor/production-ca can show which certificate authority (CA) a workload uses. Previously, workload configurations, such as credential helper settings in machine images and configuration management templates, referenced trust anchors and profiles by ARNs that contain system-generated IDs, which differ in every account and Region. With this launch, you can assign the same alias in each account and Region, so one configuration template works across them with only the accoun

title: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute timeout for on-demand Event Functions
summary: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute function timeout for Event Functions that run on demand, doubling the 15-minute limit for synchronous , asynchronous , and event source mapping (ESM) invocations. On Lambda Managed Instances , synchronous invocations also support up to 30 minutes, while asynchronous and ESM invocations keep the 90-minute timeout launched in September 2026. You can now run long-running workloads such as AI inference, media transcoding, and financial calculations for spiky or steady-state traffic without re-architecting your applications. Customers use Event Functions to build event-driven processors, API backends, and data pipelines. By default, Event Functions run on demand, and Lambda scales them automatically to handle spiky traffic. For steady-state traffic, you can also run them on Lambda Managed Instances, which runs functions on Amazon EC2 instances and maintains the operational simplicity of Lambda.
