title: Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming now provides a Linux broadcast SDK
summary: The Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) Linux broadcast SDK is now available for IVS Real-Time Streaming. Applications running on Linux can join an IVS stage, receive audio from participants, and send audio back to the stage in real time. The SDK provides a C API and Go language bindings. The Linux broadcast SDK is ideal for AI applications that enrich live streams by processing audio, such as transcription, translation, and content moderation, as well as voice agents that converse with participants. Amazon IVS is a managed live streaming solution designed to make low-latency or real-time video available to viewers around the world. Visit the AWS Region table for a full list of AWS Regions where the Amazon IVS console and APIs for control and creation of video streams are available. To learn more, see IVS Broadcast SDK: Linux Guide .

title: AWS WAF launches new Security Analytics Dashboard for real-time investigations
summary: AWS WAF now gives you one place to find and stop unwanted traffic across every application in your account. The new AWS WAF security analytics dashboard brings together traffic from all of your protection packs (web ACLs), whether they protect Regional resources or Amazon CloudFront distributions, into a single view. The dashboard also lets you search request logs right in the console, with no logging pipeline to build, and includes 21 days of full-fidelity request data at no additional cost. It is available alongside the existing dashboard for each protection pack (WebACL), which continues to work as it does today. Until now, spotting a trend across your applications, such as a bot campaign hitting several endpoints or a spike in blocked requests, meant opening each web ACL in turn or individually querying AWS WAF logs. With the AWS WAF security analytics dashboard, you can analyze traffic data from every protection pack (WebACL) at once. You can filter and group traffic by dimensions

title: Amazon Cognito now supports AWS Secrets Manager for app client secrets
summary: Amazon Cognito now integrates with AWS Secrets Manager , so you can store and manage your user pool app client secrets in Secrets Manager. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. An app client secret authenticates your application to Cognito. Previously, you had to manage and rotate these secrets in Cognito directly. With this integration, you can leverage Secrets Manager for capabilities including rotation, access control with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies, and encryption with an AWS managed key or your own AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. This can help with periodic credential rotation or compliance requirements; this also helps with keeping secrets out of the console. You can enable this integration for either a new or an existing app client, and disable it at any time. This integration is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito and AWS Secrets Man

title: AWS Partner Central now supports AI-assisted listing experience for product, services, and solutions
summary: AWS Marketplace search, Agent Mode, and AWS sales teams use listings to recommend partner offerings to AWS customers. Partners who sell software and services can now create and improve their listings in AWS Partner Central with the new AI-assisted listing experience. It drafts content from a partner's website and other materials, then shows which sections need clearer details, use cases, or evidence of customer outcomes. For single-AMI products, it also drafts the usage instructions buyers see after subscribing. Partners see, for each section, whether it meets what buyers look for, and choose which suggestions to use and review all content before publishing. Partners can position products and professional services as distinct solutions for different industries, use cases, or outcomes. Each solution gets its own AWS Marketplace page, bringing its case studies and AWS Specializations together with the listing's pricing, reviews, and trust information, so buyers can evaluate and buy from

title: Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration now supports Amazon VPC
summary: Aurora PostgreSQL databases created with express configuration can now move into an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) with a single API call or a modify action in the Amazon RDS console. This helps you take AI-built prototypes and other applications to production without migrating data, while meeting your security and compliance requirements. You can also create a new database cluster inside a VPC using express configuration. With express configuration, Aurora PostgreSQL lets you create and query a serverless database in seconds. Connectivity runs through an internet access gateway, which makes this a good fit for rapid prototyping and AI agent-driven development. When your application is ready for production, a single ModifyDBCluster API call moves the cluster into a VPC and turns off the internet access gateway. That gives you security groups, private subnets, and features such as Aurora Global Database, Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, and Amazon RDS Proxy. The move requires no d

title: Amazon Aurora now supports moving clusters to a different VPC
summary: Aurora PostgreSQL and Aurora MySQL clusters can now move from one Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) to another without data migration. You can move a cluster with a single API call or a modify action in the Amazon RDS console. This lets you move a cluster to a VPC with more IP address space or a non-overlapping CIDR range, consolidate your network architecture, or meet changing security and compliance requirements. Previously, moving an Aurora cluster to a different VPC meant creating a new cluster in the target VPC, migrating your data, and updating your applications with new connection strings. Now, a single ModifyDBCluster API call moves your existing cluster to the new VPC. Your data stays in place, your cluster endpoint stays the same, and connectivity is interrupted only briefly during the move. Before you start, turn off features that are tied to the cluster's current VPC, such as Aurora Global Database, Amazon RDS Proxy, and Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments. You can set them

title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports restarting existing connectors
service: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
summary: Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now supports restarting both existing and newly created connectors and their tasks in place, enabling fast recovery for streaming data pipelines. Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, recovering from failures required deleting and recreating the connector, resulting in downtime and operational overhead. With this feature, you can restart your connector and all its tasks in place, or selectively restart only the failed tasks, making recovery seamless. You can also restart connectors that have no failed tasks to recover from transient issues or to pick up changes in external systems or dependencies. This restart capability is available at no additional cost through the Amazon MSK Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDK, and AWS CDK in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Connect is avai

title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports multi-Region peering across continents
summary: Amazon Aurora DSQL now lets you create multi-Region clusters whose Regions are on different continents, such as US East (N. Virginia) and Europe (Ireland). Until now, the Regions in a multi-Region cluster had to be in the same geographic Region set. With intercontinental multi-Region clusters, applications on two continents read and write to one strongly consistent database. If a Region becomes unavailable, committed writes are preserved and applications keep reading and writing in the other Region. You choose the two peer Regions and the witness Region. Place your database close to users on each continent, or separate failure domains as widely as your resilience needs require. Intercontinental multi-Region clusters are available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL supports multi-Region clusters. To learn more, see Multi-Region cluster availability in the Aurora DSQL User Guide.

title: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer contact sharing at subscription
summary: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer contact sharing. When customers subscribe to a third-party product, they can share their contact information with the seller. This helps sellers onboard new customers, send deployment guides and setup instructions, provide technical support, and share product updates from the start of the subscription. Customers share their first name, last name, email address, company name, and country or region in the deployment contact information section of the AWS Marketplace procurement page. AWS Marketplace pre-fills this section from the customer's previous purchases, AWS Profile , or AWS account details where available, so customers don't need to enter it again for each subscription. Customers can complete or edit any field before they subscribe, and view what they shared on the agreement details page in the AWS Marketplace console. Sellers can view the customer's contact information on the agreement details page in AWS Partner Central, or retrieve it with th

title: AgentCore runtime instances now support Nested Virtualization
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances now support nested virtualization, so your agents can run their own virtual machines and emulators inside a session with Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM). Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. Nested virtualization serves agents that rely on tools that run in a virtual machine, such as mobile emulators or virtual machine sandboxes. You turn on nested virtualization when you create a Linux capacity provider, and agents in every session on its instances can use KVM. For example, your agents can run Android emulators to build and test mobile apps, or start lightweight virtual machines to isolate the code that they run. Nested virtualization works on supported Intel-based instance types, including the C7i, C8i, M7i, M8i, R7i, and R8i families. Nested virtualization is available on supported instance types in all AWS Regions where AgentCore runt

title: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store raises API throughput limits
summary: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store has increased the default throughput limits for five API operations. For accounts that have turned on the higher throughput setting, the quotas have changed as follows, in transactions per second (TPS): GetParametersByPath (from 100 to 500 TPS) PutParameter (10 to 50) DeleteParameter (5 to 50) DescribeParameters (10 to 100) GetParameterHistory (10 to 100) Parameter Store provides powerful, hierarchical storage for configuration data. The higher quotas give more headroom to workloads that call these operations in bursts. Examples include applications that load configuration by path when many AWS Lambda functions start at once, infrastructure as code deployments that create or update many parameters, and cleanup jobs that bulk-delete stale parameters.

title: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks now supported in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region
summary: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks are now supported in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. Outposts racks extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to virtually any on-premises data center or colocation space for a truly consistent hybrid experience. Organizations of every size, from startups to enterprises to public sector agencies, can now order Outposts racks connected to this newly supported Region to optimize for latency and data residency needs. This regional expansion provides additional flexibility in the number of AWS Regions that customers' Outposts can connect to. To learn more about second-generation Outposts racks, read the AWS Outposts blog post and user guide . For the latest list of countries and territories and the AWS Regions where second-generation Outposts racks are supported, see the AWS Outposts FAQs page . For pricing information in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region, please refer to this page .

title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports closed-source models in Amazon Bedrock
summary: AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS announces expanded Amazon Bedrock support in AWS Revenue Measurement. Partners can now gain attributed revenue visibility for their solutions' use of closed-source models in Amazon Bedrock, giving them a more complete view of the revenue their solutions drive. Until now, only Amazon models (such as Amazon Nova) and open-weight models in Amazon Bedrock were included in AWS Revenue Measurement. With this update, attributed revenue for Amazon Bedrock reflects the total Bedrock charges, including closed-source model usage. Partners who already use Resource Tagging, User Agent string, Identity Tagging, or SaaS Account Tagging for Amazon Bedrock automatically benefit from the expanded coverage, with no additional implementation needed. AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more, review the Amazon Bedrock

title: AWS Partner Central Agents now guide higher-quality co-sell submissions and explain co-sell motions
summary: Today, AWS announces that AWS Partner Central Agents now guide AWS Partners to create and enrich opportunities for a high-quality submission, and explain the assigned co-sell motion of each opportunity and why AWS assigned it. Since the launch of Agentic co-selling on June 16, 2026, AWS Partner Central Agents score every opportunity with an Opportunity Quality Score and assign co-sell motions including AWS Field-engaged, Agent-engaged, or Partner-led. When partners create an opportunity, the agents now guide them to a high-quality submission by asking for the details the Opportunity Quality Score measures, such as the customer's business problem, dated next steps, the Partner Primary Need from AWS, and the AWS services the customer will adopt, based on the co-selling best-practice guidance . After submission, the agents explain the reason behind each opportunity's co-sell motion and why AWS assigned it. Where the partner can act, the agents recommend the next step: for Agent-engaged op

title: AWS Partner Central Agents now generate Value Realization Plans
summary: Today, AWS announces that AWS Partner Central Agents can now generate Value Realization Plans (VRPs) for the Business Value Realization (BVR) motion in AWS Partner Central . The VRP is the plan of record for a BVR engagement. The agentic experience generates a VRP that includes the customer's business goals; plan for adoption, change management, and governance; and baseline key performance indicators (KPIs) for Partners to review and finalize. AWS Partner Central launched the BVR motion on June 16, 2026, to help Partners drive business outcomes for their customers by structuring AWS service adoption into defined stages, with funding tied to demonstrated value. With this launch, Partners in the BVR motion no longer start a VRP from a blank page. The agents recommend KPIs, ramp targets, and baseline measurements based on nomination data, opportunity context, and service benchmarks. They also flag gaps before submission, such as a lack of customer sponsorship, and identify next steps. Par

title: AWS Network Firewall launches explicit proxy functionality and NAT Gateway association
summary: You can now associate AWS Network Firewall with NAT Gateway and use it both as an explicit proxy and a transparent firewall with native network address translation. You can use this capability with existing Network Firewall features to filter traffic to and from your applications and prevent data exfiltration and malware injection. AWS Network Firewall is a stateful, managed, network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention service for your VPC. Customers use it to filter their traffic and secure AWS resources. With this launch, you can configure Network Firewall with native NAT Gateway association and use it for both explicit proxy and routed filtering functionalities. Both these functionalities are governed by a single security policy that you maintain centrally. This capability works with existing Network Firewall features including managed rule groups from Amazon or Marketplace, active threat defense, Geo-IP filtering, URL and domain category filtering, container attribute-b

title: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer approval workflows
summary: Today, AWS Marketplace announces the general availability of buyer approvals. This lets you decide which AWS Marketplace purchases need sign-off, who approves them, and where approval happens. You can define buying policies for the conditions that matter to you, such as purchase amount, product type, pricing, and whether an offer is public or private. Additionally, you can choose to route each purchase request to the right place: the AWS Marketplace console, a chain of approvers by email, or your procurement system in Coupa or SAP Ariba. When you route approvals by email, procurement, finance, legal, and cloud governance teams can approve requests without needing to sign into the AWS console. They see the product, price, terms, and can approve right from their email. For example, you can route large software commitments to Coupa or SAP Ariba for review, send mid-size purchases to multiple approvers by email, and let low-cost or pay-as-you-go purchases go through without approval. When

title: AWS Marketplace now offers Express Checkout for buyers without an AWS account
summary: Today, AWS announces AWS Marketplace Express Checkout , a simpler way for businesses that don't have an existing AWS account to buy software from established vendors in AWS Marketplace . Express Checkout is built for businesses that don't use AWS today and just want to buy software. With no cloud setup required, buyers sign in with an email address or a social login, pay with a credit or debit card, and check out in a few steps. Businesses that buy multiple applications this way can manage all of their Express Checkout subscriptions in one place, without a separate billing login for each vendor. From there, they can update their card, download invoices, or cancel a subscription themselves. For sellers, Express Checkout opens a new segment of self-serve business buyers, using the same listing and AWS Marketplace integration they use today. Sellers with an eligible public SaaS listing can request to add their product to the Express Checkout catalog. Express Checkout is available for elig

title: AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Rust is now generally available
summary: Today, AWS announces the general availability of the open source AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Rust. Rust developers can use the SDK to build resilient, long-running workflows using Lambda durable functions, to create multi-step applications like infrastructure automation, deployment rollouts with approval gates, and pipelines that call AI models and pause for human review directly in their Rust code without implementing custom progress tracking. Lambda durable functions extend Lambda's event-driven programming model with operations that checkpoint progress automatically and pause execution for up to one year when waiting on external events. With the SDK, developers write a durable function as an ordinary async Rust function that awaits each durable operation like any other future and can run independent operations concurrently. The SDK includes steps that save their results, callbacks for human-in-the-loop and agent-in-the-loop workflows, invocations of other durable functions,

title: AWS Health now supports resource and account tags
summary: AWS Health now supports resource and account tags in Health events. This new capability enables you to enrich Health events with resource tags and account tags, providing additional context to help you manage and respond to events more effectively. With this feature, you can now view resource tags directly within Health events for supported AWS services. This allows you to quickly identify which resources are affected and understand their business context without needing to navigate to individual service consoles. Additionally, account-level tags help you categorize and filter events across your organization, making it easier to route notifications and automate responses based on your organizational structure. This enhancement is particularly valuable for organizations managing large-scale AWS deployments. By leveraging tags in Health events, you can streamline incident response workflows, improve cost allocation tracking for health-related events, and enable more granular event filter

title: AWS expands Amazon Connect Customer Competency to Software Partners
summary: AWS announces the expansion of the Amazon Connect Customer Competency to Software Partners. The AWS Specialization now recognizes both Services and Software Partners with technical depth and proven success on Amazon Connect Customer—from migrating legacy contact centers and operationalizing AI at scale, to building new solutions on top of Amazon Connect Customer. Modern customers want smooth, tailored interactions wherever they engage, but legacy customer experience systems weren't designed to provide them. They rely on queues, manual routing, and handle-time metrics as control mechanisms, with AI added as a separate layer rather than built in from the start. The Competency adds three new categories for Software Partners: Customer Experience – Solution Extensions , for solutions that integrate with Amazon Connect Customer across the customer experience lifecycle; Connect A2A Collaboration – Agent Certification , for third-party AI agents certified to work alongside Amazon Connect Custo

title: Announcing Data as a Service for AWS Marketplace
summary: Today, AWS Marketplace announces the general availability of Data as a Service, a new product type that lets customers buy third-party datasets and licensed content. Customers often have the models and compute they need, but buying third-party data means adding each provider as a new supplier, negotiating separate contracts, and waiting on procurement cycles. Customers can now find and subscribe to Data as a Service products from AWS Marketplace sellers, and use them to enrich artificial intelligence (AI) applications, analytics, and other workloads. Customers purchase Data as a Service products through public or private offers, and charges appear on their existing AWS invoice. For example, an investment team evaluating private companies can connect its AI agents to private-market data through an API and to credit analysis through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Sellers set their own prices and license terms, using a contract, pay-as-you-go, or contract with consumption pricing

title: Amazon WorkSpaces now lets developers enable Nested Virtualization
summary: Developers on Amazon WorkSpaces Personal can now turn on Nested Virtualization for their own WorkSpaces from the Windows WorkSpaces client, without asking an administrator to make each change. Once an administrator grants self-service permission for the directory, developers can run Docker Desktop, Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2), and Android emulators directly on their WorkSpaces. Administrators can now grant a directory-level self-service permission for Nested Virtualization. Once granted, end users can turn the setting on or off for their own Windows WorkSpace from the WorkSpaces client. Administrators keep control because the permission is set per directory. Self-service is supported on WorkSpaces Personal, using the Desktop Cloud Visualization (DCV) protocol, on Standard bundles and higher. Power (4 vCPU) or higher is recommended. Value and Graphics bundles are not supported. Nested virtualization is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon WorkSpaces is available, excluding t

title: Amazon VPC Flow Logs now supports Amazon EKS metadata
summary: Amazon VPC Flow Logs now adds Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) metadata to flow log records. Each record identifies the pod that sent or received the traffic, along with its cluster, namespace and labels. This makes it faster to investigate security events, understand traffic patterns, and troubleshoot network issues in your EKS clusters, without running monitoring software on your nodes. Amazon EKS runs pods on Amazon EC2 instances, called nodes, and many pods can share one node's network interfaces. Previously, flow log records showed the network interface and IP address for each flow, not the pod behind it. Pods are short-lived, so by the time you investigated unexpected traffic, that IP address could belong to a different pod. To trace traffic back to the right pod, teams built custom tools or ran monitoring software on every node. Now, each record names the pod that sent or received the traffic, so one log gives you both VPC and Kubernetes context. For example, if a

title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects rising response times, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your generative AI inference endpoints
summary: Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors the response time and GPU use of generative AI inference endpoints by default and notifies customers when responses slow down, GPUs sit mostly idle, or a configuration falls behind. Customers run GenAI Inference Recommendations to test configurations designed to restore response time or lower cost on their recent traffic, and they see measured results before anything changes in production. The best configuration for generative AI inference endpoints changes after deployment, as traffic shifts and new serving techniques become available. An endpoint whose latency rises or whose GPUs sit idle keeps running until users complain or the bill arrives. With this launch, SageMaker AI tracks response time and GPU capacity use and checks each endpoint's configuration. It does not read customer requests or responses. Findings include slower response times, unused GPU capacity, and configuration gaps such as an older serving container, missing speculative decoding,

title: Amazon Polly now supports voice cloning
summary: Today, we are excited to announce the general availability of voice cloning in Amazon Polly, as a gated release. Using a few minutes of recordings from a consenting speaker, you can now create a cloned voice that sounds like that speaker. The cloned voices run on the Amazon Polly Generative engine, which delivers similar naturalness and accuracy as the rest of the generative voices. Voice cloning launches in seven languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Hindi. Each cloned voice speaks the language it was recorded in. The cloned voices are automatically encrypted and access-controlled: only you can access your cloned voices. Amazon Polly is a managed service that turns text into natural-sounding speech. With voice cloning, you can give your brand one recognizable voice across IVR and contact centers, voice agents, mobile apps, advertising, and connected devices. You can also create multiple voices for content creation use cases such as audiobooks, e-learnin

title: Amazon Inspector Code Security adds GitHub Enterprise Server and private connectivity
summary: Amazon Inspector Code Security now supports GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) integration and private network connectivity for GHES and GitLab Self-Managed. Code Security is also launching automatic fix pull requests in public preview. Organizations that host GHES or GitLab Self-Managed in private networks can now connect through Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) configurations or AWS CodeConnections, so they can scan repositories without opening their firewalls to the entire AWS IP address range. Amazon Inspector Code Security scans first-party application source code, third-party dependencies, and Infrastructure as Code for vulnerabilities in repositories on GitHub, GHES, and GitLab Self-Managed. With automatic fix pull requests, Amazon Inspector turns its suggested fix into a pull request that developers review and choose whether to merge, instead of applying the fix by hand. It opens pull requests only for high-confidence fixes to static application security testing (SAST) fi

title: Amazon EC2 launches performance status checks and new utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring
summary: Customers can now use Amazon EC2 performance status checks and new utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring to observe and act on the performance of their EC2 workloads without setup within the instance, complementing their in-guest tooling. Customers running performance-sensitive EC2 workloads can use these signals to monitor their CPU and GPU resources, tune capacity needs, and troubleshoot application issues. EC2 performance status checks identify nonterminal hardware conditions that impact performance on accelerated computing instances. These checks also recommend an action, such as rebooting to complete GPU memory row remapping without replacing the instance. The additions to Detailed Monitoring include support for OpenTelemetry metrics, one-minute GPU metrics that help teams tune accelerated workloads, and a new, higher resolution 10-second CPU utilization metric that helps customers size and scale compute capacity using EC2 Auto Scaling. Customers can selectively opt into

title: Amazon Connect Customer now provides AI chat summaries in the CCP
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now provides agents with a generative AI-powered post-contact summary of each chat conversation inside the Contact Control Panel (CCP) within seconds after the chat ends, so agents can complete after contact work from the summary instead of rereading the transcript. The summary covers what the customer needed, the actions the agent took, and any open items, and it appears at the end of the chat transcript. Conversational analytics already generates these summaries for voice and email contacts in the CCP, and this launch adds chat. An airline agent who finishes a flight rebooking chat sees the new travel date, the fare difference charged, and the confirmation sent, then writes the wrap-up note from those three facts. Summaries follow your flow's redaction settings and use the same security profile permissions as voice summaries, so administrators who already enabled voice summaries can turn on chat analytics with post-contact summary in the Set recording and anal

title: Amazon Connect Customer enables Cases by default for new instances
summary: Amazon Connect Customer enables Cases by default for new instances, so operations teams can start tracking and resolving customer issues on day one without any setup work. New instances come with Cases connected to rules for setting SLAs, Customer Profiles for personalizing customer experiences, and Amazon EventBridge for triggering actions in other business applications when a case is updated. Administrators of existing instances can enable these integrations with one click in the AWS Management Console. Newly added case fields sync automatically, so admins don't have to update integrations each time they create fields. Cases is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .

title: Amazon Cognito now supports dynamic client registration
summary: Amazon Cognito now supports OAuth dynamic client registration (DCR, RFC 7591). Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. With DCR support, Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and AI agents can register themselves at runtime. Previously, you had to create an application client in advance for each AI client before it could connect to an MCP server that uses Cognito for authorization. With DCR, Cognito advertises a registration endpoint in its OAuth authorization server metadata. MCP clients that support dynamic client registration discover the endpoint, register to receive a client ID, and then sign users in. You control who can register: either require registration requests to present an access token with a registration scope, or turn on open registration so that any client can register. Dynamically registered clients appear with your other app clients with a client ID prefix and a client type you can filter

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity adds private certificate authority support
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports private certificate authorities (CAs) for custom OAuth 2.0 credential providers. If you already connect your agents to identity providers (IdPs) hosted in your VPC, you can now configure those connections to trust certificates issued by your own CA — including AWS Private CA, enterprise CAs, and self-signed root CAs. AgentCore Identity has supported private IdP connectivity through Amazon VPC Lattice, but until now the IdP still had to present a publicly trusted TLS certificate over that private connection. With private CA support, you store your CA certificate in AWS Secrets Manager or Amazon S3 and reference it from your credential provider configuration. AgentCore Identity uses it to verify the IdP's server certificate directly, removing the need for a publicly trusted certificate or additional infrastructure on the private network path. You can rotate the CA certificate without downtime by combining the current and new certificates in

title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports PL/pgSQL functions and procedures
summary: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports PL/pgSQL, enabling developers to create and execute stored functions and procedures directly in the database. Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database designed for applications requiring active-active availability across multiple AWS Regions with fast reads and writes. You can now encapsulate procedural programming constructs such as IF/ELSE statements, loops, and variable assignments alongside SQL operations within the database. PL/pgSQL support reduces network round trips and improves application performance for data validation workflows, complex calculations, and transactional operations requiring multiple steps. Financial applications can implement account transfer procedures that validate balances, update multiple tables, and handle error conditions within a single database function. PL/pgSQL support is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL is available. To learn more, see PL/pgSQL in the Aurora DSQL User Guide.

title: Amazon S3 Tables now support promoting replicas to writable tables
summary: Amazon S3 Tables replication now lets you make a read-only replica of your Apache Iceberg table a standalone, writable table with a single API call. S3 Tables replication keeps read-only replica tables in sync with your source tables across table buckets, AWS Regions, and accounts. Instead of copying a replica into a new table, you can promote it in place to move writes to another Region. When you disassociate a replica from replication, the standalone table keeps its namespace and table name, so your queries and pipeline code carry over when you point your applications at it. The promoted table then works like an S3 table you created, and you can use it as a source for new replicas. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where S3 Tables replication is supported. You can use the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or S3 Tables API. For pricing details, visit the Amazon S3 pricing page . To learn more, see the S3 Tables overview page and documentation .

title: AWS AppConfig launches support for managing native AI model and AI prompt configuration
summary: Today, AWS AppConfig introduces two new configuration profile types to help you manage the settings for your generative AI applications: AI model invocation configurations, and AI prompt configurations. You can now change model settings and prompts while your application is running, without redeploying code. These updates use AWS AppConfig's safe deployment practices, including gradual rollouts and automatic rollback. This can allow you to move faster and safer, and avoid unexpected behaviors and tokenomics results with rapidly evolving AI solutions. AI model invocation configurations store the settings your application uses to call an AI model. These include the model identifier, inference parameters such as temperature and maximum tokens, and messages such as system prompts and example conversation turns. Provider-specific options are managed in custom parameters, so the same schema works across AI providers. Similarly, AI prompt configurations store prompts as separately versioned a

title: AWS CloudFormation StackSets adds progress visibility to simplify tracking deployments at scale
summary: AWS CloudFormation StackSets now shows stage-by-stage progress for deployments across accounts and AWS Regions, whether you target tens of accounts or thousands. You can follow each deployment as it progresses and take action when needed, without waiting for it to finish. StackSets lets you consistently apply the same infrastructure or application components, such as networking and security settings, across many accounts and Regions in one operation. With this launch, you can see how many stack instances are deployed, how many remain, and which ones need attention. This gives you confidence that a rollout is on track at every stage. Stage-level progress gives you a clear, detailed view of where each deployment stands. Previously, a StackSets deployment showed an overall status while it ran. Now, StackSets also reports progress for two stages. The first is role provisioning, which prepares access in each target account of a service-managed stack set. The second is stack deployment, whic

title: Amazon OpenSearch Memory is now generally available
summary: Today, AWS announced the general availability of Amazon OpenSearch Memory, a new serverless capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service for adding persistent memory to AI agents. OpenSearch Memory stores agent interactions as searchable events, derives useful memories, and retrieves relevant context across sessions, so agents can recall prior decisions, earlier interactions, and user preferences without replaying the full conversation history to the model. Customers can give agents long-term memory without provisioning infrastructure or building separate extraction, indexing, consolidation, and retrieval systems. OpenSearch Memory stores the original events verbatim, makes them searchable within seconds, and asynchronously derives structured memories. It manages the full memory lifecycle, including extraction, embedding, indexing, consolidation (adding, updating, or skipping memories as new information arrives), and retrieval using keyword, semantic, and hybrid search. Customers control ac

title: Introducing the Apache Spark Optimization Agent for AWS Glue ETL
summary: AWS Glue ETL now offers the Apache Spark Optimization Agent, which analyzes completed Spark job runs and delivers cost and performance optimization recommendations within minutes. You can select a cost or performance goal, and the agent returns specific configuration changes with the telemetry evidence and reasoning behind each suggestion. You can use the agent on any completed job run from the AWS Glue console, or from your own tools through the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio MCP Server. The agent takes the job's configuration, logs, and Spark telemetry together with your chosen goal and returns recommendations computed by a deterministic recommendation engine. The engine reads all job artifacts together to identify what is driving runtime and cost: too little parallelism, a skewed join key, memory pressure forcing spill, idle executors, or capacity provisioned beyond what the job uses. When cost and performance trade off, the agent improves the metric you chose while keeping any reg

title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports cross-Region inference routing
summary: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces cross-Region inference routing, which helps keep inference applications available when a region runs short of capacity by sending requests to endpoints deployed in other AWS Regions and AWS accounts. Models served on accelerated instances can reach capacity limits in a single Region, and an unhealthy endpoint can lead to throttling and errors for end users. Previously, teams had to build and maintain their own routing, health checks, and retry logic across Regions. With cross-Region inference routing in SageMaker AI, developers create an inference router, register the real-time endpoints, asynchronous endpoints, and inference components they already run, and point their applications at the router. The router prefers endpoints in its own Region, shifts new requests to healthy destinations in other Regions as errors rise, and returns traffic gradually after the local endpoint recovers. Existing endpoints, models, and containers do not change. Endpoint

title: AWS Lambda now supports GPU instances for Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances
summary: AWS Lambda now supports GPU instances (G-series) for Event Functions running on Lambda Managed Instances, enabling serverless GPU workloads like machine learning inference, media processing, and rendering. Lambda handles all infrastructure tasks, including instance lifecycle, driver management, and auto scaling, while maximizing GPU utilization across concurrent requests with standard EC2 pricing plus a management fee

title: Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports CMCD and additional log fields
summary: Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports additional access log fields that were previously available only in CloudFront real-time logs. You can now include these fields in your standard logs and deliver them to Amazon S3, Amazon CloudWatch Logs, or Amazon Data Firehose, without setting up an additional data stream for real-time logs. The new fields include the IP address of the CloudFront server that handled the request, identifiers that separate traffic on a primary distribution from traffic on a staging distribution, and a media quality confidence score. They also include Common Media Client Data (CMCD) fields, which video players send with each request to report details like bitrate, buffer length, and playback session ID. Streaming teams can use these fields to match playback problems that viewers see with CloudFront delivery data, which makes troubleshooting faster. These fields are available in all CloudFront edge locations, and standard logging pricing applies. To learn m

title: AWS Lambda adds support for GPU instances on Lambda Managed Instances
summary: AWS Lambda now supports GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances using EC2 G-series instances . You can now run GPU-accelerated workloads including AI inference, media processing, 3D rendering, scientific computing, and financial simulations on Lambda without managing GPU drivers, frameworks, or scaling. Lambda runs multiple invocations concurrently in each execution environment and scales responsively based on GPU utilization, CPU utilization, and concurrency to keep your GPUs busy and reduce costs. GPU-accelerated functions integrate with the same 200+ AWS event sources as other Event Functions, so you can add GPU compute as another step in your serverless application. Running GPU workloads today requires customers to provision hardware, manage driver and framework dependencies, and build custom scaling and capacity management. With this launch, you can go from code to a running GPU workload in minutes. Lambda provides GPU base images preconfigured with frameworks

title: Amazon CloudFront Announces WebSocket and gRPC Support for Origin Mutual TLS
summary: Amazon CloudFront (CF) now supports WebSocket and gRPC traffic to application origins in AWS regions, with mutual TLS authentication between CF and the application origin (origin mTLS). Customers can now use TLS certificates to authenticate requests from CloudFront while setting up WebSocket or gRPC connections to their origins. Origin mTLS protects internet facing applications that need persistent, bidirectional or streaming connections, such as chat platforms, collaborative editing tools or live dashboards from unauthenticated requests. Previously, customers serving WebSocket or gRPC traffic through CloudFront had to use shared secrets or IP allow-lists to identify requests originating from CloudFront. This was operationally complex and did not provide strong authentication. With Origin mTLS, customers can use one TLS based authentication for HTTP, WebSocket and gRPC traffic to an application origin. This works with application origins within AWS such as Application Load Balancer and

title: Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL minor version 8.4.13
summary: Starting today, Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for MySQL supports MySQL minor version 8.4.13, the latest minor released by community MySQL. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by the MySQL community. Learn more about the enhancements in RDS for MySQL 8.4.13 in the Amazon RDS user guide and MySQL 8.4.13 release notes. You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your instances in phases, validating on lower-priority environments before upgrading your most critical ones. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. Learn more about performi

title: Amazon RDS for MySQL now supports MySQL major version 9.7
summary: Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL major version 9.7, the latest Long-Term Support release from MySQL community. Amazon RDS for MySQL 9.7 launches with community MySQL 9.7.4. This launch introduces support for the Replication Applier Metrics component, JSON Duality Views, and Hypergraph Optimizer. The Replication Applier Metrics help you diagnose replication lag by adding two Performance Schema tables that report per-channel applier backlog, throughput, and wait statistics, along with each worker's progress on its current transaction. JSON Duality Views let applications read and write the same relational tables as JSON documents. The Hypergraph Optimizer is an opt-in query optimizer that can improve execution plans for complex, multi-join queries. For more details, refer to the MySQL 9.7.4 release notes and the Amazon RDS for MySQL release notes . You can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments , in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot. Learn

title: Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes reduces price for large hosts
summary: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Hybrid Nodes now has lower pricing for large nodes, capping the billed vCPU per node at 32 vCPU, so you are no longer charged for vCPUs above that per node threshold. Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes lets you use your existing on-premises and edge infrastructure as nodes in Amazon EKS clusters. You can now use your largest servers, including those with GPUs, with Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes at lower cost. With this change, the Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes cost of a large server no longer grows with its vCPU count. At the first pricing tier, a 64 vCPU node now costs 50% less than before, and a 256 vCPU node costs 88% less, as both are now billed only for 32 vCPUs. This makes Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes more cost-effective for large bare-metal and GPU servers running compute-intensive workloads, such as AI/ML training and inference, that must stay on-premises for data residency, latency, or regulatory reasons. The pricing change applies automatically to all new h

title: Amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery
summary: Amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery (PITR), so you can restore the user data in a user pool to an earlier time. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices. Previously, you had to build and maintain your own export and restore process, and restored users received new identifiers and had to reset their passwords. With PITR, you choose a recovery point, preview how many users, groups, multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings, and passkeys the recovery will create, update, or delete, and then start or cancel the recovery. Recovered users keep their identifiers, passwords, MFA settings, and passkeys, so they can sign in without resetting their credentials. For example, if a script deletes or modifies users by mistake, you can restore the user data to the moment before it ran. PITR is enabled automatically for user pools on the Essentials and Plus feature plans at no additional charge. The recovery window is u

title: Amazon RDS now supports fast storage volume initialization
summary: Amazon RDS now initializes storage volumes faster when you perform a point-in-time restore (PITR), create a read replica, or convert a Single-AZ instance to Multi-AZ. Each of these operations creates storage volumes from a snapshot, and the data blocks are downloaded from Amazon S3 before you can access them. With fast storage volume initialization, you get a fully performant DB instance in a predictable amount of time. Previously, the initialization rate varied with your workload and with which blocks were accessed. As there was no dedicated bandwidth, so you could see increased I/O latency and had no way to tell when an instance would reach full performance. Now, each database instance is initialized at up to 4 TiB per hour, across every gp3 and io2 storage volume attached to the instance. If concurrent initialization across your account exceeds the available bandwidth, the remaining blocks initialize on a best-effort basis, so initialization is never slower than today. Your DB insta

title: Amazon CloudFront Functions now supports network calls
summary: Amazon CloudFront Functions can now make network calls and act on the response during a request. CloudFront Functions runs lightweight JavaScript at CloudFront edge locations to customize requests and responses. Previously, if your logic depended on data from another service, you had to use Lambda@Edge or move that logic to your origin. Now your functions can use real-time data to personalize, authenticate, or route requests at the edge, close to your viewers. With the new cf.fetch() method, your functions can call your API endpoints and use the response to decide how to handle each request. For example, you can check an AI agent's permissions and usage budget so that only authorized requests reach your API or MCP server, or send request signals to a security or fraud detection service to block or challenge bad traffic. With cf.beacon() , you can send analytics events in the background without slowing down viewers, even for content served from cache. Both methods take advantage of the

title: AWS Lambda now supports customer-managed runtimes, giving platform teams centralized control over runtime contents and updates
summary: AWS Lambda now supports customer-managed runtimes for Lambda Event Functions (formerly Lambda functions). Customer-managed runtimes are a standalone resource type that fully decouples runtime management from function deployment. Platform teams gain centralized control over the runtime contents, updates, access, and lifecycle, including the ability to push updates to shared components without per-function redeployments. Application teams consume the runtime from their functions in the same way as a Lambda-managed runtime, preserving their familiar developer experience. Many organizations require every function to include approved components, such as SDKs, certificates, and security or monitoring tools. Previously, sharing these through Lambda Layers or container images meant redeploying every function to pick up a change. With customer-managed runtimes, platform teams manage these components in a central runtime, packaged as OCI container images in Amazon ECR and compatible with existin

title: AWS IAM account access manager is now even easier to deploy and use
summary: Deploying and using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) account access manager is now even easier: you can use AWS managed policies to enable and administer it; you can include it in your infrastructure-as-code (IaC) configurations; and its role assignments are integrated in a growing number of third-party identity and entitlement management solutions. Administering workforce access with account access manager requires permissions across several services, including AWS IAM Identity Center, AWS Organizations, AWS KMS, and AWS IAM. Previously, defining administrative access required hand-assembling multi-service IAM policies. The new AWS managed policies enable faster ramp up with broadly scoped job-aligned permissions for: 1/ Full administrator (AWSAccountAccessManagerAdministrator) - used to enable and manage account access manager in the AWS organization management account and to map users/groups to IAM roles; 2/ Entitlement Manager (AWSAccountAccessManagerEntitlementManager) - u

title: AWS Deadline Cloud now supports Amazon EC2 G7 instances in service-managed fleets
summary: AWS Deadline Cloud now supports Amazon EC2 G7 instances in service-managed fleets. Deadline Cloud is a fully managed service that helps teams run compute-intensive workloads for visual effects, animation, product design, simulation, and gaming. G7 instances give customers more options to scale GPU capacity quickly. You can add G7 instances to your service-managed fleets in sizes from g7.2xlarge to g7.48xlarge, with On-Demand or Spot pricing on Linux or Windows workers. This lets you scale GPU rendering capacity to match your production schedule without managing your own render farm infrastructure. To get started, create or update a service-managed fleet in the Deadline Cloud console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs, and select the RTX PRO 4500 GPU accelerator. G7 instances are available in the US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), and Asia Pacific (Sydney) Regions. To learn more, see Use a GPU accelerator in the AWS Deadline Cloud User Guide

title: AWS Control Tower now supports existing Amazon S3 bucket for log delivery
summary: AWS Control Tower now lets you use an existing Amazon S3 bucket in your landing zone to store AWS Config and AWS CloudTrail logs. Previously, AWS Control Tower required you to use the Amazon S3 bucket it creates and manages for log storage. Now, customers who want full control of bucket policies, lifecycle rules, and logging infrastructure can consolidate centralized logs in an Amazon S3 bucket they already manage. You can use your own Amazon S3 bucket for both AWS Config and AWS CloudTrail, giving you full control of bucket policies, lifecycle rules, and logging infrastructure. You can switch between self-managed and AWS Control Tower managed buckets at any time, and your Amazon S3 buckets are preserved during landing zone updates, resets, and decommissioning. The bucket must be owned by an AWS account in your organization, be located in your AWS Control Tower home Region, and be preconfigured with the bucket policy that AWS Control Tower requires. This feature is supported in landing

title: Amazon ElastiCache now supports distributed KV caching for self-hosted LLM inference
summary: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now offers fully managed distributed KV caching, a new capability that reduces self-hosted large language model (LLM) inference costs by up to 40% and time to first token (TTFT) by up to 80%. Customers who self-host LLMs pay for redundant GPU work because small, isolated caches on each server can't hold or share the growing context AI agents and chat applications resend. Distributed KV caching extends GPU-local caches with a shared tier so any server can reuse KV state for days across sessions, routing shifts, and server failures. GPUs can fetch cached KV state in milliseconds to serve more requests and respond faster. Distributed KV caching runs on cache.i8ge.48xlarge nodes in the same Availability Zone as the GPU fleet and connects to GPUs through Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). title: Amazon CloudWatch simplifies network performance monitoring for your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
summary: Amazon CloudWatch Network Monitoring now allows you to monitor the health of the AWS network paths that your workloads take by using performance monitors. Performance monitors provide near real-time visibility into whether the AWS network is healthy for your workloads, without installing any software. Performance monitors report per-path metrics such as latency, a network impact score that shows network health, and traffic volume across all flows in your VPCs. You simply select the VPCs you want to monitor, and metrics are available within minutes. Using telemetry AWS already collects, with no additional services to enable, performance monitors determine the paths your traffic takes, within and across Availability Zones, across AWS Regions, and to AWS services, for TCP, UDP, and ICMP traffic. They then score each path by comparing it with its own recent history and with all other paths AWS measures at the same time. For example, a path that suddenly degrades, or degrades with many othe

title: Amazon Braket adds PAUSED device status
summary: Amazon Braket now offers a new device status, PAUSED, to give customers clear and actionable information on when they can submit quantum tasks and hybrid jobs and when those tasks and jobs will run. Device status now tells you: ONLINE: The device is accepting quantum tasks and hybrid jobs and is actively processing them during its availability window. (New) PAUSED: The device is accepting quantum tasks and hybrid jobs but isn't processing them right now, because it is outside its availability window, in short-term maintenance, or in a reservation. Tasks and jobs you submit stay QUEUED and run once the device is ONLINE. OFFLINE: The device is unavailable and isn't accepting new quantum tasks or hybrid jobs, for example due to scheduled maintenance, upgrades, or operational issues. RETIRED: The device has been permanently decommissioned and is no longer available on Amazon Braket. title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports audit logging
summary: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports database-internal audit logging, a fully managed capability that captures SQL statements executed on your cluster. Previously, AWS CloudTrail recorded who connected to a DSQL cluster, but not what they did once inside it. Now, financial institutions and regulated enterprises can meet production compliance requirements by capturing DDL, DML, DCL, and SELECT statements with full statement text, bind parameters, acting principal (both PostgreSQL role and AWS IAM identity), timestamp, table name, and transaction identifier. With audit logging, you can feed SIEM systems directly from Amazon S3, satisfy auditor requirements for change accountability, and reconstruct events after security incidents. Logs are delivered as structured JSON to your S3 bucket via CloudWatch Vended Logs. Configuration requires a single SQL setting—no extension to load and no log-shipping pipeline to build. Audit logging is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL is available.

title: Amazon S3 Replication adds exclusions and Multi-Region key resolution
summary: You can now replicate data in Amazon S3 buckets with fewer replication rules using two new S3 Replication capabilities, exclusions and Multi-Region key resolution. Buckets that many tenants or applications share often need many rules to skip certain data or to match encryption keys in each AWS Region. With these capabilities, customers who manage multi-tenant and shared buckets can replace many replication rules with a single rule. With exclusions, you can replicate an entire bucket while skipping specific prefixes or tagged objects, such as logs or experimental data. With Multi-Region key resolution, S3 Replication encrypts each replica with the matching AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) Multi-Region key in the destination Region, so replicas meet the same encryption requirements as their source objects. For example, a bucket that stores data for hundreds of tenants, each with its own Multi-Region key, can replicate with a single rule, including tenants you add later. Exclusions an

title: AgentCore runtime instances now support privileged mode
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances now support privileged mode, which lets your agents install system-level software and run nested containers. Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. You turn on privileged mode when you create or update an agent runtime that runs on runtime instances. For example, a coding agent can start its service dependencies, such as Postgres and Redis, as containers and run its integration tests against them. A code-modernization agent can install the compilers and libraries that a migration needs. A session that runs a privileged agent runs only that agent, so elevated privileges stay with one agent on its instance. Agents that don't use privileged mode keep the default standard mode, so existing agents don't change. Standard mode suits most agents. Use privileged mode only if your agent needs to install system-level software or run containers. Privilege

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports higher pod density on EKS-orchestrated clusters
summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports higher pod density per node on EKS-orchestrated clusters, allowing you to get more out of every instance. This leaves more room for your applications alongside system DaemonSets for monitoring, logging, and security, and helps increase GPU, CPU and memory utilization on nodes, allowing you to run the same work using fewer instances. As you schedule more pods, the Amazon VPC CNI automatically adds network capacity to the node. Autoscaling with Karpenter also supports the higher pod capacity, so new nodes take on more pods as your cluster scales out. Here are a few examples of workloads that benefit from higher pod density: Model inference - Serve more model replicas or more models from each GPU instance, including on smaller types such as ml.g5 and ml.g6. title: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications adds support for smart card redirection
summary: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications now supports smart card redirection on single-session and multi-session fleets, so users can access the smart card connected to their local device from applications inside their streaming session. It also extends smart card sign-in, previously limited to single-session fleets, to multi-session fleets. This launch helps public sector, healthcare, and other regulated organizations that use Common Access Card (CAC) or Personal Identity Verification (PIV) cards run those workflows on multi-session fleets. Administrators can turn smart card sign-in for Active Directory and smart card redirection on or off independently for each stack. Smart card sign-in lets users sign in to domain-joined streaming instances with their smart card instead of a password, while redirected smart cards support in-session authentication, digital signing, and email encryption. For example, a government agency can move CAC users from single-session to multi-session fleets and keep CAC

title: Amazon EMR Serverless introduces Flex execution
summary: Amazon EMR Serverless now supports Flex execution, a new option that reduces the cost of non-urgent Spark batch jobs by up to 60% by running them on spare compute capacity. With Flex, you enable a single configuration when submitting a job, with no changes to Spark scripts or job definitions. Flex execution is designed for workloads that have flexible completion requirements, such as nightly batch ETL, backfill jobs, and development or testing pipelines. Start and execution times of Flex jobs vary because spare compute resources may not always be available immediately and may be reclaimed during execution. To reduce the likelihood and impact of interruptions, EMR Serverless spans availability zones, diversifies across instance types, places the Spark driver on dedicated capacity to protect job state, and retries interrupted tasks through Spark's built-in fault tolerance. You can also use Flex execution with Serverless Storage to offload shuffle data, adding another layer of resilience

title: Introducing the Apache Spark Optimization Agent for Amazon EMR Serverless
summary: Amazon EMR Serverless now offers the Apache Spark optimization agent, which analyzes completed Spark job runs and delivers cost and performance optimization recommendations in seconds. You can select a cost or performance goal, and the agent returns specific configuration changes with the telemetry evidence and plain-language reasoning behind each suggestion. The agent can analyze a single run or compare it against a known-good baseline to pinpoint what changed. You access it from the EMR Serverless console or through the SageMaker Unified Studio MCP Server. The agent takes the job's configuration, logs, and Spark telemetry together with your chosen intent and returns recommendations computed by a deterministic recommendation engine. The engine reads all job artifacts together to identify what is driving runtime and cost: too little parallelism, a skewed join key, memory pressure forcing spill, idle executors, or capacity provisioned beyond what the job uses. title: Amazon EMR 8.2 is now available
summary: Amazon EMR 8.2 is now available with new features across Amazon EMR on EC2, Amazon EMR on EKS, and Amazon EMR Serverless. This release upgrades Apache Spark to 4.1.3, Apache Iceberg to 1.11.0, and Delta Lake to 4.2.0, and it is designated a Long Term Support (LTS) release. This release makes it easier to run secure, governed analytics at scale — you can now write to the same Delta Lake table on Amazon S3 from multiple clusters concurrently, refresh Iceberg materialized views incrementally, and propagate end-user identity from Spark jobs and interactive sessions all the way to AWS Lake Formation and Amazon S3 so access is authorized and audited as the original user. Amazon EMR 8.2 expands governance and performance across all three deployment options. C8ine instances offer up to 2.5 times higher packet performance per vCPU versus prior generation network optimized instances, providing up to 2x higher network throughput for traffic going through Internet gateways compared to existing C6in network optimized instances. C8ine instances are designed for security and network virtual appliances, including virtual firewalls, load balancers, and Telco 5G UPF workloads. Amazon EC2 C8gn instances feature the latest 6th generation AWS Nitro Cards, and offer up to 600 Gbps network bandwidth, the highest network bandwidth among network optimized EC2 instances. Take advantage of the enhanced networking capabilities of C8gn to scale performance and throughput, while optimizing the cost of running network-intensive workloads such as network virtual appliances, data analytics, CPU-based artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) inference. For increased scalability, C8gn instances offer instance sizes up to 48xlarge, up to 384 GiB of memory, and up to 120 Gbps of bandwidth to Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS). Teams that run proxy services to route container pulls across Regions, a common pattern for optimizing latency or availability, previously had to request, refresh, and coordinate a separate token for every Region behind the proxy. summary: Today, AWS Security Hub adds installed software and resource usage as signals for resource criticality, which indicates how important a resource is to your business. Security Hub uses criticality to rank exposure findings, so that central security teams can prioritize the exposures that affect their most important resources. Security Hub already infers criticality from resource tags and names, but inconsistently tagged resources often have an Unknown criticality, which makes their exposures harder to prioritize. With installed software and resource usage as additional signals, more of your resources receive a meaningful criticality with no tagging or configuration required. For example, an EC2 instance that runs a database engine and serves steady traffic receives a higher criticality than an instance that runs only monitoring agents and sits idle. title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now supports short-term memory retention of up to 10 years
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now lets you keep short-term memory events for up to 10 years, up from one year. Developers can now use short-term memory as a long-lived record of agent conversations and interactions. This helps when that history needs to stay available for a long time, such as for compliance and audit, for users who come back after months away, or for agents that need to look back at past sessions. You set retention on the memory resource, and it's applied to each event when the event is created, so existing events keep their original retention. Standard short-term memory storage charges apply for as long as you keep the data. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where AgentCore Memory is available. To get started, see the AgentCore Memory documentation .

summary: Amazon API Gateway now offers a native JWT authorizer for REST APIs, a new authorizer type that validates JSON Web Tokens directly in the gateway. Until now, validating tokens from an OpenID Connect or OAuth 2.0 identity provider other than Amazon Cognito required a Lambda authorizer. You now configure token validation instead of writing and operating code for it. You can define one or more issuers, the audiences accepted for each, the signing algorithms you permit, and any additional claims a token may present. API Gateway verifies each token's signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and claims on every request. You can attach one authorizer to many methods and require different scopes on each. This fits machine-to-machine APIs, mobile and web backends, and multi-tenant APIs that accept tokens from several identity providers. title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now provides full session summaries
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now keeps a full session summary for every session. It's a single record that gives a snapshot of what happened in the conversation. Summary chunks cover the conversation in more detail, while the full session summary captures the overall picture of where the session stands. AgentCore Memory updates it as new events arrive, so it always reflects the session so far. This works well for developers who want a quick recap rather than a play-by-play. Full session summaries come with the summary strategy and need no extra setup. Every memory that has a summary strategy gets them automatically, including existing sessions. Each summary is stored as a long-term memory record next to the session's summary chunks. You retrieve it with the Memory operations you already use, and you can filter by record type to return only full session summaries. title: AWS Lambda now supports scale to and from zero for Lambda Managed Instances
summary: AWS Lambda now supports scale to and from zero for Event Functions running on Lambda Managed Instances (LMI). Lambda automatically scales execution environments for your function to zero during idle periods and scales them back up when requests arrive, without requiring you to provision minimum capacity. This makes LMI cost-effective for intermittent workloads such as asynchronous processing, development, and test environments. Lambda Managed Instances lets you run Lambda functions on your Amazon EC2 instances while maintaining the operational simplicity of Lambda. With Lambda Managed Instances, you can access specialized compute configurations and drive cost efficiency through EC2 pricing advantages, without managing infrastructure. Previously, customers needed to keep a minimum number of execution environments running even when there was no traffic. title: Amazon SageMaker now supports AI data preparation capabilities to build high-quality datasets for model development
summary: Building high-quality training datasets has traditionally required weeks of manual labeling and data cleaning. Amazon SageMaker now offers AI data preparation capabilities that help data scientists and ML engineers build high-quality training and evaluation datasets for both text-based model customization and traditional ML. Teams can generate synthetic examples grounded in their own documents, auto-label records at scale with confidence scores, incorporate expert feedback through human review, evaluate data quality, and transform data for their chosen training or evaluation technique. Synthetic data generation creates training, evaluation, and test data from a specification grounded in your documents. Auto-labeling labels data at scale with built-in task types including classification, named entity recognition, extractive question answering, ordinal rating, and summarization, plus custom tasks. Rows below your confidence threshold go to a human review queue in the Label Studio Communi

title: Amazon Cognito now supports authentication level and method token claims
summary: Amazon Cognito now supports authentication context class reference (ACR) and authentication methods reference (AMR), by adding ACR and AMR claims to access, ID, and refresh tokens. Your application can use the authentication level (ACR) to make authorization decisions, such as requiring additional factors for sensitive operations. It can also use completed methods (AMR), such as time-based one-time password (TOTP), for auditing and compliance. Amazon Cognito defines four authentication levels based on the factors a user completes, from password-only (level 1) to a password with a TOTP (level 4). Each token reflects the level achieved during sign-in, so your application can make authorization decisions based on how a user authenticated. If your application requires a stronger level, you can request a target level in your application's sign-in flow or through managed login, and Amazon Cognito issues new tokens once the user completes the required factors. You can also customize ACR level

title: Amazon DynamoDB caching is now available with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey
summary: Today, AWS announces the general availability of DynamoDB caching with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey, a serverless alternative to Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) that delivers sub-millisecond read latency for frequently accessed DynamoDB data. Previously, if you needed faster reads than the single-digit millisecond latency of DynamoDB, you had to provision and scale DAX nodes or run your own cache and keep it in sync with DynamoDB. Now you can access DynamoDB table data from a write-through cache that updates as data changes and scales automatically to meet changing workload demands, with no clusters or nodes to manage. DynamoDB caching requires no application logic changes and minimal configuration. You choose which DynamoDB tables and APIs to cache and how long to retain cached data. Your application's IAM credentials are used to access DynamoDB, so existing access control policies are automatically applied. DynamoDB caching is available in all commercial and AWS GovClou

title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports ingest pipelines
summary: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports ingest pipelines, so you can clean, enrich, and vectorize documents inside your collection as they are indexed, without running separate preprocessing infrastructure. Teams building search, log analytics, and generative AI applications can replace data-prep code in Lambda functions or ETL jobs with transformations that apply consistently to every document, regardless of how it is ingested. You can use ingest pipelines to normalize and clean data with processors such as copy, date, dot_expander, join, lowercase, uppercase, remove, rename, set, and trim. For semantic and AI search, you can chunk long text with text_chunking and generate embeddings at ingest time with text_embedding, text_image_embedding, and sparse_encoding. The ml_inference processor calls any model you have connected and lets you map its input and output fields yourself. You create and manage pipelines with the familiar OpenSearch _ingest/pipeline APIs. You can test a pipeline

title: Amazon OpenSearch UI is now available in the Africa (Cape Town) Region
summary: Amazon OpenSearch UI has expanded to the AWS Africa (Cape Town) Region, bringing availability to 25 AWS Regions. OpenSearch UI provides a single endpoint to query, visualize, and analyze data across Amazon OpenSearch Service domains running OpenSearch version 1.3 or later and OpenSearch Serverless collections, including Classic and NextGen. One OpenSearch UI application can connect to multiple domains and collections. Workspaces organize dashboards, saved queries, and other content, with purpose-built experiences for observability, security analytics, and search. The Discover interface supports multiple data sources and query languages, including Piped Processing Language (PPL) and SQL. It also includes a data selector, query autocomplete, and an updated design. OpenSearch UI runs separately from your domains and collections, giving you access to the latest UI capabilities without requiring cluster upgrades.
