title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports batch actions on up to 100 cases at once
summary: Cases in Amazon Connect Customer now lets agents and supervisors assign, comment on, and update the status of up to 100 cases at once, so teams spend less time on repetitive case updates. When one issue affects many customers, such as a shipping delay or a service outage, teams no longer need to update each case one at a time. Agents and supervisors with the appropriate permissions can select the related cases and change the assignee, add a comment, or close them in a single action. Developers can also use batch APIs to make the same updates programmatically. Cases is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .

title: The next generation AgentCore runtime is now the default
summary: Starting today, new runtimes in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore use the next generation of AgentCore runtime by default. The new runtime restores each session from a snapshot of your initialized agent, scales compute and memory with the work, and scales idle agents to zero. Every session still runs in its own hardware-isolated Firecracker microVM. Your agents can run heavy work like compiling a large codebase, driving a browser, or loading a local model inside the session. Sessions scale to 8 vCPU and 32 GB of memory and support container images up to 10 GB. On a 2 GB image, sessions start in under 2 seconds at P75, down from 29.7 seconds on the previous generation. Idle agents scale to zero, and memory is reclaimed within minutes of release. For multi-turn agents, that means up to 68% less billed memory per session. Existing runtimes stay on the current version until you move them. To move an existing runtime, or to use the next generation in a Region where it isn't the default yet, set plat

title: Ornith-1.0-9B and Ornith-1.0-35B models now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
summary: DeepReinforce AI's Ornith-1.0-9B and Ornith-1.0-35B models are now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, expanding the portfolio of foundation models available to AWS customers. These two models are part of the Ornith 1.0 family of open-source, self-scaffolding agentic coding models released under the MIT license, achieving state-of-the-art performance among open-source models of comparable size on coding benchmarks such as Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE-Bench, NL2Repo, and OpenClaw. These models address different agentic coding challenges with specialized capabilities: Ornith-1.0-9B is a lightweight 9B-parameter dense model post-trained on Qwen 3.5 9B, designed for efficient single-GPU deployment. With a 256K-token context window and 32 decoder layers, it is well-suited for individual developers and small teams running agentic coding workflows on a single GPU — including laptops with consumer-grade hardware. Its self-improving training framework uses reinforcement learning to jointly opti

title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless supports intelligent ingestion for time series collection
summary: The next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports intelligent ingestion for time series collections. You can bring logs and event data from Amazon S3 into a time series collection without operating an ingestion pipeline. With intelligent ingestion, you can now complete the setup and get data ingested with a few clicks in the AWS Management Console or with a single API call. Intelligent ingestion detects the data type, parses each record, and indexes it into your collection. It works with observability logs in JSON, NDJSON, and JSON arrays. Use an ingestion job for one-time loads, use an ingestion stream to keep the collection up to date as new objects arrive in S3, or backfill and then stream. Source buckets can be in the same AWS account as the collection or in a different one. Capacity scales with your workload up to the collection's configured limit, and you pay only for active processing. Once ingested, your data gets everything time series collections already provid

title: Amazon EKS Provisioned Control Plane now offers a 24 GB etcd database on 4XL and 8XL tiers
summary: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) now offers a larger 24 GB etcd database, up from 16 GB, for 4XL and 8XL Provisioned Control Plane clusters. etcd is the key-value store in the Kubernetes control plane that holds your cluster state, so its size limits how many Kubernetes objects your cluster can store. With 50% more capacity, you can run bigger clusters with more pods, jobs, events, and custom resources. The larger database gives more headroom to workloads that create and update many Kubernetes objects, such as large-scale AI/ML training and inference, batch processing, and CI/CD pipelines. When the etcd database fills up, you can’t add or change objects in your cluster, so the extra headroom helps keep these workloads running as they scale. To get the larger database, choose the 4XL or 8XL tier of Provisioned Control Plane on a cluster running EKS version 1.34 or later. Existing clusters on the 4XL and 8XL tiers running these versions get the larger database automatically

title: Amazon Cognito now supports user pool session management
summary: Amazon Cognito now supports session management for user pools, giving you visibility into and control over the sessions your users establish when they sign in to your applications. Single sign-on (SSO) sessions are created when a user signs in through managed login and let them access other app clients without re-authenticating. Token sessions are created when a user signs in to an app client and receives tokens. Session management lets you list a user's active SSO and token sessions across all devices and app clients and revoke any of them on demand. You can also now configure how long each app client reuses an SSO session before requiring re-authentication, instead of the previous fixed one-hour duration. Each session includes details such as session type, app client ID, device type, last activity time and location, and initial sign-in time, so you can build your own end-user or admin session experiences. You can revoke an individual session, optionally with its linked sessions, or u

title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports the x86 CPU architecture
summary: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports the x86 CPU architecture, so you can run your existing x86 applications, tools, and software dependencies without recompiling or porting them. When you create a MicroVM image, you can now choose between x86 and Arm (AWS Graviton) to give each user or job an isolated MicroVM on the architecture your workload uses. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume, and state preservation for running user or AI-generated code, in applications such as AI coding assistants, CI/CD runners, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. Today’s launch enables you to run x86-based workloads on Lambda MicroVMs as-is. title: Amazon OpenSearch Service announces managed cross-Region disaster recovery

Managed disaster recovery delivers a recovery point objective (RPO) of under one minute and a recovery time objective (RTO) of under 20 minutes. Read-view objects can now be reused which eliminates the global mutex on closure. The error log now reports warnings when the history-list length (HLL) crosses innodb_max_purge_lag and when purge lag begins delaying DML, so you can detect purge backlogs before they affect performance. summary: Amazon S3 Access Grants can now discover and list all your grants across multiple AWS accounts with a single API call, eliminating the need to query each account separately. A single ListCallerAccessGrants call returns grants from your own S3 Access Grants instance and every instance shared with you, giving you a complete view of the S3 data you can access. By setting the new InstanceScope parameter to ALL in your ListCallerAccessGrants request, S3 Access Grants queries every instance shared with you through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) and returns all the grants in one combined response, each identifying the account that owns it. summary: Eligible customers can now access OpenAI’s specialized cybersecurity models Daybreak Red: GPT-5.6 Cyber and Daybreak Blue: GPT-5.6 Sol through the bedrock-runtime endpoint on Amazon Bedrock. Daybreak Red is designed for advanced, authorized tasks such as vulnerability research, exploit reproduction, and mitigation development. AWS Network Firewall is a managed network security service that protects your Amazon VPCs with access control and threat detection. The new policy model strengthens your security posture by layering firewall and IPS protections instead of combining them, which also makes policies easier to manage. You author firewall rules that enforce deny-by-default access control, such as allowing traffic only to approved domains. For IPS rules, you can use managed rule groups from AWS or AWS Marketplace partners, which update automatically as new threats emerge. You can also create your own custom IPS rule groups. When a free trial ends, the buyer's subscription continues at the seller's usage-based pricing, so buyers pay only for what they use after the trial. This helps sellers turn more trial users into paying customers. Buyers get a simple way to evaluate software before they buy, with no new subscription and no interruption in access. Sellers can offer a free trial of 7 to 90 days that converts to a paid subscription at the price they set. Buyers see the trial length, conversion date, and pricing before they subscribe. They receive reminder emails before the trial converts and can cancel at any time before conversion at no charge. summary: Amazon CloudWatch now offers accelerated compute insights, a capability that provides monitoring and observability for self-hosted AI inference workloads running in Amazon EKS clusters. Previously, platform and AI teams lacked fleet-level visibility into their accelerators, whether workloads were running efficiently, and what was causing performance issues. Accelerated compute insights collects telemetry from across the inference stack to help teams identify idle accelerators, optimize workloads to reduce costs, and troubleshoot common inference issues such as high time to first token. Getting started is as simple as enabling the Amazon CloudWatch Observability add-on for Amazon EKS, which discovers every NVIDIA GPU in the cluster automatically. Each record captures the requester, operation, table name, namespace, response status, and request timing, using the same space-delimited format as S3 server access logs for general purpose buckets. While the primary cluster keeps serving your workload, you can run the same search queries on both clusters and compare their performance using Amazon CloudWatch metrics. After you finish validating, you can cut over to the cloned cluster. If you keep the previous version for a retention period you choose, you can roll back to it at any time during that period. You can see the amortized cost of each instance launched into a Capacity Block and the amortized cost of unused capacity, so you can attribute your upfront fee to the workloads that used it and identify capacity that went unused. Previously, a Capacity Block's upfront fee appeared as a single charge on the purchase date, making it difficult to see how that cost was spread across usage over the reservation. Now the amortized cost appears alongside your instance usage, so you can allocate GPU costs to the teams, projects, and applications that ran on the reserved capacity. You can also see what share of your reservation went unused and plan future Capacity Block purchases. summary: Starting today, you can add Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML and interruptible Capacity Reservations to Capacity Reservation Resource Groups in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Amazon EC2 offers different reservation offerings such as On-Demand Capacity Reservations (ODCRs), interruptible Capacity Reservations, and Capacity Blocks for ML. Now you can add any type of Capacity Reservation to a Capacity Reservation Resource Group, making it easier to launch EC2 instances across your entire portfolio of reserved capacity. summary: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports external catalog's vended credentials in Apache Iceberg REST catalog federation. You can now read external Iceberg tables from Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, Amazon Redshift, and AWS Glue using coarse-grained table grants in your external Iceberg catalog. Glue Data Catalog already federates to external Iceberg REST catalogs through an AWS IAM role that you configure with access to your Amazon S3 buckets. This enhancement in Glue Data Catalog provides another way to connect to an external Iceberg catalog and read only the tables that the external catalog authorizes. It uses temporary security credentials that are scoped to the Amazon S3 storage prefix and vended by your external Iceberg catalog. AWS Lake Formation manages access control when you query an external table using any AWS analytics engine, letting you restrict access further down to specific rows and columns and share external Iceberg tables across AWS accounts. Customers can now use these new Regions to leverage Amazon SES to send emails and, if needed, to help manage data requirements. Amazon SES is a scalable, cost-effective, and flexible cloud-based email service that allows digital marketers and application developers to send marketing, notification, and transactional emails from within any application. title: AWS Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory for your compute resources
summary: Today, AWS announces that AWS Security Hub now provides a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) inventory, giving central security teams a continuously updated, organization-wide view of the software packages and applications installed on their compute resources. Security Hub builds the inventory from the SBOMs that Amazon Inspector generates for Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon ECR container images, and AWS Lambda functions, with no additional configuration. The SBOM page lists each package with its version, type, and the number of resources where it is installed. You can filter and group the list by package attributes, account, and region. On the resource detail page, the Installed software tab lists every package on that resource, so you can judge its function and criticality while triaging any finding. title: Announcing Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
summary: Today, we are announcing the general availability of Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Web Answer is a managed tool that returns a synthesized, grounded, cited answer to a natural-language question in a single call, so agent builders can attach it to an agent and get back a finished answer grounded in current web sources, without building and maintaining their own search, retrieve, synthesis, and citation pipeline. Web Answer builds on Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which launched in June, extending it from "find the web content" to "return the finished answer," a capability customers have been asking for. With Web Answer, your agent sends a question and receives a synthesized cited answer in one tool call. Web Answer works like an agent; it plans its own searches, runs several in parallel, and decides when it has gathered enough evidence to answer. You stay in control of the boundaries, with domain include, deny lists and publish-date filters that scope where it looks.

title: Amazon DynamoDB now supports bulk put items
summary: Today, AWS announces the general availability of bulk put items for Amazon DynamoDB, a fully managed feature that writes data from Amazon S3 into your existing DynamoDB tables. Many DynamoDB applications use data that other systems produce and store in Amazon S3. Writing this data into existing DynamoDB tables has typically meant building custom pipelines and managing table capacity. With bulk put items, developers and data engineers can write this data without impacting existing workloads or building a custom ingestion pipeline, in a cost-efficient way. You point bulk put items at the S3 location of your input files, and DynamoDB handles the rest. Each item supports its own condition expression, so you can enforce insert-only or version-guarded writes. The Standard tier fits most workloads, and the Accelerated tier is for more time-sensitive workloads. Common use cases include daily refreshes, large catalog enrichments, backfills, and migrations. title: Amazon Cognito announces 99.99% Service Level Agreement for the Plus feature plan
summary: Starting November 1, 2026, the Amazon Cognito Service Level Agreement (SLA) commits to a Monthly Uptime Percentage of 99.99% for user pools on the Plus feature plan, up from 99.9%. User pools already on Plus are automatically covered by the new Service Commitment. User pools on Essentials and Lite stay at the 99.9% Service Commitment with no change to their terms. To qualify for the 99.99% Service Commitment, you can switch a user pool to the Plus feature plan using the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS Software Development Kits (SDKs). The Plus feature plan also includes threat protection features such as adaptive authentication, compromised credentials detection, and threat and user activity logging and export. For full terms and exclusions, see the Amazon Cognito SLA . To learn more about feature plans, see user pool feature plans .

title: IAM Roles Anywhere now supports automatic certificate revocation checking
summary: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles Anywhere now supports automatic revocation checking using certificate revocation list (CRL) distribution points (CDPs). This helps keep revocation checks in sync with your certificate authority (CA) and can help improve your security posture. When you enable this capability on a trust anchor, IAM Roles Anywhere reads the CDP URLs embedded in authenticating certificates, downloads the corresponding CRLs, and denies credential requests that use revoked certificates. Previously, to check revocation status, you had to import CRLs into IAM Roles Anywhere and re-import them each time your CA published an update, which added operational overhead. With this launch, IAM Roles Anywhere downloads CRLs from your CDPs and refreshes them periodically, so you no longer need to re-import them. You can use this capability with AWS Private Certificate Authority or your own public key infrastructure (PKI), provided your certificates include publicly accessib

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service optimized engine now supports agent traces
summary: Today, the Amazon OpenSearch Service optimized engine adds support for agent traces, including OpenTelemetry traces. Your traces and logs now live in the same place. You can follow a request or an agent session from start to finish, find the step that failed or slowed down, and check the related logs without switching tools. The optimized engine maps OpenTelemetry logs and traces to object, nested, and flat object fields, with support for multi-valued arrays. Span events, span links, prompts, and tool calls retain their nested structure, allowing field-level queries without flattening data during ingestion. On hot-tier data, the engine supports update, delete, and upsert operations by document ID. When data arrives late or with errors, you can correct it in place, so your dashboards and alerts work from accurate data. In OpenSearch UI, you can analyze this data with Discover Traces, application performance monitoring, the service map, and the agent traces and sessions views. These feat

title: Amazon FSx for Lustre delivers 16x higher metadata IOPS on Intelligent-Tiering file systems
summary: Amazon FSx for Lustre now supports up to 192,000 metadata I/O operations per second (IOPS) on file systems that use the Intelligent-Tiering storage class, 16x higher than the previous maximum of 12,000 IOPS. The FSx for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering storage class delivers the lowest-cost and only fully elastic Lustre file storage in the cloud. It is optimized for workloads that mix hot and cold data and do not require consistent SSD-level performance. A file system's metadata IOPS determine how many files and directories you can create, list, read, and delete per second. Today's launch allows you to scale to even higher levels of performance, accelerate time-to-results, and optimize your storage costs for metadata-intensive machine learning research and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads. title: AWS Security Hub Network Scanning now available in AWS GovCloud (US)
summary: AWS Security Hub Network Scanning feature is now supported in AWS GovCloud (US). Network Scanning probes your resources from the internet to detect actual reachability, not just what could be reachable based on security group rules and route tables. It discovers public IP addresses, virtual machines, and load balancers across your AWS environments, identifies reachable ports, and determines what services are running behind them. This complements Security Hub's existing network reachability findings, which identify configurations that could make a resource reachable from the internet. Network Scanning confirms that configurations do exist which make a resource reachable from the internet. Each reachable port generates a Security Hub finding with evidence of the port and service discovered. Security Hub Exposures then automatically correlates these findings with other findings and resource configurations to determine broader risk. title: AWS WAF AI traffic monetization now supports fiat payouts through Stripe
summary: AWS WAF AI traffic monetization now integrates with Stripe. Publishers, content owners, and API providers can collect stablecoin payments from AI bots and agents that settle in local currency directly to their Stripe balance. With this launch, customers can monetize agent access without holding stablecoins or managing a crypto wallet. Stripe is now available as a new payout method alongside existing stablecoin payouts. To get started, connect your Stripe account to AWS WAF through Stripe Connect in the AWS WAF console. Your existing pricing and agent policies work unchanged. title: Amazon SageMaker AI Studio Now Supports IAM Identity Center Multi-Region Replication
summary: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports IAM Identity Center (IdC) multi-region replication, enabling you to deploy SageMaker AI Studio domains in different regions from your IdC instance's primary region. Previously, the primary IdC instance had to reside in the same region as the SageMaker AI Studio domain; now customers can replicate their primary IdC instance into the region where they wish to use SageMaker AI Studio domains. This capability helps customers maintain compliance while utilizing centralized workforce identity management. As an Amazon SageMaker AI Studio administrator, you can deploy SageMaker AI domains that align with your workforce's location and data residency requirements, independent of where your primary IdC instance is set up. Now, the AWS assistant provides the same personalized, account-aware guidance and actions with a name that immediately communicates what the product does. With the ImdsV1Enabled metric, you can configure CloudWatch dashboards and alarms to track instances that still allow IMDSv1, identify migration gaps, and prioritize remediation, without building your own tooling to check the metadata options of instances across accounts and Regions. This gives you a reliable, ongoing signal to track and complete your IMDSv2 migration. The ImdsV1Enabled CloudWatch metric is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost. summary: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is now available in the Asia Pacific (Taipei) and Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Regions, adding to the list of available Regions where you can use Amazon DocumentDB. Amazon DocumentDB is a fully managed, native JSON database that makes it simple and cost-effective to operate critical document workloads at virtually any scale without managing infrastructure. Amazon DocumentDB is designed to give you the scalability and durability you need when operating mission-critical MongoDB workloads. title: Amazon Connect Customer now shows associated cases in contact records

Supervisors can now identify the cases associated with an interaction directly on the Contact Details page without searching individual cases. Analysts can access the same information through the DescribeContact API and contact event streams to measure the number of interactions per case. title: Amazon S3 Tables now provide a simple, cost-effective path for data lake modernization
summary: Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of your Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg. Iceberg adds ACID transactions, schema evolution, and time travel to your data lake, but moving off Hive usually means building a migration pipeline for each table, which can take weeks. You can now let S3 Tables manage your migration, resulting in query-ready Iceberg tables that stay optimized as data grows. S3 Tables validate, convert, and copy your data while production workloads keep running. To lower migration risk, you can review each step, sync destination tables with source changes as often as you need, or roll back to your source data. You pay only for the data that the job copies, with no charge for the Hive-to-Iceberg conversion, and source objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering stay in their current access tier. title: Amazon EC2 and VPC now display related resources for all resource types
summary: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC), and AWS Global View now display related resources for all resource types in their consoles. Previously, only security groups had an option to view related resources. Now you can see relationships for all EC2 and VPC resource types, including EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes, Launch Templates, Auto Scaling groups, subnets, route tables, and more. The Related Resources tab has also been moved to the console toolbar for easier access. This capability helps you better understand your infrastructure dependencies and troubleshoot issues more efficiently. For example, when investigating an EC2 instance issue, you can quickly view its associated EBS volumes, security groups, subnets, and route tables without navigating between multiple console pages. title: New features for Amazon EC2 Capacity Manager
summary: Amazon EC2 Capacity Manager now offers real-time supportability checks and capacity fulfillment metrics. Real-time supportability checks help customers find capacity by scoring how well each instance type and Availability Zone can support a request, without launching or reserving instances. Capacity fulfillment metrics show how much capacity was delivered against the amount requested. Global enterprises that run thousands of workloads across hundreds of accounts often spread each one across multiple instance types and Availability Zones, giving Amazon EC2 more options to fulfill each request. Starting today, customers can use the supportability checks in Capacity Manager to understand which Availability Zones and instance types give them the best chance of getting the capacity they need. The check returns a High, Medium, or Low score for each option, plus an overall score. summary: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents pause emails while waiting for information or approvals, freeing them to handle higher-priority contacts and resume their work later. Paused time is tracked separately from active handling time, giving supervisors a more accurate view of the time agents spend working on emails. Agents can pause and resume emails directly from the Agent Workspace or Contact Control Panel (CCP) and see how long each email has been paused. Supervisors can monitor paused emails and pause duration in real time, and use flows to automatically resume or transfer emails that remain paused beyond a configured threshold. summary: Amazon CloudWatch now supports bearer token authentication, using API keys (bearer tokens), as an additional option for sending OpenTelemetry traces to the AWS X-Ray OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) traces endpoint. Any OTLP/HTTP client that can set an Authorization header, including the OpenTelemetry Collector and OpenTelemetry SDK exporters, can now authenticate with a bearer token instead of signing requests with AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4). This helps teams send traces from workloads that can't use the AWS SDK or short-term credentials, such as applications running on premises or in other clouds, CI/CD pipelines, and third-party tools that support only a static Authorization header. SigV4 remains the recommended authentication method for sending traces to CloudWatch, and the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) SDKs continue to use SigV4 by default with no changes required. title: Amazon EKS Capabilities now supports Argo CD Notifications

Previously, RDS snapshot charges were aggregated at the database instance level on the Cost and Usage report as well as the Cost Explorer. This meant that while understanding the snapshot charges, you could only see the aggregate view at the database instance instead of drilling down to each individual snapshot. Customers can now scale processing for Kafka workloads beyond the partition count of a topic, increasing throughput during traffic spikes and improving processing resilience. Customers building event-driven Kafka workloads for use cases such as image and video encoding, fraud detection, notification delivery, and telemetry ingestion treat each event as an independent unit of work, where processing speed matters more than strict ordering. Previously, Kafka ESMs used the Kafka consumer group protocol, which assigns each partition to exactly one consumer within a consumer group. Customers needing higher parallelism had to over-partition topics or move traffic to a separate queuing system, adding infrastructure to operate and producer code to maintain. title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in flows
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to invoke Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools in customer experience flows through the new 'External Tool' block. With this launch, you can connect flows to third-party applications through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and reuse the same tools used by your agentic experiences to retrieve data or trigger actions, without writing custom Lambda functions. For example, when a customer contacts a financial institution about a recent transaction, a flow can use the External Tool block to retrieve relevant context from a third-party application, such as case history from their CRM system, or transaction details from a banking platform. This feature is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). To learn more about this feature, refer to the administrator guide . To

title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Cases and External Tool events in the Wait block
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now supports Cases and External Tool events in the Wait block, giving you more control over how your customer experience flows react to real-time data changes. In addition to waiting for a Lambda function to complete, you can now wait until a Connect Case field meets a specified condition or an External Tool invocation completes. This enables you to wait for critical information before advancing an interaction, reducing unnecessary transfers and saving time for both your end-customers and agents. For example, you can hold a flow until a refund status field is updated on a case, then automatically resume and route the interaction based on the outcome. To learn more about this feature, refer to the administrator guide and availability of Connect Customer features by Region . To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

title: EC2 Amazon Machine Images can now be scanned for vulnerabilities through Amazon Inspector
summary: Amazon Inspector now extends its vulnerability scanning to EC2 Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), enabling you to identify software vulnerabilities in your AMIs without launching instances or installing additional software. This helps you fix issues at the source before AMIs are used to launch instances across your fleet. With this capability, you can run continuous evaluations to monitor your AMI catalog for newly discovered vulnerabilities, or perform targeted one-time scans for specific AMIs directly from the EC2 Console. You can enable AMI scanning for an account or across your entire organization in Amazon Inspector. For AWS Security Hub customers, you can enable AMI scanning as an add-on across your organization, and findings are also delivered to Security Hub. Based on the scan results, you can enable the Allowed AMIs setting and specify security criteria that AMIs must meet to be available within your account and enforce this setting across the entire organization using Declarative

summary: Amazon Textract now provides an updated text detection model that improves accuracy, expands language support, and enhances multilingual table extraction. The updated model applies to the DetectDocumentText and AnalyzeDocument APIs and requires no changes to your Amazon Textract API requests or response schema. Your applications are served by the updated model automatically, so you can continue calling Amazon Textract exactly as before. The updated model expands language coverage to more than 40 languages, including Albanian, Arabic, Basque, Belarusian, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latvian, Lithuanian, Luxembourgish, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Serbian Cyrillic, Serbian Latin, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Turkmen, and Ukrainian, enabling reliable processing of previously unsupporte

title: Amazon Textract now available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich)
summary: Amazon Textract is now available in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich) Regions. Amazon Textract is a machine learning service that automatically extracts text, handwriting, and data from scanned documents, going beyond simple optical character recognition (OCR) to identify and extract text and structured data. At launch in these Regions, Amazon Textract supports text detection and document analysis. This includes the DetectDocumentText, AnalyzeDocument, StartDocumentTextDetection, GetDocumentTextDetection, StartDocumentAnalysis, and GetDocumentAnalysis operations. The AnalyzeExpense, AnalyzeID, and AnalyzeLending operations, and Custom Queries (adapters), are not available in these Regions at this time. With this launch, Amazon Textract is available in a total of 18 AWS Regions: US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe

title: Amazon CloudFront now supports self-service increases in AWS Service Quotas
summary: Amazon CloudFront now supports AWS Service Quotas, so you can view, monitor, and request increases for 28 CloudFront quotas from the Service Quotas console or API. Until now, increasing a quota on resources such as distributions, cache policies, origins, or alternate domain names meant opening a support case and waiting for manual review. If you have AWS Business Support or higher, requests for limit increases within published thresholds are now approved automatically. For example, you can raise your distribution quota from 500 to 1,000, or the number of alternate domain names per distribution from 100 to 500, without opening a support case. Some quotas also publish usage metrics to Amazon CloudWatch every 5 minutes, so you can set alarms and request an increase before you reach a limit.. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon CloudFront is supported. To get started, visit the Service Quotas console to view and request increases for your CloudFront quotas. title: AWS Compute Optimizer now supports additional Amazon EC2 instance types in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
summary: AWS Compute Optimizer now provides rightsizing recommendations for 389 additional Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance types in AWS GovCloud (US-West) and 276 in AWS GovCloud (US-East) Regions. Customers running regulated and government workloads can find the same cost and performance opportunities on current-generation instance types without manual analysis. Compute Optimizer has expanded support to include the latest generation families in every workload category. The additions include Compute Optimized (C7i, C7i-flex, C8g, C8gn), General Purpose (M7i, M7i-flex, M8g, M8gd, M8i, M8i-flex), Memory Optimized (R7i, R8g, R8gd, R8i, R8i-flex), Memory Intensive (X2iedn, X8i), and Storage Optimized (I7i, I7ie, I8g, I8ge) instance types. With this expansion, Compute Optimizer supports 724 instance types across 102 families in AWS GovCloud (US-West) and 542 instance types across 69 families in AWS GovCloud (US-East), in both EC2 instance and EC2 Auto Scaling group recommendations

title: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts
summary: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts, helping agents resume work without losing progress when connectivity is interrupted or when their browser is accidentally closed or refreshed. When agents return, their drafts are restored with the message body, recipients, subject line, and attachment references intact. Customers can also access saved draft data in their Amazon S3 buckets to build integrations with other applications.

title: Amazon CloudFront now provides viewer ISP and post-quantum TLS details
summary: Amazon CloudFront can now forward two new optional headers to your origin. The CloudFront-Viewer-ISP header contains the name of the viewer's internet service provider (ISP), so you can see which network a request came from. The CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details header describes the cryptography used on each viewer's TLS connection, so you can see whether a connection used post-quantum cryptography (PQC). With CloudFront-Viewer-ISP, you can break down traffic and performance by network. You can also isolate unusual traffic from a single provider. CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details includes the key exchange, signature scheme, and signature public key type for each connection. You can use it to measure the share of viewers that actually connect with PQC and identify clients that do not yet do so. To forward either header to your origin, add it to an origin request policy and attach the policy to your distribution. title: Amazon MSK now supports TLS 1.3 for data in transit
service: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
summary: Amazon MSK now supports version 1.3 of Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol for MSK Provisioned clusters through encryption policies. TLS 1.3 delivers faster, more secure encryption for streaming data and is increasingly required by compliance frameworks and enterprise security standards. It is also one of the prerequisites for post-quantum cryptography for protecting data against attacks that collect encrypted traffic now with the intent to decrypt it later. Customers can opt in to TLS 1.3 by selecting a named security policy in their MSK cluster configuration, with no change to existing clusters until a policy is applied. A named security policy defines which TLS version and cipher suites a cluster can accept. With this launch, Amazon MSK provides a set of policies customers can select and any connection that does not meet the selected policy requirements is rejected. This allows customers to stay in control of their security and compliance posture. Policies that support both TLS

title: AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions
summary: AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions. When you enable it, CloudFront adds the script tag for the AWS WAF JavaScript SDK to the HTML it serves, with no change to your application code, build process, or deployment. The SDK supplies the client-side signals used by three AWS WAF managed rule groups: Bot Control at the targeted inspection level, Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP), and Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP). Previously, supplying those signals required you to add a script tag to every page of every application you wanted to protect, and to maintain that tag across releases. For teams running many applications, or serving pages produced by systems they do not control, this created recurring work and a common source of misconfiguration, where a protection was enabled in AWS WAF but the client-side integration was missing. Enabling automatic SDK integration on the web ACL protecting your CloudFront distrib

title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows and flow modules, simplifying how you build, test, and deploy customer experience flows while minimizing impact to live end-customer traffic. With this launch, you can now create immutable versions of a flow and attach one or more friendly names (i.e., aliases) to a version, then point resources such as queues, quick connects, and phone numbers at an alias instead of a specific version. Rolling out a new version takes a single update, with no need to republish or relink each resource. For example, you can publish an updated customer experience flow as a new version and validate it in a test environment while live traffic stays on the current version, then repoint the production alias to move every phone number to the new version in a single update. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more, see Flow versioning and aliasing in the Amazon Connect Customer Admi

title: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics
service: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
summary: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon CloudWatch . The integration collects Kafka exporter metrics and consumer-group lag metrics from your Amazon MSK clusters. Managed Prometheus collectors discover and collect Prometheus metrics from your workloads, so you don't run and operate collection agents yourself. You ingest the collected metrics into an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace or into Amazon CloudWatch, where you query and analyze them. You monitor Kafka stream health and consumer performance with consumer-group metrics. This helps you detect processing bottlenecks in your streaming applications. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where managed Prometheus collectors are generally available. To learn more, see the documentation for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon CloudWatch .

title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports Apache Iceberg table optimization in the US West (N. California) Region
summary: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports automatic table optimization for Apache Iceberg tables in the US West (N. California) Region. Apache Iceberg is an open table format that delivers fast query performance over large tables in data lakes. With this launch, you can enable table optimization for individual tables or for all tables in your Data Catalog. Apache Iceberg tables accumulate small files, snapshots, and unreferenced files with every write, which slows queries and increases storage costs over time. Table optimization continuously monitors your tables to compact small files in the background, remove snapshots that are past your retention settings, and delete unreferenced files that are no longer needed. You can monitor each run from the AWS Glue console, Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and logs. You can enable table optimization using the AWS Glue console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. For the full list of Regions where table optimization is available, see Supported Regions for table optimizers

title: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning for real-time endpoints
summary: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning, enabling you to run several models on a single GPU instead of dedicating a whole accelerator to each one. Using NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, SageMaker AI divides a GPU into as many as seven isolated partitions, each with its own memory and compute. Customers serving small and mid-size models, such as fine-tuned variants, embedding models, rerankers, and classifiers, previously had to give every model an entire accelerator, so an instance hosted no more models than it had GPUs and paid for GPU capacity those models could never use. With GPU partitioning, you choose how to divide the GPUs behind your endpoint and place each model on a partition sized to fit it. Several models then share one accelerator with hardware-enforced isolation, so a busy model cannot take memory or throughput from the models beside it. Right-sizing an accelerator to a workload also opens up newer instance generations that would otherwise

title: Amazon Quick Introduces Quick Essentials
summary: Amazon Quick introduces Quick Essentials for enterprises. The plan makes it easier for organizations to get started with all the features of Quick such as AI-powered chat, Research, Flows, and Apps, and lets users view and interact with Quick Sight dashboards and reports and then manage adoption at the desired pace. In AWS Regions where Amazon Quick is available, Quick Sight Reader users are upgraded to Quick Essentials at no additional per-user cost. With Quick Essentials, Quick Sight Readers can ask their dashboards questions in plain language, like what drove a revenue dip in March, and dig into the details with follow-up questions. They can turn the answer into a document, presentation, or spreadsheet for their team. When they need more context, Research pulls from their data, files, and the web into a detailed report with citations. If they need the same update every week, Flows can build it and send it automatically. When they need a tool that doesn't exist yet, like a request tr

title: AWS Marketplace now enables partners to list once and sell through multiple subsidiary accounts
summary: Today, AWS announces that AWS partners who operate multiple legal entities can publish a product listing once in their primary account and enable their local subsidiaries to sell it through direct private offers — eliminating the need to recreate and maintain duplicate listings across every account. From the primary account, which retains ownership of the listing, partners authorize which products each subsidiary can sell and which buyer countries it can extend private offers to. Each subsidiary transacts under its own local tax identity, selects the local currencies it supports, and sets its own disbursement preferences and bank account. The AWS Marketplace insights report in the primary account provides a consolidated view of offers, agreements, and renewals across all connected subsidiary accounts. title: Amazon Aurora now supports post-quantum TLS key exchange
summary: Starting today, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in transit. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18 and higher support modification of the ssl_groups parameter. You can select cryptographic groups from the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL allow list to align with your organization's security standards. Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full PostgreSQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at our getting started page .

title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports updating connector plugins and worker configurations
service: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
summary: Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now lets you update the custom plugin and worker configuration of an existing connector. This is useful when you need to update the custom plugin to run a new version of your connector code, for example one with updated dependencies. You can also update the worker configuration to change worker-level settings, such as switching key and value converters or tuning producer and consumer properties for throughput and latency. Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, updating a connector's plugin or worker configuration meant deleting the connector and recreating it - a disruptive operation that added risk and operational overhead. With this launch, you can update a connector's plugin and worker configuration in place. The connector keeps its committed offsets, so its tasks

title: AWS Step Functions workflows now available as AI agent tools
summary: You can now use your AWS Step Functions workflows as tools for AI agents through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. Your agent decides when to run a workflow and what input to pass, and Step Functions runs each step exactly as you defined it. Agents can use your existing Standard and Express workflows as tools. AWS Step Functions is a visual workflow service capable of orchestrating over 220 AWS services to help customers build distributed applications at scale. AgentCore Gateway connects AI agents to tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). With this launch, your agents can run multi-step business processes in the same order every time. For example, a customer support agent can start your refund workflow, and Step Functions runs the eligibility check, manager approval, and credit steps, so every refund follows your policy. Agents can also look up workflow runs, so an operations agent can tell your on-call engineer which order runs failed overnight and where, letting them go stra

title: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management and cross-account backup in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
summary: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management, cross-account backup, and delegated administrators in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. These capabilities help you centrally manage, monitor, and copy backups across the accounts in your organization using AWS Organizations. With cross-account management, you can deploy organization-wide backup policies from your AWS Organizations management account or a delegated administrator account. You can also monitor backup, copy, and restore jobs across all of your organization accounts from one place. With cross-account backup, you can copy recovery points to a backup vault in another account in your organization, which adds protection against accidental or malicious deletion in the source account. You can also register a member account as a delegated administrator, so your teams can manage backups across your organization without needing access to your management account. There is no additional charge to use these capabilitie

title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations
summary: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations, named permission sets that control what actions individual project members can perform. Previously, project members could only be assigned Owner or Contributor designations, which provided nearly identical permissions. With custom designations, administrators define permission sets that align with their organization's personas and assign them to project members. Designations govern all actions within a project, providing administrators with a single permission model for separation of duties. Administrators create designations in the SageMaker Unified Studio administration portal by selecting permissions grouped into categories such as Catalog, Subscriptions, Connections, Notebooks, and Data Agent. For example, a "Data Steward" designation might include permissions to approve subscription requests and publish assets, while an "Analyst" designation is limited to querying data and running notebooks. title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports SOCI-indexed images to start training jobs in seconds
summary: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces support for Seekable OCI (SOCI)-indexed container images for training and processing jobs, so your jobs start running your code sooner. SOCI-indexed images start Amazon SageMaker AI training containers in seconds, cutting GPU idle time during image pulls by up to 90%, with no impact on training performance. Before a training or processing job can run, SageMaker AI downloads its container image to the instance. For deep learning images, which routinely exceed 10 GB, that download adds minutes to the start of every job, and you pay for that time. Now, when your image includes a SOCI index, SageMaker AI lazy-loads the image, fetching only the files needed to start the container and streaming the rest in the background as your code runs. To use this feature, reference a SOCI-indexed image from a private Amazon ECR repository in your training or processing job. title: Amazon Redshift announces hands-off automated cross-region backups
summary: Amazon Redshift announces automated cross-region snapshot copy for Amazon Redshift. You can now have your Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster or serverless workgroup automatically backed up to the target AWS region(s) you choose. The automated cross-region snapshot copy feature will automatically, always copy the most recent snapshot with no manual intervention, continuously and incrementally and ensure your cluster is backed-up to the destination region(s), giving you additional options for business continuity. The benefit to enabling the new automated cross-region snapshot copy feature is that you do not need to manually intervene to initiate a cross-region snapshot copy when an unplanned outage event occurs. Also, this feature takes the most recent snapshot available on your system to copy to the destination region, so you don't have to wait for the next snapshot to be taken, making it independent of your snapshot schedule on your local cluster. title: Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade to Grafana version 13.2
summary: Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade from Grafana version 12.4 to 13.2. Upgrading to version 13.2 brings features launched as part of open-source Grafana versions 13.0 to 13.2. These include Git Sync for dashboards, dynamic dashboards, and PromQL query support in the Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin. With Git Sync, you can treat dashboards as code by linking a workspace to a Git repository. Dashboard modifications can be tracked, reviewed, and reverted through version control. Dynamic dashboards bring a more adaptable approach to layout and paneling. You can construct responsive views driven by conditions that respond to the data and variables in scope. With Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin support for Prometheus Query Language, you can use PromQL to query metrics that CloudWatch takes in via its OpenTelemetry (OTLP) endpoint, in addition to the existing Metric Search and Metrics Insights query types. title: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in additional Regions
summary: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in two additional AWS Regions: Canada (Central) and Africa (Cape Town). DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for Amazon DynamoDB that delivers up to ten times performance improvement, from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds, even at millions of requests per second. With DAX, you can accelerate read-intensive and bursty workloads such as real-time bidding, gaming leaderboards, and retail product catalogs, while offloading read traffic from your DynamoDB tables. DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, so you can add microsecond-latency caching to your applications with minimal code changes. Customers can now keep cached data within the Region and meet low-latency requirements while benefiting from a fully managed service, including automated patching and failover. To learn more, see the Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator page . For the full list of Regions where DAX is available, see the AWS Regional Services page .

title: Amazon Connect Customer Outbound Campaigns now provides journey analytics
summary: Amazon Connect Customer Outbound Campaigns now provides flow designer analytics for journeys, so you can see directly on a journey flow how many customers reached each step and which branch they took. A journey is a multi-step outbound campaign that reaches your customers by voice, email, SMS, or WhatsApp, and branches based on customer behavior. Campaign managers can use these metrics to find the steps in a journey that need changes. A collections team running a payment reminder journey can see how many customers moved from the first SMS reminder to a follow-up call. If the SMS step shows a high error rate, the team can add an email step to its error branch so future customers on that path still get a reminder. You can use flow designer analytics for journeys in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Eur

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 is now available
summary: AWS announces the general availability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 (@aws/agentcore 1.0.0), rebuilt with faster startup, a consistent command structure, and support for more AgentCore resources. The CLI helps developers create, develop, deploy, and operate AI agents and supporting resources from the terminal. With version 1.0, developers can use the project workflow or work directly with harnesses, runtimes, memory, identity, gateways, and payments without first adding them to a project. Developers can invoke existing resources by ID or ARN, open an interactive shell, export a harness, and use searchable menus, resource pickers, and guided workflows. Consistent global flags provide region selection, JSON output, debugging, and version information across commands. Existing projects can be migrated to AgentCore version 1 using the agentcore migrate command. Install AgentCore CLI version 1.0 from npm or explore the source on GitHub . To learn more, visit the Amazon Bedrock

title: Public endpoints for Amazon ElastiCache Serverless now in AWS GovCloud (US)
summary: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports public endpoints in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. A public endpoint lets you connect to your cache from a serverless function or any application running outside a VPC, without setting up a VPN, a bastion host, or an SSH tunnel. With a public endpoint, ElastiCache Serverless gives you a fully managed cache with no VPC to configure and no infrastructure to provision, and you can create one in under a minute. Every connection uses IAM authentication over TLS 1.3, so there's no password to store or rotate. Connect using Valkey GLIDE 2.2 or later, which has built-in IAM support, or another Valkey client paired with the Developer Toolkit for ElastiCache, an open-source library that generates and refreshes IAM authentication tokens for you. With this expansion, public endpoints for ElastiCache Serverless are now available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. title: AWS Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading for Lambda Managed Instances
summary: AWS Lambda now supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) for lazy loading Event Functions packaged as Open Container Initiative (OCI) images running on Lambda Managed Instances . With SOCI support, Lambda fetches only the files needed at each stage of the execution environment startup rather than downloading the entire image upfront, reducing container startup times by up to 70%. Customers building compute-intensive applications such as data processing pipelines, high-throughput API backends, and batch computation workloads require substantial memory and CPU resources to process large datasets, serve low-latency responses at scale, and run complex computations efficiently. Container images for these workloads can reach several gigabytes, and downloading and preparing the full image can take several minutes when provisioning new execution environments. title: Introducing time series collections for the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
summary: Today, we're announcing support for time series collections on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless. With time series collections, you can ingest, store, and analyze logs, metrics, traces, and event data without provisioning or managing clusters. They absorb ingest spikes automatically, keep recent data fast to query, and make months or years of history searchable at low cost, all in the same collection. Time series collections add a new, lower-cost warm storage tier in addition to the existing hot storage tier, so customers can retain their infrequently accessed data without paying hot storage prices. Customers can choose how long data stays hot before transitiong to warm storage. With up to 100 TB of hot storage per collection, time series collections can handle high-volume observability workloads such as application monitoring, security analytics, and IoT telemetry. Alerting and anomaly detection are also now available, so customers can get notified about issues and s

title: Amazon EKS Dashboard now provides fleet-wide visibility into certificate authority (CA) rotation
summary: Today, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) announces certificate authority (CA) rotation visibility in the Amazon EKS Dashboard, giving you a consolidated view of CA rotation across your clusters. The Amazon EKS Dashboard already provides centralized visibility into your clusters across AWS Regions and accounts, and it now includes CA rotation, so you can see where action is needed without checking each cluster individually. Each Amazon EKS cluster has its own CA, and clusters created since 2018 have CAs with a 10-year validity period that are now approaching the point where rotation activities should begin. In the EKS Dashboard, you can now see your clusters and their CA rotation status, which clusters have CAs approaching expiration, and upcoming automated rotation events, so platform teams who operate many clusters can prioritize action across their fleet from one place. title: AWS Lambda durable functions now exports live telemetry for execution insights
summary: AWS Lambda announces the Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter plugin for Lambda durable functions. This new observability plugin captures the step-by-step history of your durable executions and sends them to one or more destinations of your choice. You can use the exported data to gather operational and business insights and keep history beyond the standard retention period. We are also releasing a companion Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents such as Kiro query your exported telemetry data using natural language. Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year. The new Telemetry Exporter sends data such as execution status, operation timing, step input and output, and errors to 13 built-in destinations. Destinations include Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 for Amazon Athena, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Aurora, and Amazon OpenSearch Service. You can redact sensitive fields before export and set a s

title: Amazon ECS Managed Instances adds cross-instance and Spot consolidation
summary: Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Managed Instances introduces two infrastructure optimization updates: cross-instance and Spot consolidation. Cross-instance consolidation evaluates tasks running across multiple underutilized instances together, packing them onto fewer instances to raise utilization and lower costs. Spot consolidation extends this capability to Spot capacity, consolidating underutilized Spot Instances after first verifying replacement capacity is available. Amazon ECS Managed Instances provisions, configures, and operates right-sized Amazon EC2 instances for your workloads, balancing availability and cost. Its infrastructure optimization continuously monitors your fleet, reclaiming idle capacity and consolidating underutilized instances with graceful start-before-stop task replacement. title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports Kubernetes Gateway API
summary: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports the Kubernetes Gateway API, giving customers a standard, portable way to define how traffic reaches their applications. Customers can configure application load balancing using Gateway and HTTPRoute resources, and EKS Auto Mode provisions and manages the underlying AWS infrastructure automatically. With this launch, EKS Auto Mode customers can adopt the next-generation Kubernetes traffic management standard without installing or configuring a separate controller. Capabilities include HTTP and gRPC routing, cross-namespace traffic routing for multi-team environments, weighted traffic splitting, header-based routing, and automatic TLS certificate discovery through AWS Certificate Manager. Existing workloads using Ingress resources continue to work alongside Gateway API resources. To get started, see the Amazon EKS documentation . Gateway API support is included as part of EKS Auto Mode and is available in all AWS Regions where EKS Auto Mode is supported.

title: AWS IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now supports change notifications through Amazon EventBridge
summary: AWS IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now delivers real-time events to Amazon EventBridge when users, groups, or group memberships or the identity store itself is created, updated, or deleted. AWS IAM Identity Center Identity Store is a central repository that allows you to manage identities and access across AWS accounts and applications, serving as the identity source for AWS IAM Identity Center. This new capability helps you automatically respond to identity lifecycle events and support your security and compliance processes by detecting changes as they happen. With Identity Store change notifications, you can build automated workflows that respond to identity changes in your organization. For example, security teams can create EventBridge rules that trigger AWS Lambda functions to audit user provisioning activity, send alerts to security information and event management (SIEM) systems, or update access in downstream applications when users or groups change. title: AWS Backup adds restore testing support for Amazon Redshift
summary: AWS Backup restore testing now supports Amazon Redshift. Restore testing helps you automate and periodically run restore tests of your backups, so you can confirm that your Amazon Redshift backups restore successfully and measure how long the restores take. You can now include Amazon Redshift in your restore testing plans alongside other supported AWS resources across storage, compute, and database services. Restore testing plans automatically select recovery points, run restores on a schedule, and measure restore job completion time against your recovery time objectives (RTO). This helps you evaluate recovery readiness and meet regulatory and compliance requirements for disaster recovery and business continuity. To get started, create a restore testing plan and assign your Amazon Redshift resources by Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or tag. title: Announcing the AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business unified storefront
summary: Today, AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business announced the unified storefront. Organizations can now give their teams one curated catalog that puts software, data, and AI tools from AWS Marketplace alongside physical goods and supplies from Amazon Business. Many enterprises already buy from both, but they manage two catalogs with duplicated approval rules and separate reporting. The unified storefront can now give procurement teams one front door for both. Built on AWS Marketplace Storefront, the unified storefront lets administrators connect their organization's Amazon Business account and import Amazon Business products into their branded storefront. Administrators set governance rules once, and they apply across both catalogs. Buyers can browse AWS Marketplace listings and Amazon Business products in one place. title: SageMaker MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16
summary: Amazon SageMaker AI MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16, bringing a redesigned tracing experience and faster experiment tracking to your generative AI and machine learning workflows. MLflow 3.16 improves debugging and analysis of generative AI applications and agents. The redesigned trace explorer is now the default, with adjustable row height, reorderable columns, custom columns from any trace tag or metadata field. This release also accelerates metric charts for experiments with large metric histories. New MLflow Apps are created on MLflow 3.16 by default. Existing MLflow Apps will be upgraded to MLflow 3.16 during an upcoming maintenance window, with no action required. MLflow 3.16 is available in all AWS Regions where MLflow Apps are available. To learn more, visit the SageMaker AI MLflow developer guide .

title: Amazon Connect Customer supports inline attachment previews
summary: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents preview attachments directly in the agent workspace, reducing contact handling time and limiting the need to download sensitive customer information. Agents can preview PDFs, images, and text files across email, chat, and cases, navigate between attachments, and view multi-page documents without leaving the conversation. Amazon Connect Customer attachment previews is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London) regions . To learn more and get started, please refer to the help documentation or visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

title: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports up to 384 ACUs
summary: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports database capacity of up to 384 Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs) for Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition, a 50% increase from the previous maximum of 256 ACUs. Each ACU provides approximately 2 gibibytes (GiB) of memory with corresponding CPU and networking, so a single Aurora serverless database can now scale up to 768 GiB of memory. When the workload completes, Aurora serverless automatically scales down to zero. This makes Aurora serverless especially well-suited for agentic AI applications, which typically have bursts of activity, long idle windows, and unpredictable traffic patterns. Aurora serverless handles all of it automatically, scaling capacity with your agents, so you only pay for what you use. With 384 ACU support, customers can now use Aurora serverless for even more demanding workloads while continuing to scale down to zero when not in use, paying only for the capacity consumed. title: Amazon ElastiCache expands data tiering to R8gd and R7gd nodes in Europe (Spain) and Asia Pacific (Hyderabad)
summary: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey data tiering is now available on Graviton4-based R8gd nodes in the AWS Europe (Spain) Region, and on Graviton3-based R7gd nodes in the Europe (Spain) and Asia Pacific (Hyderabad) Regions. Data tiering is a lower-cost way to scale your Valkey clusters to hundreds of terabytes of capacity. It uses solid state drives (SSDs) on each node alongside memory. When memory fills up, ElastiCache automatically moves the least recently used items to SSD. When your application reads an item stored on SSD, ElastiCache moves it back into memory before serving the request. Data tiering is a good fit for workloads that regularly access up to 20% of their dataset, and for applications that can tolerate some extra latency when they read data from SSD. R8gd nodes are powered by AWS Graviton4 processors. They deliver up to 47% higher throughput, up to 43% lower P99 latency, and up to 31% better price-performance than Graviton3-based nodes of the same size. R7gd nodes are powere

title: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now supports changing durability on existing clusters
summary: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now lets you enable or disable durability on your existing node-based clusters. Previously, you couldn't change the durability configuration of an existing cluster in place. This made it harder to move from caching to persistent data store use cases, or to adapt as your application requirements change. Now you can change durability at any point in your application's lifecycle. You can choose between two durability options: synchronous and asynchronous writes. Synchronous writes persist data across at least two AZs before responding to the client, designed for zero data loss at single-digit millisecond write latency. Asynchronous writes persist data after responding to the client, maintaining microsecond write latency at no additional cost. However, up to 10 seconds of uncommitted data could be lost in the rare event of a failure. Both options maintain microsecond read latency. title: Amazon Neptune now supports online index rebuild to reclaim storage
summary: Amazon Neptune Database now supports online index rebuild, a new capability that helps database administrators and application teams defragment Neptune indexes and reclaim unused storage space without taking their database offline. Over time, insert, update, and delete operations create gaps of unused space within data pages, keeping the VolumeBytesUsed metric artificially elevated even after data is deleted. This fragmentation increases I/O costs and degrades query performance for teams running Gremlin, openCypher, or SPARQL workloads at scale. With online index rebuild, read and write queries continue uninterrupted on both the writer instance and read replicas throughout the entire rebuild process. You can target all indexes, only quad indexes, or only dictionary indexes, making this feature well-suited for post-deletion cleanup, periodic maintenance, storage limit management, and performance tuning on heavily fragmented databases. title: Amazon ECR now supports replication backfill for existing container images
summary: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replication backfill, enabling you to replicate existing images in your private registry to your configured replication registry destinations. Previously, replication only applied to images pushed after the replication configuration was enabled, requiring customers to manually retag images to trigger replication of preexisting images. With replication backfill, you can now replicate your full image catalog to new or existing destinations with a single API call. Replication backfill is useful when expanding to a new AWS Region, validating disaster recovery readiness, updating replication rules, or ensuring complete image catalogs exist across Regions for compliance purposes. You can run up to ten backfill jobs concurrently, monitor progress and per-image results through new APIs, and stop a job at any time without deleting images that have already been replicated. Replication backfill is available in all AWS Regions where Amazo

title: Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports ModifyVolume API
summary: Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances now supports the ModifyVolume API, which lets you change volume size, volume type, IOPS, or throughput in place, without detaching the volume or restarting the instance. Previously, changing storage capacity or performance on a deployed managed instance required rebuilding it. With ModifyVolume, you can increase volume size up to 16,384 GiB, switch between supported Amazon EBS volume types, adjust IOPS for gp3, io1, and io2 volumes, and modify throughput for gp3 volumes. The API supports idempotency tokens to prevent duplicate changes, and you can track progress with the Amazon EC2 DescribeVolumesModifications operation. ModifyVolume is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon WorkSpaces Core Managed Instances is available. To get started, call ModifyVolume directly, or use it through your WorkSpaces Core partner solution once available. title: Amazon IVS Low-Latency Streaming now provides a failover slate
summary: Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) Low-Latency Streaming now provides a failover slate, an animated image that IVS displays to viewers when a broadcaster's stream is unexpectedly interrupted. Instead of a buffering wheel or frozen frame, viewers see the slate until the broadcaster reconnects. Live playback then resumes automatically, without viewers needing to refresh their player. The failover slate helps you retain your audience during momentary disruptions and is ideal for broadcasters streaming from mobile devices or from locations with unreliable connectivity. You can enable the failover slate on new or existing channels and monitor slate activity with Amazon EventBridge events and Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Amazon IVS is a managed live streaming solution designed to make low-latency or real-time video available to viewers around the world. summary: Today, AWS announces light mode support in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio for Identity Center (IDC) based domains. Customers can now configure the visual interface mode to match their preference, choosing between dark and light themes. With this launch, customers can set this visual preference in both IAM-based and IDC-based domains. Light mode helps improve readability in bright environments and provides a familiar visual experience for customers who prefer lighter interfaces. Combined with the existing dark mode, this update gives you full control over the appearance of your development environment, improving accessibility and reducing eye strain across varying lighting conditions. In SageMaker Unified Studio settings, you can choose 'Customize appearance' under your Profile settings to select between visual modes including dark mode, light mode, and device setting, which matches your operating system's setting.
