title: Amazon Connect Customer expands testing and simulation to validate flow action outcomes
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now enables you to validate the outcomes of your customer experience flow actions during testing and simulation. In addition to confirming that an action started, you can now verify the data it returns when it completes, such as a Lambda function response, an Amazon Lex resolved intent, or the variables set by an Agentic CX block. When a test fails, you can pinpoint the exact action that returned an unexpected result instead of tracing it back from a downstream step, so you can resolve issues faster and launch flow changes with greater confidence. To learn more about this feature, see testing and simulation in the Connect Customer administrator guide. For a complete list of testing and simulation capabilities available by AWS Region, refer to Availability of Connect Customer features by Region . title: Amazon Connect Customer now lets you view metrics by customer lifetime value and repeat-caller status
summary: Now you can view your metrics across customer segments: customer lifetime value (LTV) and repeat callers. See how any metric differs for repeat callers versus the rest of your contacts, or how results hold up among your highest-LTV customers; so you can spot the groups trending the wrong way before it shows up in the aggregate. Where a segment is underperforming, you can act. Route high-LTV customers to your most effective people, adjust the knowledge bases and self-service flows that repeat callers are falling back from, or refine agent guidance for segments where satisfaction is slipping. The segment tells you where to look; the metrics tell you what to fix.

title: Amazon Connect Customer now measures the outcomes that drive retention and revenue
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now scores the outcome of your customer interactions. It shows whether the customer left satisfied, is at risk of churning, made a purchase, or resolved their need in self-service. You can now see whether an interaction worked, not just how efficiently it ran. Each metric comes with a default definition you can adjust to match how your business defines success and are available both through the analytics dashboards and APIs.

title: AWS Key Management Service now supports ML-KEM for post-quantum key encapsulation
summary: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now supports Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM), a post-quantum cryptography standard under NIST FIPS 203 , which enables two parties to establish a shared secret. NIST designed ML-KEM to replace the classical key-establishment schemes, like DH/ECDH key agreement, and RSA-based key transport, in their strategic cryptographic roadmap (see NIST IR 8547 ). ML-KEM addresses the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat to those classical schemes, where an adversary records the key-establishment exchange today and recovers the shared secret once sufficiently powerful quantum computers become available. KMS supports all three ML-KEM key specs defined in NIST FIPS 203: ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024. The Encapsulate API uses the public key to produce a random 32-byte shared secret and its ciphertext form. title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports cross-Region trusted identity propagation
summary: Trusted identity propagation carries a user's identity with their request, so AWS services can grant permissions based on who the user is and their underlying group associations, and log that user's access for auditing. With cross-Region support, this identity context can now be propagated to AWS services running in different AWS Regions, giving you greater flexibility in how you architect and deploy across AWS Regions. Customers often distribute workloads across AWS Regions for many reasons including separating the compute from the data it queries, to running workloads where capacity is available, or for disaster recovery and global scale. Previously, trusted identity propagation required all of the AWS services accessing a user's identity to reside in the same AWS Region. To reach services in another AWS Region, customers had to either grant access through broad IAM roles that cannot distinguish individual users or consolidate all their services into a single AWS Region. title: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now supports Launch Before Terminate at account-level to replace instances
summary: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now lets you enable Launch Before Terminate as the default replacement behavior across all Auto Scaling groups in your account. When enabled, Auto Scaling launches a replacement instance and waits for it to pass health checks before terminating the instance it replaces, helping your applications maintain full capacity and availability during instance replacement events. This applies to replacement events such as instance refreshes, rebalancing, health checks, and maximum-instance-lifetime replacements. You can enable Launch Before Terminate through AWS EC2 Auto Scaling account settings, which let you configure the behavior once at the account level instead of on each Auto Scaling group individually. You can manage the setting with the new `PutAccountSetting` and `DescribeAccountSettings` APIs, available through the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports OAuth for Apache Iceberg REST Catalog APIs
summary: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports OAuth 2.0 bearer token authentication for Apache Iceberg REST Catalog (IRC) APIs using AWS Sign-In. The Apache Iceberg REST Catalog specification defines OAuth 2.0 as its standard authentication mechanism, and query engines such as Apache Spark, Trino, and Apache Flink implement it natively. These engines and external integration partners can now authenticate to the Glue Data Catalog Iceberg endpoint using standard OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens, in addition to AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4). You can now grant partners federated access to your Iceberg tables without distributing AWS credentials. Using OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693), you exchange an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity token for a short-lived, Glue-scoped bearer token and include it in IRC requests following the same standards-based pattern used across the Iceberg ecosystem. title: Web Search on AWS Bedrock now supports domain filtering and user location controls
summary: Web Search on AWS Bedrock now supports two new controls that give you more precision over the results that ground a model's response: domain filtering and user location. Both are configured directly on the web_search tool in your existing OpenAI Responses API request. With domain filtering, you can restrict Web Search results to a set of domains you choose. Using the filters parameter, you specify up to 100 allowed_domains to limit results to trusted sources, or up to 100 blocked_domains to exclude sources you don't want. This is useful when you want responses grounded only in specific sites, or when you need to keep certain domains out of results. With user location, you can optionally specify location parameters so that Web Search can return results relevant to that geography. This helps with location-dependent questions, such as regional availability or local services. title: Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now supports persistent chat across linked AWS Regions
summary: Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now provides customers a mechanism to deliver long, persistent chat experiences across linked AWS Regions. With this capability, end users can resume previous conversations with full context, metadata, and transcripts carried over across Regions, eliminating the need for end users to repeat information and allowing agents to provide personalized service with access to the entire conversation history across AWS Regions. For example, an end user can start a chat in US-East (N. Virginia) and later come back to it in the linked US-West (Oregon) Region, continuing the same conversation with an agent with full conversation history and chat attachment. To adopt this capability, onboard to Global routing . This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency is supported. To learn more, visit Amazon Connect Customer Admin Guide .

title: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now support 1:1 NAT
summary: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now provide managed one-to-one network address translation (NAT) directly on their attachments, through integration with Regional Private NAT Gateway. This enables customers to connect private networks that share the same IP address ranges without renumbering either network, deploying a NAT appliance, or writing return-traffic rules. Networks with overlapping Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) blocks have long been unable to communicate, a common blocker during mergers and acquisitions, when connecting partner networks over AWS Site-to-Site VPN, in multicloud connectivity, and when independently provisioned VPCs need to interconnect. Using this capability, customers can define address-translation rules on a AWS Transit Gateway or AWS Cloud WAN attachment, specifying the private IP range each source CIDR translates to, across Amazon VPC, AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and SD-WAN appliances connected through Transit Gateway Connect. title: Amazon EMR on EKS reduces EMR charge by 30 percent
summary: Amazon EMR announces a reduction of 30 percent in the EMR charge added to EKS when running EMR on EKS. This price decrease applies to both the per-vCPU-hour charge and the per-GB-hour charge, while the underlying Amazon EKS charges remain unchanged. All EMR workloads running on the EKS deployment option benefit from this change. Now, you can run Apache Spark workloads on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) at a lower cost, and the new price automatically applies to your EMR on EKS workloads with no additional action required on your end. The 30% reduction in EMR on EKS pricing is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon EMR on EKS is available. To learn more about EMR on EKS, visit the Amazon EMR on EKS documentation and the Amazon EMR pricing page .

summary: Amazon Connect Customer Profiles now allows administrators to customize which customer data that agents see in the agent workspace, and how it is displayed, using layouts they build in Profile Explorer. Customer Profiles provides agents with a real-time, unified view of each customer during interactions, combining contact history with customer data from multiple sources. Agents who handle different kinds of requests need different customer data in front of them. Within Profile Explorer, administrators can create and save each layout of Customer Profiles widgets, such as contact history, contact information, and lifetime value calculated attributes, and assign it to agents in place of the legacy Customer Profiles view. For example, an airline baggage claims agent sees contact history, active flights, and baggage ticket information, while a loyalty agent sees loyalty status, preferences, and upcoming flights. title: Amazon OpenSearch Service introduces intelligent ingestion for logs and documents in Amazon S3
summary: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now offers intelligent ingestion, a fully managed feature that turns logs and documents stored in Amazon S3 into searchable content in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (NextGen) collections . With intelligent ingestion, you can set up ingestion with a few clicks in the AWS Management Console or a single API call, with no ingestion infrastructure to manage. Intelligent ingestion supports observability logs and structured data in JSON, NDJSON, and JSON array formats, and unstructured files in PDF, Word, plain text, and Markdown formats. You choose an S3 source and a collection index, and intelligent ingestion handles the rest. It automatically detects data types, parses documents, describes images, chunks text, generates vector embeddings, and indexes the results. You don't need to manage ingestion or document-processing infrastructure, or size capacity in advance. title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports a 5-second default refresh interval
summary: Starting today, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless reduces the default refresh interval to 5 seconds for both search and vector collections. The refresh interval controls how quickly newly ingested documents become available for search. By lowering the default from 10 seconds to 5 seconds, newly written data becomes searchable faster, giving applications quicker read-after-write visibility automatically, with no configuration changes and no action required on your part. This improvement applies to the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless and takes effect by default on both search and vector collections. Faster refresh is valuable for workloads that continuously ingest data and need near real-time retrieval, including full-text search over frequently updated content as well as vector use cases such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, and recommendation and personalization systems. title: AWS CloudFormation now simplifies stack update rollback operations
summary: AWS CloudFormation now makes it simpler to complete an update rollback and get back to deploying. An update rollback returns your stack to a known good state. Starting today, if some resources cannot roll back automatically, force rollback enables you to complete the rollback in a single operation. It works across every CloudFormation workflow, from the AWS CLI , and SDKs to AWS CDK and AI agents. With force rollback, CloudFormation completes the update rollback and returns your stack to a deployable state in a single operation, instead of requiring you to identify, list, and retry the operation for each affected resource. Any resource that still needs attention, such as one affected by a change outside CloudFormation, is recorded for you to review and resolve it before your next deployment. title: Amazon SageMaker AI announces training session APIs for serverless model customization
summary: Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization now supports training session APIs, giving customers full control over their post-training algorithm without provisioning or managing GPU infrastructure. Managed techniques, including SFT, DPO, and other reinforcement learning methods, let customers pick a technique and a model and have SageMaker AI run the training. With training session APIs, teams get to write the training loop, whether that's reproducing SFT or DPO on their own terms or implementing a custom loss, a new RL reward signal, a data curriculum, or an algorithm straight from the latest research. Operations such as forward_backward(), optim_step(), and sample() become API calls against a live, stateful session, so customers compose whatever training procedure their technique requires while SageMaker AI handles GPU allocation, model and LoRA loading, distributed execution, fault recovery, checkpoint storage, and security. title: AWS Direct Connect announces 100G expansion in Bangalore, India
summary: Today, AWS announced the expansion of 100 Gbps dedicated connections at the existing AWS Direct Connect location in the Netmagic DC2 data center near Bangalore, India. You can now establish private, direct network access to all public AWS Regions (except those in China), AWS GovCloud Regions, and AWS Local Zones from this location. The Direct Connect service enables you to establish a private, physical network connection between AWS and your data center, office, or colocation environment. These private connections can provide a more consistent network experience than those made over the public internet. For more information on the over 150 Direct Connect locations worldwide, visit the locations section of the Direct Connect product detail pages . Or, visit our getting started page to learn more about how to purchase and deploy Direct Connect.

title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports pausing and resuming connectors
service: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
summary: Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now supports pausing and resuming connectors, letting you temporarily pause a connector from processing records and resume it later. This is useful when you need to stop data flow during maintenance on a source database or a sink target, or to pause processing while you investigate an upstream or downstream issue. Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, pausing a connector meant deleting it and recreating it - a more disruptive operation, adding risk and operational overhead. With this launch, you can pause a running connector and resume it in place when you are ready — a paused connector keeps its configuration, capacity settings, and committed offsets, and its tasks continue processing from the offsets they last committed when you resume. title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports serverless model customization for Muse Glimmer, Qwen 3.8 and Ministral 3 models
summary: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports serverless model customization for Muse Glimmer, Qwen3.8 27B, and Ministral 3 3B, 8B, and 14B models. In addition to deploying these models on SageMaker AI, you can now adapt them to your specific domains and workflows, using supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), and reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) techniques. You can also adapt these models with either low-rank adaptation (LoRA) or full fine-tuning techniques. This launch adds these models to a wide variety of models available for serverless customization on SageMaker AI, including models from the Nova, Gemma 4, Nemotron 3.5, Qwen, Llama, gpt-oss, and DeepSeek families. Model customization lets you tailor foundation models with your proprietary data so a smaller, right-sized model can match frontier-model quality on your tasks, while also reducing cost and latency. title: AgentCore Gateway now supports Bedrock InvokeModel APIs and model fallback
summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway now supports the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream APIs on its inference endpoint, along with model fallback routing for inference traffic. With InvokeModel support, you can point your existing Amazon Bedrock SDK integration at the gateway and reach any model provider through one governed endpoint, without rewriting client code for each provider. With model fallback, the gateway automatically routes a request to an alternative model or provider when the primary destination is throttled, out of capacity, or unreachable, so your agents stay available without each client implementing its own retry logic. For fallback routing, you define an ordered chain of alternative destinations in a gateway rule, along with the conditions that trigger a switch, such as throttling, server errors, or response timeouts. title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 4 additional AWS regions
summary: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 4 additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Thailand), and Europe (Spain). With this launch, you can use Lambda MicroVMs in a total of 14 AWS Regions. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume speeds, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code. Developers can use Lambda MicroVMs to give each user or job their own isolated compute environment without managing virtualization infrastructure or choosing between isolation, speed, and state retention. MicroVMs enable secure, stateful, and responsive code execution for applications including AI coding assistants, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. With today's launch, developers can run Lambda MicroVMs closer to their end-users in 4 additional Regions, helping meet latency and data residency requirements. To get started, create a Micro

title: Amazon Quick Now Available in the AWS Singapore Region
summary: Amazon Quick is now available in the AWS Asia Pacific (Singapore) region (ap-southeast-1). This launch allows customers in Singapore to access the full power of Amazon Quick while meeting local requirements for data sovereignty. Amazon Quick provides business users an agentic teammate that quickly answers questions at work and turns those answers into actions. With Amazon Quick, every user is empowered to make better decisions faster and take actions without switching applications using AI they can trust. Today’s launch allows customers to take advantage of Amazon Quick’s capabilities including AI-powered chat, Research, Spaces, and QuickSight dashboards — with their data stored and processed locally within the AWS Singapore region. For a full list of AWS regions where Amazon Quick is available, visit the Quick regional availability page. To learn more, visit the Amazon Quick documentation or product detail page .

title: CVE-2026-85781 - Unverified access point ownership in Amazon EFS CSI Driver
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-099-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 09/04/2026 11:45 AM PDT Description: The Amazon EFS CSI Driver is an open-source Kubernetes Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver that lets Kubernetes workloads use Amazon EFS file systems. We identified CVE-2026-85781, an issue in the driver's volume-deletion logic. When the controller is configured with the non-default --delete-access-point-root-dir=true option, it did not verify that the EFS access point referenced by a PersistentVolume's volume handle belonged to the file system referenced by that same volume handle. An authenticated Kubernetes user with permission to create PersistentVolumes could use a crafted volume handle to cause the controller to recursively delete directories from an Amazon EFS file system that the user was not otherwise authorized to modify. This issue does not affect Amazon EFS itself; Amazon EFS access controls operated as designed. Impacted versions: <=

title: CVE-2026-85654 - Code injection in the CDK generator in Amazon awslabs.dynamodb-mcp-server
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-097-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 09/04/2026 10:00 AM PDT Description: Amazon awslabs.dynamodb-mcp-server is an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI coding assistants to interact with Amazon DynamoDB, including table design, data modeling, and CDK infrastructure generation. We identified CVE-2026-85654, an improper neutralization of special elements used in a template engine in the CDK generator component. Under certain circumstances, a context-dependent actor could execute arbitrary code on the host that deploys the generated application via crafted table, index, or attribute names in a data model file. Impacted versions: >= 2.0.10 AND <= 2.1.5 Please refer to the article below for the most up-to-date and complete information related to this AWS Security Bulletin.

title: CVE-2026-83551 - Cleartext storage of HMAC signing key in Amazon SageMaker Python SDK
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-093-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 09/01/2026 11:00 AM PDT Description: SageMaker Python SDK's @step and @remote decorator pipeline component uses an HMAC key to protect the integrity of serialized function payloads stored in S3. We identified an issue where the HMAC secret key is stored in cleartext within pipeline definitions and accessible via the DescribePipeline API. This allows an actor with a role in that account that has permissions to invoke DescribePipeline to extract the key, create cloud-pickled payloads with valid HMACs, and overwrite S3 objects, achieving code execution in another user's pipeline execution context within the same AWS account. Impacted versions: - HMAC Configuration in SageMaker Python SDK v3 < v3.11.0 - HMAC Configuration in SageMaker Python SDK v2 < v2.256.0 Please refer to the article below for the most up-to-date and complete information related to this AWS Security Bulletin.

We identified CVE-2026-83497 where a remote authenticated user with basic read/search permissions can run arbitrary code on the server by providing a crafted cursor parameter to the plugins/sql endpoint. Amazon-ssm-agent makes it possible for Systems Manager to update, manage, and configure these resources. We identified CVE-2026-81849, where an improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in the aws:downloadContent plugin in amazon-ssm-agent before 3.3.4515.0 might allow an authenticated remote user whose ssm:SendCommand permission is restricted to the AWS-DownloadContent document, to write arbitrary files outside the intended download directory with root privileges, via crafted object keys in the S3 source the document is directed to retrieve. title: CVE-2026-77811 - Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Integration Template Asset in OpenSearch Dashboards
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-088-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 08/21/2026 13:00 PM PDT Description: Amazon OpenSearch Service is a managed service that makes it easy to deploy, operate, and scale OpenSearch clusters. We identified CVE-2026-77811, a stored cross-site scripting issue in the dashboards-observability plugin in OpenSearch Dashboards. Improper input validation in the integrations static file endpoint allows a remote authenticated actor with write permissions to OpenSearch Dashboards saved objects to upload a custom integration containing arbitrary JavaScript. When another user accesses the static file endpoint directly, the script executes in their browser session and can perform actions on their behalf, including making API calls to OpenSearch with their privileges. Affected products & versions: OpenSearch Dashboards dashboards-observability plugin (open-source, self-managed): - Affected: versions before 3.4 and versions before 2.19.6 -

title: CVE-2026-77810 - Issue with Athena Federated Query Neptune Connector
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-087-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 08/21/2026 12:30 PM PDT Description: Amazon Athena is a serverless, interactive query service that lets you analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Athena Query Federation is a feature that allows you to connect to data sources outside of Amazon S3 like DynamoDB, Azure Synapse, and custom connectors using standard SQL syntax. These connectors are open source and deployed to the Athena service on a regular basis. We identified CVE-2026-77810, in the Neptune connector where a user with access to Neptune through Athena Federated Query could gain access to properties in the Lambda supplying the compute for the connector. Impacted versions: <=v2026.28.1 AND >=v2024.15.1 Please refer to the article below for the most up-to-date and complete information related to this AWS Security Bulletin.

AWS Transform adds storage migration assessments for Amazon S3, EBS, EFS, and FSx
summary: Migration assessments in AWS Transform now evaluate on-premises storage for migration to AWS. Instead of manually analyzing thousands of volumes across protocols, capacity, and performance, you upload a storage inventory and AWS Transform does the mapping for you. It matches each workload to the best-fit service, sizes the recommendation, and projects costs to produce a total cost of ownership business case. Bring NAS shares, SAN LUNs, direct-attached disks, or backup repositories via a NetApp Digital Advisor export, RVTools file, or other inventory. AWS Transform routes workloads across Amazon S3, Amazon EBS, Amazon EFS, and Amazon FSx (NetApp ONTAP, Windows File Server, OpenZFS, Lustre). Run what-if scenarios to compare deployment options such as Single-AZ vs. Multi-AZ or cost-optimized vs. performance-optimized, then ask follow-up questions about any result in chat. Storage migration assessments are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is available. To learn more, see th

title: AWS Direct Connect announces 100G expansion in Manchester, England
summary: Today, AWS announced the expansion of 10 Gbps and 100 Gbps dedicated connections with MACsec encryption capabilities at the existing AWS Direct Connect location in the Equinix MA3 data center near Manchester, England. You can now establish private, direct network access to all public AWS Regions (except those in China), AWS GovCloud Regions, and AWS Local Zones from this location. This is the third AWS Direct Connect location in England to provide 100 Gbps connections with MACsec encryption capabilities. The Direct Connect service enables you to establish a private, physical network connection between AWS and your data center, office, or colocation environment. These private connections can provide a more consistent network experience than those made over the public internet. For more information on the over 150 Direct Connect locations worldwide, visit the locations section of the Direct Connect product detail pages . title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
summary: Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate, in near real-time. With user data in the standby Region, you can redirect traffic and keep authentication available if there is a disruption in your primary Region. Previously, MRR was available in 16 commercial Regions. You can now also use MRR to replicate between additional AWS Regions, helping you meet resilience, data residency, and compliance requirements in the Regions that best align with your business needs. MRR is available as an add-on for user pools in the Essentials or Plus feature tiers, and requires a multi-Region AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK). title: Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS now support On-Demand Capacity Reservations
summary: Starting today, you can reserve compute capacity for your Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS DB instances in one or more Availability Zones for as long as you need it. Reserving capacity helps ensure that DB instance create, restore, scale-compute, and start operations don't fail because of insufficient capacity. On-Demand Capacity Reservations are designed for workloads that need assurance that specific DB instance capacity will be available when they need it for business-critical events, such as migrations, product launches, seasonal peaks, high-availability deployments, or disaster recovery. You choose the DB instance class, engine, Availability Zones, and reserved capacity per Availability Zone, and RDS holds that capacity for you. Capacity can be reserved in two or more Availability Zones to support Multi-AZ deployments. title: Amazon Connect Customer launches two new layouts for agent workspace
summary: Amazon Connect Customer now offers two different layouts that optimize screen space on the agent workspace. Contact center agents spend hours each day in the agent workspace, which includes all of the contact controls and applications they need to resolve customer issues. Agents who handle different channels and workflows want the workspace arranged differently, so that they can quickly read, respond, and access their tools. Now, administrators can choose the best layout for each team, maximizing agent efficiency and satisfaction. On the Modern layout, contact controls are at the top of the workspace, maximizing screen space for the applications beneath during voice calls. When agents handle chat, email, and task contacts on the Modern layout, they now have a taller, wider area to read and respond. The Classic layout offers a familiar experience for agents already using the agent workspace, now with contact controls that expand and contract by channel and a resizable agent assist appli

title: Amazon S3 server access log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs now available in five additional AWS Regions
summary: Amazon S3 server access log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, AWS European Sovereign Cloud, and AWS China Regions. With your access logs in CloudWatch Logs, you can query them as they arrive, set alarms, and encrypt them with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. This new delivery path complements the existing delivery of server access logs to S3 general purpose buckets, giving you more flexibility in how you monitor and analyze access to your data. With delivery to CloudWatch Logs, you can set alarms on error rates, monitor traffic patterns, investigate access incidents, and correlate S3 access activity with the rest of your operational data. S3 server access log delivery to CloudWatch Logs is now available in all AWS Regions. Amazon CloudWatch Logs charges for vended logs apply. For pricing details, visit Amazon CloudWatch pricing . To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 User Guide .

title: AWS Network Firewall now supports Route 53 Resolved IP Validation
summary: AWS Network Firewall now supports IP validation, extending domain-based filtering beyond HTTP/HTTPS to protocols such as SFTP and SSH. This new capability validates that a connection's destination IP address was resolved through your VPC's Amazon Route 53 VPC Resolver, closing security gaps where clients could bypass domain rules. This feature enables Network Firewall customers to implement domain filtering rules for any protocol, not just HTTP/HTTPS, providing more flexible security policies than IP-based rules alone. It simplifies protection against Server Name Identifier (SNI) spoofing by validating the IPs resolved by the Route 53 VPC Resolver against the SNI, ensuring traffic only reaches legitimately resolved destinations. Organizations can now enforce consistent domain-based security policies across all outbound traffic types, from web applications to file transfer protocols, without complex workarounds. Additionally, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall can be used with your VPC Reso

title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports custom sequence lengths for serverless model customization jobs
summary: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces the ability to configure the sequence length used during your serverless model customization job. Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization supports fine-tuning for many open-weight models, including models from popular families including gpt-oss, Gemma, Llama, Nemotron, and Qwen. Previously, each fine-tuning recipe ran at a fixed sequence length that customers could not modify. Customers sometimes need to modify these parameters to achieve better results for their use case. Customers also asked for longer sequence lengths than the static defaults we supported on some models. Now, you can set sequence length parameters as part of the customization job's hyperparameters, anywhere up to the published maximum for your chosen model and technique. You can set the dataset_max_len hyperparameter for SFT and DPO jobs or set max_prompt_length and max_response_length hyperparameters for RFT jobs. This gives you more control to match your training dat

title: Announcing Amazon ECS Gateway, a managed ingress solution for your ECS services
summary: AWS announces Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Gateway, a new resource that simplifies ingress networking for containerized applications by dynamically provisioning and managing Application Load Balancers (ALBs) and their supporting resources directly in your account. With ECS Gateway, platform teams define organizational networking standards once on a gateway and associate it with one or more clusters, giving organizations a centralized way to govern how traffic reaches their ECS services. Application teams simply opt in to inherit those standards without requiring networking expertise. ECS Gateway offers host-based routing, allows up to 25 services to share an ALB to optimize infrastructure costs, and gives each service a unique Domain Name System (DNS) hostname. ECS manages the full lifecycle of the underlying infrastructure, provisioning the first ALB when your first service connects, adding more ALBs when capacity is reached, and removing them when no longer needed. title: Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating replicas
summary: Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating a replica without deleting its table or data. Global tables provide fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active replication. You can now stop replication to and from a replica and continue using the same table as a single-Region table. An account can leave a shared multi-account global table and continue using its table independently. You can also stop replication to a Region while keeping its table for local workloads, validation, or audit, without creating a replacement table or copying data. DynamoDB supports disassociating replicas in all AWS Regions for same-account and multi-account global tables that use multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC). To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, DynamoDB API, or AWS CloudFormation. For more information, see Disassociating replicas in the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide.

title: Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway: A fully-managed ingress solution for ECS services
summary: Try Amazon ECS Gateway, a new account-level resource that simplifies ingress networking for containerized workloads by dynamically provisioning and managing the necessary infrastructure on your behalf, with all resources created directly in your account.

title: Amazon WorkSpaces simplifies secure AI agent access to enterprise cloud desktops with less infrastructure to operate and manage
summary: WorkSpaces for AI agents now handles authentication and desktop connections as part of the managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) service, so you can connect agents to governed cloud desktops, removing the need to write custom code. This makes it easy to use WorkSpaces with any client that supports MCP. Connecting an agent to a desktop previously required you to manage presession requirements; generate, invoke, and rotate streaming URLs manually, adding complexity every time a session expired. You can now create sessions with your existing AWS credentials through OAuth 2.0, and the service handles the connection lifecycle. You configure once which desktop stack to use, and your agents reach the right desktop without ever seeing or handling the underlying streaming connection. You can also query session state to see which desktop stack, fleet, and session an agent is connected to, and generate a link for real-time observability of your agent. title: AWS announces TorchNeuron: Native PyTorch Support for AWS Trainium (Public Beta)
summary: Today, AWS launched the public beta of TorchNeuron, an open source native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium. Trainium is a portfolio of AI chips designed to deliver high performance and cost efficiency for deep learning AI training and inference workloads. TorchNeuron enables AI scientists and researchers to experiment and build models with PyTorch natively on Trainium. With TorchNeuron, developers can enable their PyTorch code on Trainium simply by switching to .to('neuron') while maintaining full PyTorch compatibility with eager execution, torch.compile, and standard PyTorch APIs. Additionally, TorchNeuron integrates with Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) to enable custom operators and performance optimization for Trainium hardware. TorchNeuron is available as open source through the TorchNeuron github repo for Amazon EC2 Trainium2 instances and Amazon EC2 Trainium3 instances. To learn more about TorchNeuron and AWS Trainium accelerators, visit the AWS Neuron page .

title: AWS Partner Central launches Program Navigator, Case Study Generator, and streamlined specialization review
summary: AWS Partner Central now features Program Navigator, a unified experience that lets partners discover, apply for, and track AWS Specialization program applications in one place. Partners can browse specialization designations, view requirements and benefits, and submit applications through a guided, step-by-step workflow. The new Case Study Generator in AWS Partner Central gives partners a redesigned creation experience with three starting paths: build a case study directly with AI assistance, import from an existing customer success story URL, or auto-populate from an opportunity. Case studies created for go-to-market purposes now follow a streamlined review path, a lightweight policy validation that lets partners publish directly to AWS domains without a specialization review. The deeper specialization-level review applies only to case studies associated with Program Navigator applications. Additionally, AWS has streamlined the specialization application review process through Program

title: AWS IAM Identity Center simplifies identity source changes from Active Directory
summary: AWS IAM Identity Center now retains your workforce identities and their assignments when you change your identity source from Active Directory to an external identity provider (IdP), such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, or to the Identity Center directory. Specifically, it preserves your users, groups, group memberships, permission set assignments, and application assignments. Previously, this change required you to recreate them in IAM Identity Center. IAM Identity Center helps you connect your workforce identities to AWS once and manage their access centrally across AWS applications and accounts. When you change your identity source from Active Directory, your existing identity store remains in place, so your users and groups keep the same IDs. As a result, users retain their access to AWS accounts and applications, and policies that reference your user IDs, group IDs, or identity store ID continue to work. To make this change, configure your new identity source with the standard setu

title: Amazon CloudWatch Alarms now supports tags in alarm actions payload
summary: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces support for including alarm tags in action payloads and Amazon EventBridge events, enabling customers to route and filter alarm notifications by tag without additional lookups. When enabled on an alarm, CloudWatch adds the alarm tags to the messages it sends to Amazon SNS, AWS Lambda, and Amazon EventBridge each time the alarm changes state. This option is designed for customers who route many alarms through a shared notification pipeline and need to identify the owning team, environment, or service directly from the message. With tags in actions payloads, customers can avoid the extra work of correlating tag metadata with alarm events after the fact. For example, a team that routes hundreds of alarms through a single SNS topic to a Lambda function previously had to call ListTagsForResource for each event to find the owning team before paging. With this feature, the tags arrive in the notification, so the function can route directly from the message.

title: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails now supports Standard tier for contextual grounding checks
summary: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails now offers a Standard tier for contextual grounding checks, which detect and filter hallucinations by checking whether a model response is grounded in your reference source and relevant to the user's query. The Standard tier is more robust than the Classic tier. It supports responses that include reasoning or conversational content, scores differently worded responses with the same meaning more consistently, and provides more comprehensive language support, matching the Standard tier for content filters and denied topics. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides configurable safeguards for generative AI applications on any foundation model through the ApplyGuardrail API. Until now, contextual grounding checks applied strict grounding suited to summarization, paraphrasing, and question answering. summary: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) now supports AWS PrivateLink for ACME public certificate issuance, allowing you to request and renew public TLS certificates over a private network path that stays within the AWS network. You can now create a VPC interface endpoint to the ACM ACME service and route issuance traffic from any ACMEv2-compatible client through your VPC. If you're already using ACME with ACM, setup requires no changes to your ACME clients. After you create your managed ACME endpoint in ACM, you create a standard VPC interface endpoint using the VPC console, AWS CLI, or AWS CloudFormation. Private DNS resolves your existing ACME directory URL to the interface endpoint inside your VPC automatically, so the same client configuration and directory URL continue to work with no reconfiguration. Issuance operations—account creation, order creation, domain validation, finalization, and certificate retrieval—then flow over PrivateLink. All activity remains visible in the ACM console wit

title: Amazon Redshift adds support for creating and refreshing Apache Iceberg materialized views
summary: Amazon Redshift now supports the creation and refresh of Apache Iceberg materialized views. Materialized views pre-compute expensive joins and aggregations once and store the results in an Apache Iceberg table in Amazon S3 or Amazon S3 table buckets, registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Materialized views are created using familiar SQL — CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... USING ICEBERG and the results are instantly queryable by any Iceberg-compatible engine, including Amazon Athena, Apache Spark on Amazon EMR and AWS Glue, and third-party engines such as Trino, or Snowflake. Redshift keeps them current by recomputing only what has changed with manual incremental refresh, and because the results are Iceberg tables in the Glue Data Catalog, they are governed and discovered like any other catalog table. title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports network access controls for Identity Store
summary: AWS IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience for your workforce to AWS accounts and applications. IAM Identity Center now supports network access controls for Identity Store, which stores your users and groups. You can restrict access to the Identity Store API and the SCIM API based on the network that requests originate from. Your custom applications and user provisioning workflows use the Identity Store API to manage and look up users and groups, and your external identity provider uses the SCIM API to synchronize users and groups. For the Identity Store API, you can require that requests arrive only through allowed VPC endpoints in your account or organization, or from specific source VPCs. For both APIs, you can allow requests only from specific IP ranges. Within the same configuration, you can apply different restrictions to each API. title: CVE-2026-104019 - OS command injection in the Studio Space startup script in Amazon SageMaker Distribution
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-125-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 10/02/2026 13:00 PM PDT Description: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is an AWS service that unifies data, analytics, and AI development. It lets you find and access your organization's data and act on it with integrated, purpose-built tools. We identified CVE-2026-104019, an issue with the startup of SageMaker Spaces in SageMaker Unified Studio. The startup script in a SageMaker Space performs a network validation against all the available SageMaker connections in a project. Under certain conditions, improper sanitization of connection details during this validation could allow arbitrary code to be executed in the Space of another project member. title: CVE-2026-103505 - Mount Option Injection in Amazon EFS CSI Driver
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-120-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 10/01/2026 08:30 AM PDT Description: The Amazon EFS CSI Driver is a Container Storage Interface driver that allows Kubernetes clusters to use Amazon Elastic File System. We identified CVE-2026-103505, where an actor with PersistentVolume creation privileges can inject additional mount options through the mounttargetipmap volumeAttribute. Appending comma-separated values to a value inside that JSON map causes the mount utility to parse them as separate mount options. Impacted versions: >= v3.1.0 AND <= v3.4.2 Please refer to the article below for the most up-to-date and complete information related to this AWS Security Bulletin.

title: CVE-2026-104002: Fail-open error handling in the data masking utility in Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python)
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-123-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 10/01/2026 14:00 PM PDT Description: Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python) is a developer toolkit that implements serverless best practices and increases developer velocity. We identified CVE-2026-104002, a fail-open error handling issue within the data masking utility of Powertools for AWS Lambda (Python). This issue might allow actors to read sensitive field values that the application intended to mask. Impacted versions: >=3.6.0 AND <=3.34.0 Please refer to the article below for the most up-to-date and complete information related to this AWS Security Bulletin.

title: Announcing AWS Well-Architected Agent, an AI-powered intelligence to optimize your cloud environment (preview)
summary: Introducing the public preview of AWS Well-Architected Agent, an AI-powered service that analyzes your AWS environment to deliver targeted, contextual recommendations for improving your applications' cost, security, performance, and resilience—with ready-to-implement fixes aligned to your business goals.

title: Amazon S3 Tables now support all Apache Iceberg V3 data types
summary: Amazon S3 Tables now support all data types in the Apache Iceberg V3 spec, along with column default values, deletion vectors, and row lineage. Upgrade existing V2 tables or create new V3 tables with built-in compaction, maintenance, and engine compatibility.

title: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports metadata pre-filtering for higher recall on filtered searches
summary: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports metadata pre filtering, delivering up to 5x higher recall on filtered searches. Filters evaluate before similarity search so scoped queries return more relevant results. Ideal for RAG, agentic apps, and document search.

title: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL now supports direct querying of Apache Iceberg and Parquet data in your data lake
summary: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL now lets you directly query Apache Iceberg and Parquet data stored in your data lake alongside live operational data—no ETL pipelines required. Powered by DuckDB embedded within Aurora, this capability enables single queries that join transactional and historical data using familiar PostgreSQL syntax. It supports AWS Glue Data Catalog, S3, and S3 Tables, with optimizations like predicate pushdown and caching for efficient performance.

title: Introducing enhanced custom event buses in Amazon EventBridge for enterprise-scale event-driven applications
summary: Amazon EventBridge announces an enhanced custom event bus for organizations scaling event-driven applications across teams and accounts. Deploy a single event bus shared across all AWS accounts in your organization, with ordering guarantees, a simplified Subscriber resource, and improved economics at scale.

title: CVE-2026-95985 - Kiro IDE Allows Agentic Writes to Global Configurations While Working in Untrusted Workspaces
summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-117-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 09/24/2026 10:00 AM PDT Description: Kiro is an agentic IDE that users install on their desktop. We identified CVE-2026-95985. The file write tool in Kiro IDE before version 1.0.242 might allow remote unauthenticated actors to execute arbitrary commands and to inject crafted instructions into the agent's context. When a user runs the agent in a crafted repository as an untrusted workspace, sending any message can cause agent modifications to auto-loaded global configuration paths. Impacted versions: < 1.0.242 Please refer to the article below for the most up-to-date and complete information related to this AWS Security Bulletin. View article

title: Now on Amazon CloudWatch Omni: collaborative AI-powered observability for your applications
summary: Amazon CloudWatch Omni is the next evolution of CloudWatch — unified observability that brings your applications and AI agents into one reimagined experience, with auto-discovered topology, natural language queries, and AI-guided investigation powered by AWS DevOps Agent.

title: Introducing Amazon CloudWatch Omni: AI-powered observability for generative AI and agentic workloads
summary: Learn how Amazon CloudWatch Omni delivers AI-powered observability purpose-built for generative AI and agentic workloads. Trace, evaluate, and experiment with AI agents across any framework—directly from your IDE or a standalone web experience—using open standards and built-in evaluators for quality, correctness, and coherence.

title: New low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances are generally available
summary: AWS introduces new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors (Granite Rapids), available only on AWS. T8i instances are among the lowest-cost EC2 instances and deliver up to 30% better price performance over previous generation T3 instances.

title: AWS Elastic Beanstalk introduces Cluster Mode
summary: Run an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk Cluster Mode without provisioning or operating the compute underneath it. You provide a container image or source code; Elastic Beanstalk with service-operated compute creates and operates the environment that runs it.
